articles.title: Orange et les télécoms européens s'allient contre Starlink dans la course au satellite, la grande riposte
articles.text:
Quatre géants européens des télécoms, parmi lesquels Orange, envisagent de former un consortium pour candidater au spectre satellite européen. Ils se fixent l'objectif de concurrencer Starlink sur son propre terrain, celui de la connexion sans antenne relais.
Orange, Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone et Telefonica plancheraient en ce moment sur un projet commun visant à répondre ensemble à une prochaine mise aux enchères européenne sur le spectre satellite. Dans leur ligne de mire, une portion de fréquences que Bruxelles souhaite réserver à un acteur européen, dans le cadre d'une refonte des règles qui encadrent les communications directes vers les téléphones portables depuis l'espace. Rien n'est encore signé, mais la manœuvre en dit long sur l'ambition du Vieux Continent à réduire sa dépendance aux constellations américaines.
Un consortium européen des télécoms pour défier Starlink
Selon les informations de Bloomberg, les quatre opérateurs, dont le Français Orange, sont en train d'échanger autour d'une candidature conjointe pour capter une part des fréquences que l'Union européenne compte réserver à un opérateur local. Tous partagent l'objectif de renforcer la souveraineté satellitaire du continent, alors que les licences actuelles arrivent à échéance en 2027, donc demain. Les porte-parole des groupes concernés n'ont pas souhaité commenter ces discussions, encore informelles.
Il y a une condition de taille à considérer, posée par les autorités de la zone. Tout opérateur satellite candidat devra être détenu majoritairement par une entreprise européenne. La règle concerne directement ces quatre groupes, comptés parmi les plus grands opérateurs mobiles du continent. Reste que rien n'est acté pour l'instant : ni la formation officielle du consortium, ni même la décision de candidater n'ont été confirmées par les intéressés.
Ici, les échanges tournent autour du direct-to-mobile (ou direct-to-service), la technologie qui permet d'envoyer des textos, données et appels depuis l'orbite sans passer par une antenne relais, qui reste d'ailleurs aujourd'hui largement dominé par Starlink. La couverture terrestre européenne demeure pourtant excellente sur la majorité du territoire. La différence maintenant, c'est que Bruxelles veut se donner les moyens d'exister dans ce nouveau marché, à mesure que SpaceX développe son offre grand public sur le continent.
Bruxelles découpe le spectre, et SpaceX n'est pas d'accord
Dans le détail, le projet européen porte sur la bande des 2 GHz, une portion de fréquences radio clé pour les communications mobiles, dont l'attribution doit se jouer lors d'une prochaine mise aux enchères. Le gâteau serait divisé en trois, avec un tiers pour l'acteur européen visé par le consortium, un tiers pour IRIS², la constellation souveraine pilotée par SES (dont ArianeGroup parlait encore ce lundi), Eutelsat et Hispasat, et un dernier tiers ouvert aux acteurs internationaux. IRIS² ne devrait toutefois entrer en service qu'en 2029, d'abord tournée vers le haut débit, avec des capacités direct-to-mobile encore limitées, assurées par Hispasat.
Sans surprise, SpaceX s'oppose fermement à cette proposition qui limiterait l'accès des entreprises non-européennes au spectre. L'entreprise d'Elon Musk fournit déjà du haut débit satellite dans une large partie de l'Europe et collabore avec plusieurs opérateurs, dont Deutsche Telekom, sur le direct-to-mobile. Faute de droits de fréquences propres, elle ne peut toutefois pas proposer ce service seule sur le sol européen.
Il y a aussi le cas particulier de Vodafone, qui a mis sur pied une coentreprise à parts égales avec l'américain AST SpaceMobile, également positionné sur le direct-to-mobile. Pour espérer candidater sur le segment réservé aux Européens, l'opérateur britannique devrait revoir cette structure à 50/50. De quoi rappeler que, derrière les discussions feutrées, chaque acteur ajuste déjà ses pions sur l'échiquier satellitaire.

articles.title: Intel Set to Raise CPU Prices by Another 10% in October
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Intel Set to Raise CPU Prices by Another 10% in October
Intel is reportedly planning another 10% price increase on PC CPUs in October, according to DIGITIMES. This would be the latest in a string of price hikes made in stages over the past year. The report doesn't specify whether this price increase will affect only desktop CPUs or whether mobile CPUs will also be included. Industry sources cited by the outlet say the goal is to improve gross margin rather than growing market share. That would be especially important, since global PC shipments are expected to dip slightly from 260 million to about 250 million units in 2027, even as prices continue to climb. If Intel can push CPU shipments back up toward 200 million units, DIGITIMES estimates its market share could recover to roughly 78%.
The report also claims Intel is considering ending its low-margin Small Core product line entirely, which could open the door for Qualcomm and MediaTek to expand further into the industrial PC and IoT chip markets that Intel currently leads. On staffing, sources suggest another 5% to 10% of the workforce could be cut, following Intel's trim of its Data Center and AI group in July. Headcount reportedly sits around 75,000 now, though the same sources say Intel plans to keep hiring alongside any cuts, and that its current size is already reasonable.DIGITIMES also flagged a separate issue on the server side. Intel is said to be prioritizing its own fabs for server CPUs, which carry higher margins than chips outsourced to TSMC, but that's reportedly squeezing capacity for PC CPUs. Growing server output faster may mean sending more volume to TSMC, which puts extra eyes on how the 18A process is yielding and how 14A development is progressing.

articles.title: Belgian-Chinese semiconductor researcher arrested over alleged GaN trade-secret theft — prosecutors suspect BelGaN insiders transferred chip IP to China before the company collapsed
articles.text:
Belgian-Chinese semiconductor researcher arrested over alleged GaN trade-secret theft — prosecutors suspect BelGaN insiders transferred chip IP to China before the company collapsed
Linked Chinese company was established months after the suspect joined BelGaN
A 52-year-old Belgian-Chinese man has been arrested on suspicion of espionage for allegedly transferring specialized semiconductor intellectual property and trade secrets from Belgian chipmaker BelGaN, where he worked, to China. According to an AP News report citing details released by Belgium's federal prosecutor’s office on September 7, the Beijing-born Belgian resident was taken into custody on May 10 at a Brussels airport while attempting to board a flight to China.
The suspect — identified by Belgian media only as H.L. — previously held a senior research position at the now-defunct BelGaN, which specialized in gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductors. Investigators suspect he was concurrently leading a Chinese chip firm, GanKool, which was developing the exact same specialized gallium nitride chip technology as BelGaN. The company was established only a few months after H.L. joined BelGaN and was financed by a Chinese investment fund. The suspect now faces charges of industrial espionage, membership in a criminal organization, misuse of company assets, and unlawful disclosure of business secrets.
The espionage allegations emerged from an investigation into BelGaN's collapse. When the company collapsed into bankruptcy in the summer of 2024, Belgian authorities launched a routine financial probe into the failure. Investigators eventually uncovered highly unusual corporate activity. Instead of trying to keep BelGaN financially viable, the managers and the researcher may have actively tried to make the Belgian company “disappear” after transferring its proprietary knowledge. This led to further investigations that revealed GanKool’s existence and its connections to BelGaN.
In addition to the researcher’s role, the investigators also found evidence linking BelGaN's last CEO, a Chinese national, to the same Chinese rival. The prosecutors have said a second suspect remains at large, with Belgian media speculating that the CEO is the suspect.
The incident highlights the increasingly intense competition over technology and intellectual property in the semiconductor industry, particularly as China pushes to reduce its reliance on foreign chip technology while the U.S. continues to restrict its access to advanced processors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Just last month, South Korean court documents accused Chinese memory maker CXMT of using a detailed “Project Hefei” roadmap to obtain Samsung's proprietary DRAM technology, including a 620-step process recipe. A former Samsung engineer has already been sentenced to seven years in prison over the scheme.

articles.title: Razer Prio is great for portable gaming, cramped controls aside
articles.text:
Gaming accessory maker Razer has a number of excellent mobile controllers on the market now, but the company’s latest controller is all about portability. And while it truly shines in that respect, Razer made a few trade-offs to make it happen. But whether those matter for you ultimately comes down to how you like to game on the go, and what you like to play.
The new Razer Prio is the ultimate ultra-compact mobile controller. It folds up super small — about the length and width of a credit card, though much thicker — while still offering a full suite of controls. It’s got right and left thumbsticks, a D-pad, face and shoulder buttons, and other standards like menu and home buttons.
Smartly, Razer even made the buttons quiet. While you don’t get the oh-so-satisfying click sound out of the Prio, it also means it’s less noisy for people around you. That helps with the play-anywhere nature of the controller, since you won’t annoy people while you game.
It’s an all-around fantastic design for gaming on the go. The small size when folded up makes it super easy to slip in a backpack or purse, and the quiet buttons mean you can actually play anywhere. Plus, it works with most Androids and iPhones, as long as they’ve got a USB-C port and aren’t too long (it maxes out at 188mm). Razer also said it made the Prio compatible with most phone cases, but it won’t work with anything thicker than 15mm.
Moreover, phones are a surprisingly versatile gaming platform. Along with tons of mobile games out there, gamers can also access various titles from other platforms via various streaming tools, whether that’s streaming from a local PC or console, or cloud-based gaming through something like Xbox Game Pass.
And while I really like the Prio, unfortunately, that’s where my praise for the controller ends. See, the biggest issue I ran into with the Prio is that it’s just not very comfortable for gaming, though it varies depending on what you play.
For example, I tried playing the Android port of the excellent, Canadian-made Warframe, and while it was playable, I did not have a great time. If you’ve played Warframe at all, you know it’s a very fast-paced game with a lot of actions and inputs. I already find it tough to keep up on a normal controller, but the cramped controls on the Prio make it even worse.
Of course, that won’t be true for every game. Slower-paced titles, such as Darkest Dungeon, felt great on the Prio. I’d imagine most puzzle and platform games with controller support will also work pretty well. It’s mostly those fast-paced action titles, especially ones requiring lots of inputs, that will suffer on the Prio.
Ultimately, if comfort and ergonomics are a concern, Razer’s other controllers might be more appealing. The Kishi line, for example, offers a much more ergonomic feel that’s just like a typical console controller. They also cost a lot more.
Gameplay aside, I found the Prio setup to be quite finicky. Most phone controllers have a sliding back piece that extends to allow the controller to grip the phone.
The Prio ditches that for an elastic band which, functionally, gets the job done. However, it sacrifices some of the rigidity you’d get on other controllers.
The Prio also comes with a set of rubber inserts that adapt the controller’s fit to work with different phones and camera bump sizes. However, the included instruction book only mentioned which inserts were compatible with iPhones, so I had to trial-and-error it to figure out what was best for my Pixel. Notably, if you use a case, you can probably skip the rubber inserts entirely.
Finally, I have some concerns about wear and tear on the elastic band itself. Razer told me they did lots of durability testing to ensure it could handle tons of stretching and still return to its original shape. But even in my short time with it, there already seems to be some slight warping of the band.
All these pieces taken together certainly degrade the Prio experience, but I still think it does a great job with its core promise of portable gaming. There aren’t many phone controllers that can fold up as small as the Prio, making it the king of portability.
Unfortunately, how good the controller is will depend a lot on what you want to play. I struggled using the Prio in the games I like, but there are plenty of titles that I think would work a lot better for a controller like this. It’s worth keeping in mind when considering whether to buy the Prio.
The Razer Prio costs $139.99 in Canada and is available on Razer’s website.

articles.title: REGENT’s flying boat has finally carried people
articles.text:
An electric plane that transforms into a boat just flew its first human-crewed flight — Viceroy Seaglider has a 15,000lbs MTOW and will fly up to 180 miles
A flying boat has completed its first crewed flight
- REGENT Viceroy Seaglider has completed its first human-crewed flight above Narragansett Bay
- The electric craft flew 1,956 feet during its first crewed test
- Viceroy can shift between floating, hydrofoiling, and low-altitude flight modes
REGENT Craft has completed the first crewed flight of its Viceroy Seaglider, advancing development of an electric vessel designed for coastal transport.
The prototype carried two captains during a 30-second test above Narragansett Bay, reaching 33 ft while travelling 1,956 ft.
REGENT says the flight marks the largest human-carrying all-electric wing-in-ground-effect craft to complete such a test.
First crewed flight tests an unusual transport concept
Viceroy combines a boat-like hull, underwater foils, and wings, allowing it to shift between water travel and low-altitude flight.
At low speeds, the craft remains afloat before hydrofoils lift its hull and prepare it for flight above the surface.
During test flight, the vehicle remains close to the water, operating within one wingspan of the surface rather than climbing conventionally.
"Completing this flight test validates years of rigorous engineering and operational work and gives us the confidence to move into full-rate production,” said Mike Klinker, co-founder and CTO at REGENT.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“We showed today that flying a Seaglider is every bit as smooth and safe as we designed it to be.”
REGENT says the production model will carry 12 passengers and two crew, with a maximum takeoff weight of 15,000 lbs.
Its planned flight speed reaches 180 mph, while its stated range extends to 180 miles between coastal destinations.
The company says passengers will have large windows, substantial legroom, and lower cabin noise than conventional aircraft during travel.
The craft uses a three-layer digital control system intended to manage stability while allowing mariners to operate it like watercraft.
REGENT says certified mariners will captain the vessels, while United States Coast Guard rules will govern operations within American waters.
Commercial plans expand alongside defence work
These vessels are designed for coastal routes, where existing ports could support operations without conventional airport infrastructure.
About 40% of the global population lives in coastal communities, providing a large potential market for such services.
At the moment, the company has booked orders spanning six continents, while manufacturing capacity has been reserved across several future production years.
Earlier this year, REGENT announced an agreement involving The Twenty Five, which ordered as many as 60 Viceroy vessels.
The arrangement would make the operator REGENT's first United States delivery and launch partner for commercial Seaglider services.
Military versions for logistics, medical evacuation, surveillance missions, and other maritime applications requiring rapid movement are in development
The company holds a $15 million agreement with the United States Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory for related development work.
REGENT completed construction of a 255,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Rhode Island during June, with production activities beginning this year.
The facility is intended for structural assembly, wing and foil fitting, battery installation, systems work, and water-based testing.
“This is the moment we have been envisioning and tirelessly pursuing for the past five and a half years: REGENT has successfully proven safe, efficient ground-effect flight,” said Billy Thalheimer, co-founder and CEO at REGENT.

articles.title: La NASA prépare le X-59 à voler à vitesse supersonique sans bang
articles.text:
L’avion expérimental X-59 de la NASA a bouclé son 25e vol d’essai à Mach 1,2, avant d’entrer dans la phase qui doit confirmer qu’un vol plus rapide que le son peut ne produire, au sol, qu'un grondement discret plutôt qu'un bang.
Le X-59 est le démonstrateur du programme Quesst, piloté par la NASA. Avec sa silhouette allongée et son moteur placé au-dessus du fuselage, l’onde de choc du X-59 se disperse en plusieurs vagues plus discrètes, plutôt qu’un unique bang.
Les ingénieurs appellent ce phénomène un « sonic thump », littéralement un choc sourd, et la NASA espère, avec les données de ses essais, convaincre les régulateurs américains qu'un vol supersonique civil peut survoler des zones habitées sans gêner les riverains. Depuis son premier franchissement du mur du son, en juin, l’appareil enchaîne les vols de mise au point avant d’aborder l’étape la plus attendue du programme.
Le X-59 boucle son 25e vol avant la phase acoustique
Le 21 août dernier, le X-59 a décollé du centre de recherches en vol Armstrong, à Edwards, accompagné d’un avion de chasse pour la surveillance du vol. Le vol a duré 72 minutes, à Mach 1,2 et environ 49 000 pieds d’altitude, soit près de 15 kilomètres. Cathy Bahm, responsable du projet X-59 à la NASA a déclaré que « chaque vol nous rapproche de la transition vers la phase suivante ».
Plus tôt dans la campagne d’essais, le X-59 avait déjà volé à Mach 1,4 et 55 000 pieds. Ce sont la vitesse et l’altitude de croisière recherchées pour de futurs vols commerciaux. Le 5 juin, l’appareil avait franchi le mur du son pour la première fois, à Mach 1,1. Lors des vols précédents, l’équipe avait surtout vérifié la sécurité et la stabilité de l’appareil, avant d’aborder les performances de vitesse et d'’altitude.
Après ce vingt-cinquième vol, l'équipe du programme Quesst doit ouvrir, dans les mois à venir, la phase de validation acoustique. Des instruments installés au sol et à bord d’autres appareils mesureront la signature sonore du X-59 lors de ses passages supersoniques, avant des survols de communautés américaines sélectionnées destinés à recueillir leurs impressions sur le bruit perçu. Selon Larry Cliatt, responsable de cette validation, « c'est la phase que nous attendions ».
Washington prépare la fin de l’interdiction de 1973
Deux ans avant cette interdiction, en 1971, les États-Unis avaient abandonné leur projet d’avion supersonique civil, le Boeing 2707, un concurrent direct du Concorde. En interdisant, dès 1973, la quasi-totalité des vols supersoniques civils au-dessus du territoire américain, la FAA avait cantonné le Concorde à quelques liaisons transatlantiques, entre Paris ou Londres et New York. ON vous avait annoncé que depuis le 2 juillet, la FAA propose de remplacer cette interdiction par un critère acoustique, et un avion civil pourrait franchir Mach 1 au-dessus des terres à condition que l’intensité de son bang, une fois au sol, ne dépasse pas un seuil gênant.
Ce changement concerne l’Overture, développé par Boom Supersonic, et le X-59 de la NASA. Le premier doit voler à Mach 1,7, avec 64 à 80 passagers à bord, et ses livraisons sont espérées d’ici la fin de la décennie.
Boom Supersonic a d’ailleurs déjà fait franchir le mur du son à son démonstrateur XB-1, le 28 janvier 2025, à trois reprises et sans bang audible au sol. L’entreprise explique ce résultat par un phénomène de réfraction atmosphérique, le Mach cutoff. Au-delà d’une certaine altitude, l’onde de choc est inaudible au sol. Les ingénieurs de la NASA ont façonné le X-59 pour disperser le choc en plusieurs ondes plus discrètes. Le XB-1 de Boom Supersonic dépend plutôt de l’altitude de vol et des conditions atmosphériques du moment. Selon Blake Scholl, fondateur de Boom Supersonic, un tel vol peut être « abordable, durable et agréable, pour ceux qui sont à bord comme pour ceux qui sont au sol ».
Le régulateur américain n’a pourtant précisé aucun délai pour l’entrée en vigueur de cette nouvelle règle.

articles.title: Face aux cyberattaques, la France lance REACTIV, une unité d'intervention d'urgence
articles.text:
L’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (Anssi) vient d’annoncer sa riposte à la vague de cyberattaques qui frappe la France. Pour endiguer les « violations de données affectant les services de l’Etat », l’autorité nationale a décreté la mise en place du « Reponse & Action Interministérielle face aux Violations de données » (REACTIV). Ce « nouveau dispositif d’intervention d’urgence » doit permettre d’intervenir plus vite auprès des ministères visés par des cyberattaques et de mieux protéger les données des citoyens.
 ⬇️ Cyberattaques : l’ANSSI met en place une capacité renforcée de réaction dédiée aux services de l’État. pic.twitter.com/tOFekq2MIw
— ANSSI (@ANSSI_FR) September 7, 2026
Avec cette annonce, l’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information répond aux exigences formulées par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu le mois dernier. Suite au piratage des impôts, il avait demandé à l’ANSSI de constituer de toute urgence une « nouvelle unité cyber » capable d’apporter une réponse « plus réactive » aux attaques visant l’État.
À lire aussi : Arnaques aux impôts – de fausses lettres de la DGFiP inondent les boîtes aux lettres des Français
L’ANSSI muscle sa réponse aux cyberattaques
Concrètement, l’ANSSI va rediriger immédiatement ses équipes techniques vers les ministères touchés par une cyberattaque. L’agence veut ainsi réagir plus vite et limiter les dégâts, empêcher que les données volées continuent de se propager, et aider concrètement les administrations à sécuriser les comptes piratés. Les agents dépêchés par l’ANSSI doivent aussi permettre aux ministères de comprendre ce qui s’est passé, ce qui devrait éviter qu’un incident analogue ne se reproduise.
« Ce renforcement doit permettre de mieux circonscrire les attaques et de lutter plus réactivement contre les exfiltrations de données », explique l’ANSSI dans le communiqué.
Ce n’est pas tout. Le dispositif s’accompagne d’un renforcement de l’autorité de l’agence. Elle pourra désormais imposer aux ministères concernés des mesures immédiates destinées à protéger les données des citoyens. Cette mesure doit permettre d’accélérer la réaction des services publics en cas d’intrusion. L’ANSSI prévoit également de prendre en charge la communication de crise en cas de fuite. Comme on l’a vu lors du piratage du fisc, celle-ci manque parfois de clarté lorsqu’elle est diffusée par les ministères piratés. C’est désormais l’agence qui pilotera l’information diffusée lorsqu’un service de l’État est visé. Le changement doit éviter les messages contradictoires entre ministères et les informations erronées.
 🚨🔴 CYBERATTAQUES EN FRANCE – REACTIV, LE PLAN DU GOUVERNEMENT DÉVOILÉ
Pour lutter contre l’intensification, à la demande du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, l’ANSSI met en place le dispositif REACTIV !
REponse & ACTion Interministérielle face aux Violations de données.… pic.twitter.com/O2hbDPG2Ty
— SaxX ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ (@_SaxX_) September 7, 2026
REACTIV ne constitue pas une mesure isolée. Le dispositif s’inscrit en fait dans l’accélération de la feuille de route gouvernementale sur la sécurité numérique de l’État. L’objectif affiché à moyen terme est de « rehausser significativement et durablement » le niveau de sécurité des réseaux ministériels, et pas seulement de gérer les cyberattaques l’une après l’autre.
L’annonce a fait réagir de nombreux experts en cybersécurité. Le chercheur Clément Domingo se veut positif et espère que la contre-attaque signe « le début de la fin de cette hécatombe numérique ». Cette riposte d’urgence survient alors que la France continue de subir des violations de données à répétition. Récemment, c’est l’Association des maires de France et des présidents d’intercommunalité (AMF) et le ministère de la Transition écologique qui se sont retrouvés dans le viseur des cybercriminels. Selon l’ANSSI, le pays figure parmi les cibles privilégiées des cybercriminels.

articles.title: From home to panchayat: Bihar’s Seema Kumari and her journey of women’s empowerment
articles.text:
From home to panchayat: Bihar’s Seema Kumari and her journey of women’s empowerment
After her first election loss, Bihar’s Seema Kumari won and began working on education, roads, women’s empowerment and water conservation.
In Dhanuki Panchayat of Sarmera block in Bihar’s Nalanda district, Seema Kumari is popularly known as the ‘Nimki Mukhiya’. Today, she is recognised as a responsible and active woman leader. Whenever she visits different government offices for panchayat-related work, people recognise her and know her by name.
But reaching this position was not easy.
Seema Kumari spent a significant part of her life managing household responsibilities. She was interested in education and had a desire to understand society, but after marriage, her life became largely confined to her home.
Whenever she visited her village to cast her vote, she interacted with local residents and noticed a significant gap between her educational background and the condition of the village. This led her to question whether her education could be used to contribute to society.
That question eventually pushed her towards politics and grassroots leadership. She contested an election for the first time but lost. Instead of considering the defeat the end of her journey, she tried again. In her second attempt, she won and began working on the development of her panchayat.
Education shaped her thinking, father inspired her
Seema Kumari was born into a middle-class family. Her father placed great importance on education and believed that everyone should have an equal opportunity to study and progress in life.
From childhood, Seema closely observed her father’s social work and often participated in it.
After completing school, she went to college and earned her graduation degree. She still wanted to continue her education, but considering the responsibilities of the family, she eventually got married.
Even after her marriage, her father continued encouraging her to pursue her studies.
Seema recalls, “My father always told me that education is very important. He explained to me that education is not only for oneself but can also be used to serve society.”
After marriage, much of her life revolved around household responsibilities. At times, she wondered why, despite completing her graduation, her role had become limited to managing her home.
The question of whether she could contribute to society gradually became stronger in her mind.
Village problems gave her a reason to enter politics
While living in the city, Seema would return to her village whenever elections were held. These visits gave her an opportunity to interact with villagers. She would walk through the village, speak to residents and listen to their concerns.
She realised that the village faced challenges beyond poverty, including gaps in education, healthcare and basic infrastructure. Many residents were unaware of government schemes, while others did not know how to access the benefits available to them.
She began to see a clear contrast between her education and the problems faced by people in her village. She felt that having an education also came with a responsibility to use it for the benefit of others.
During her conversations with villagers, some residents suggested that she contest the panchayat election.
She says, “People told me, ‘Why don’t you contest the election? You are educated. If you become the Mukhiya, our village will benefit.’ That day, I also felt that perhaps this was what I should do.”
She decided to enter the election.
Her first attempt ended in defeat. However, she did not give up. She continued meeting people, understood where she had fallen short and prepared herself for another opportunity. When she contested the election again, she won and began focusing on development work in the panchayat.
A symbol of women’s empowerment
After becoming Mukhiya, Seema began directly interacting with residents to understand the problems facing the panchayat. She believed that the first step towards successfully implementing any development plan was understanding the actual needs of the people.
She worked to create awareness about government schemes and helped residents understand the schemes and facilities available to them.
Under her leadership, repair work was carried out at a school, a new Anganwadi centre was constructed, and efforts were made to improve roads and build permanent drainage systems.
However, for Seema, development was not limited to roads and drains. She also wanted women in the panchayat to become financially independent and stand on their own feet.
With the support of a local NGO, training camps in stitching and embroidery were organised for women and girls who had limited or no formal education.
The objective was to help women develop skills that could provide them with opportunities to earn rather than remain financially dependent on others. They were also given information about different employment opportunities.
Seema says, “I wanted the women in our village to not remain confined to their homes. I wanted them to learn a skill and become self-reliant. That is why we started stitching and embroidery training.”
Water conservation through jal chaupals and street plays
Water conservation has also been one of Seema’s priorities in Dhanuki Panchayat. She believes that water scarcity could become one of the biggest challenges for rural communities in the coming years.
To create awareness about the importance of water, jal chaupals were organised in the village. During these gatherings, residents discussed water availability, responsible usage and ways to conserve water for the future.
Soak pits were constructed in public areas to support better water management. Street plays were also organised to spread awareness about responsible water use. Members of a local NGO and the health department participated in these initiatives.
According to Seema, the Gram Sabha plays an important role in identifying village problems and finding solutions. She also worked towards making panchayat meetings more regular.
She participated in training programmes organised at the district level as well. To take forward work related to the Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP), a team was formed and emphasis was placed on holding monthly meetings.
Seema says, “If we save water today, we can secure a safer future for the coming generations. We started initiatives such as jal chaupals and street plays to explain this message to people in a simple way.”
Recognition received, but the journey continues
Seema Kumari’s work has received recognition at both the state and national levels. For her efforts towards empowering women, she has received a state-level Nari Sashaktikaran Samman award. Her work in the field of water conservation has also received appreciation and recognition at the national level.
Despite these honours, Seema remains focused on the challenges that lie ahead. She wants to further improve education, healthcare and nutrition for girls in the panchayat.
She believes that the development of a village can only be considered complete when its daughters have equal opportunities to learn, grow and move forward.
A journey that began with household responsibilities has now taken Seema to the leadership of her panchayat. From losing her first election to winning the second and then working on grassroots development, her story shows that leadership does not come simply with holding a position.
It requires listening to people and standing with them through their problems.
For Seema, the position of Mukhiya is a responsibility rather than an achievement in itself. Her larger goal is to ensure that residents of the panchayat have access to facilities and opportunities that are often associated with urban areas.
Seema says, “I have realised that a woman can lead just as strongly as anyone else. My goal is to ensure that every family in the panchayat benefits from government schemes and facilities. In the coming years, I especially want to work towards improving education, healthcare and nutrition for girls.”
Her story is also the story of a village where change begins with small steps. One woman first understood her own circumstances, then recognised the needs of her community and eventually accepted the responsibility of leadership.
Today, her focus remains on making Dhanuki Panchayat better than it was before.

 Points forts
- Poids plume, malgré un grand format.
- Écran lumineux.
- Module photo de 200 Mpx performant.
Points faibles
- Tendance à la chauffe.
- Charge à 25 W seulement.
- Pas de téléobjectif.
Le design doit servir l'usage. Qu'en est-il du Galaxy S25 Edge de Samsung ? Sa finesse record, mais avant tout son poids plume rendent son utilisation quotidienne pratique. Ce terminal mobile combine la légèreté d'un petit smartphone et la diagonale d'écran confortable de ceux que l'on appelait jadis les “phablettes”. Est-ce vraiment ce que vous recherchez en tant qu'utilisateur ? La réponse vous appartient, mais il vous faudra tout de même être convaincu pour investir dans ce smartphone, certes plus mince qu'un Galaxy S25+, mais moins endurant et polyvalent en termes de capture photo, malgré un tarif de lancement supérieur. Enfin, au-delà du positionnement tarifaire de ce mobile, Samsung parvient à éviter le double écueil des performances en berne et de l'autonomie famélique, ce que nous craignions au vu des caractéristiques matérielles de son S25 Edge. C'est sans doute ce qui mérite d'être retenu et peut ouvrir la voie à d'autres itérations.

articles.title: Scientists say ‘ultrafast magnetic-field pulses’ could help AI data centers cut their energy usage by 100x — and bring sizable improvements to RAM and data storage
articles.text:
Scientists develop ‘ultrafast magnetic-field pulses’ memory system that could cut AI data center energy use by 100x — and even get close to hitting thermodynamic limits
A greener way to power AI?
- AI data centers currently use a huge amount of energy
- Scientists have found a way to cut that energy bill by "orders of magnitude"
- It involves using "ultrafast magnetic-field pulses" in RAM and storage
It’s no secret that the current artificial intelligence (AI) boom is leading to record levels of energy consumption — all that computing power needs to be fueled somehow — and it’s causing much controversy among the communities that are impacted whenever a new data center lays down its roots in their neighborhoods.
Now, though, scientists think they’ve come across a way that could radically slash the energy requirements of memory and storage, with potentially massive consequences for the future of the computing and AI industries.
In a paper published in the Advanced Materials journal (via a press release in Science Daily), researchers at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland wrote that the breakthrough would fundamentally affect the way magnetic memory operates. Right now, switching its state allows magnetic memory to control digital information, but the current methods of doing so can be costly in terms of energy.
Instead of using standard energy switching techniques, the researchers discovered an alternative that harnessed ultrafast magnetic field pulses that consumed far less energy. In fact, the paper claimed that the authors’ approach could cut energy usage by “up to two orders of magnitude” — in other words, a cut of around 100x, which is a significant reduction.
The data centers of the future
The AI revolution is only a few years old, but data center energy consumption has already become a significant issue. As the authors of the research paper put it, “Without significant improvements in efficiency, [information and communication technologies] could eventually represent a sizable share of worldwide electricity consumption and carbon emissions.” AI is playing a large role in that trend thanks to both its voracious appetite for component production and the sizable emissions it produces.
While the paper focused on magnetic memory, its theories could be applied to other fields, the authors believe. As study writer Dr. Elton J.G. Santos put it, “The same framework can be adapted to electrical currents and even ultrafast laser pulses, which are among the most cutting-edge technologies for future data storage. That means the ideas developed here could have applications far beyond the systems we studied.”
Although the research is still in the realm of theory, the paper’s authors proposed a number of practical steps that could help others build prototypes and conduct experiments.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That said, don’t expect monumental changes any time soon. There is still a long road ahead before these ideas get put into practice, if they ever do. But given the promising results of the scientists’ work, there is hope that the data centers of the future could be far less energy-intensive than those of today.

articles.title: Por qué el juego Buscaminas desapareció de Windows y cómo tenerlo gratis en el PC
articles.text:
Buscaminas ya no es una aplicación que está preinstalada en Windows, como muchos lo vivieron en los 2000. Aunque su legado sigue vivo con versiones para jugar en PC gratis, incluso sin descargar ningún programa.
Este juego no nació como entretenimiento, aunque se convirtió en una adicción para Bill Gates. Sus creadores lo diseñaron para enseñar a manejar un componente que a fines de los años 80 todavía resultaba poco común entre los usuarios domésticos: el clic del mouse.
PUBLICIDAD
La historia de la creación de Buscaminas en Windows
La primera versión del Buscaminas se desarrolló en 1989. Sus autores fueron Robert Donner y Curt Johnson, ambos empleados de Microsoft en ese momento.
Johnson diseñó la lógica del juego, mientras que Donner se encargó de adaptarla para que funcionara dentro de Windows. El objetivo no era divertir, sino familiarizar a la gente con el clic del mouse.
PUBLICIDAD
El título se popularizó recién en 1992, cuando Microsoft lo incluyó en Windows 3.1. La compañía buscaba que los usuarios practicaran el clic izquierdo y el derecho con mayor precisión, además de acostumbrarlos a las interfaces gráficas que empezaban a expandirse en esa época.
Cómo pasó de la fama mundial a la salida de Windows
Con Windows 95 llegó una interfaz más moderna, y Windows XP sumó los niveles de principiante, intermedio y experto, además de los récords de tiempo que motivaban a seguir jugando. Alrededor del juego se formaron comunidades enteras dedicadas a batir marcas y crear rankings mundiales.
PUBLICIDAD
La variedad de juegos clásicos alcanzó su punto más alto con Windows Vista y Windows 7, cuando Microsoft renovó el Buscaminas y sumó títulos como Chess Titans, Mahjong Titans y Purble Place. La compañía presentó esa colección en la feria CES de 2007.
El quiebre llegó con Windows 8, lanzado en 2012. Microsoft eliminó las versiones tradicionales integradas en el sistema y las reemplazó por aplicaciones descargables desde la Windows Store, entre ellas Microsoft Minesweeper. Una respuesta publicada por la comunidad oficial de soporte de Microsoft durante esa etapa confirmó que los juegos preinstalados de versiones anteriores ya no estaban disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
El Buscaminas desapareció como aplicación integrada en Windows 8 porque Microsoft decidió reemplazar las versiones tradicionales del sistema operativo por aplicaciones descargables desde la tienda oficial. Desde entonces, jugarlo requiere instalarlo por separado, algo que no ocurría en las versiones anteriores del sistema.
Otros títulos de la colección corrieron distinta suerte. Corazones, Chess Titans, InkBall y Purble Place no tuvieron sucesores oficiales, mientras que el 3D Pinball: Space Cadet quedó atrapado entre un error de programación y una licencia que impedía distribuirlo por separado.
PUBLICIDAD
Bill Gates se convirtió en un fanático del juego
El fundador de Microsoft tampoco fue inmune a los encantos del Buscaminas. Libby Duzan, entonces responsable de productos de entretenimiento de la empresa, contó a The Washington Post en 1994 que Gates tuvo que desinstalar el juego de su computadora.
Eso no le impidió seguir jugando. De vez en cuando recurría al ordenador de Mike Hallman, presidente de Microsoft en ese momento, y llegó a ganar una partida en apenas cinco segundos.
PUBLICIDAD
La marca fue tan alta que Tom Reeves, director de desarrollo de Microsoft, decidió superarla por otros medios: escribió un macro capaz de resolver el juego en tres segundos, un tiempo imposible para una persona.
Cuando Gates descubrió la trampa, envió un correo electrónico indignado: “Mis habilidades críticas están siendo reemplazadas por un ordenador. Esto de la tecnología está yendo demasiado lejos. ¿Cómo se puede conservar la dignidad humana cuando los ordenadores hacen las cosas importantes mejor que las personas?”.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo jugar Buscaminas hoy en el PC
Pese a su salida del sistema operativo, el juego sigue disponible de varias formas y de manera gratuita. La opción más directa es buscar la palabra “Buscaminas” en Google: el primer resultado no es un enlace, sino un módulo interactivo con un botón “Jugar” que funciona igual en PC y en móvil, incluso sin conexión a internet.
Otra alternativa es la web Minesweeper.online, que mantiene la estética clásica de Windows con estadísticas, modo nocturno y miles de tableros distintos.
Para quienes prefieren una instalación oficial, Microsoft ofrece Microsoft Minesweeper a través de su tienda, con el modo clásico, distintos niveles de dificultad, desafíos diarios y un modo aventura con gráficos actualizados.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Un barco oceanográfico pesca por accidente 26 ánforas romanas en un yacimiento oculto en Formentera
articles.text:
No solo ha sido el gobierno más extenso de nuestro pasado: los restos del Imperio Romano no dejan de ofrecer respuestas y plantear nuevas preguntas. Esta vez empezaron a tirar y a subir, y las piezas aparecieron enganchadas en las redes. Por la forma y masa, un pez no era, desde luego. La red del buque Miguel Oliver subió el pasado 5 de septiembre 26 ánforas romanas casi intactas y 17 cajas de cerámica fragmentada.
El equipo del Museo Arqueológico de Eivissa y Formentera (MAEF), por su parte, se encargó de la recepción y traslado al almacén. El lance ocurrió al sur de Formentera, a 1.400 metros de profundidad. Nadie las buscaba, porque el barco hacía ciencia pesquera, no arqueología. El hallazgo llegó al Museo Arqueológico de Ibiza y Formentera en menos de 24 horas.
Una red que perseguía merluzas. El Miguel Oliver participaba en MEDITS, el programa que audita cada año la salud de los caladeros mediterráneos. Empezó en 1994 con cuatro países: Francia, España, Italia y Grecia. Hoy suma once. Baleares entró en el 2001. Las Pitiusas, la zona más joven del programa, se incorporaron recién en 2021. Rastrean merluza, gamba roja, cigala, pulpo. Ese día, entre las mallas, apareció también el Imperio Romano.
Ánforas Dressel 20. Las piezas pertenecen al tipo Dressel 20, el envase estrella del aceite bético entre los siglos I y III. El bidón estándar, por así decirlo. Se fabricaban junto al Guadalquivir, entre Hispalis (Sevilla) y Corduba (Córdoba), y cargaban entre 40 y 80 litros de aceite. Su arcilla porosa las volvía inservibles tras un solo viaje: se llenaban, viajaban y se tiraban.
Muchas de las recuperadas en Formentera conservan sellos y tituli picti, inscripciones pintadas con el peso, el origen y el nombre del comerciante. Es la etiqueta nutricional de la Antigüedad, y la pista que permite rastrear rutas comerciales enteras. Sellos idénticos aparecen en yacimientos de Londres y de Maguncia, en la actual Alemania: el aceite bético llegaba hasta las fronteras más lejanas del Imperio.
Una montaña. Ese modelo de usar y tirar dejó una huella brutal en Roma. El Monte Testaccio, una colina artificial de 35 metros junto al Tíber, está hecha casi por completo de fragmentos de Dressel 20: unos 53 millones de ánforas, acumuladas durante un siglo. Formentera aporta ahora 26 piezas más al mismo rompecabezas logístico: cómo movía Roma millones de litros de aceite por mar sin naves cisterna.
El nombre. El Miguel Oliver no es un pesquero cualquiera. Mide 70 metros de eslora, costó 24 millones de euros y se botó en Vigo en 2007. Lleva el nombre de Miguel Oliver (Barcelona, 1918 - Mallorca, 2004), biólogo marino y secretario general de Pesca Marítima entre 1982 y 1986. Va equipado con seis laboratorios, tres ecosondas y tres radares, y está certificado como buque silencioso: emite tan poco ruido que ni siquiera espanta a las especies que estudia. El pasado 5, además de merluza, encontró veinte siglos de comercio.
1.400 metros. Ningún buzo llega ahí. La inmersión recreativa se detiene sobre los 40 metros, si bien hay retos de cinco atmósferas; la técnica, con mezclas de gases, roza los 300. A 1.400 metros solo llegan redes de arrastre, robots submarinos o sumergibles tripulados, un lujo reservado a expediciones oceanográficas de gran presupuesto. Por eso la arqueología subacuática mediterránea trabaja casi siempre en aguas someras, donde caben buzos. Un pecio a esa profundidad es prácticamente inexcavable: solo un arrastre casual, como este, lo reflota.
Manguera, desalación y agilidad. El material subacuático se deteriora rápido fuera del agua: la sal cristaliza y desintegra la cerámica. La tripulación mantuvo las ánforas hidratadas con una manguera durante todo el trayecto. En tierra, el Servicio de Patrimonio Subacuático autorizó el traslado según la Ley de Patrimonio Histórico Español, que obliga a depositar cualquier resto extraído en el museo más cercano. Ahora empieza la desalación pieza por pieza, en tanques de agua, antes de la restauración definitiva.
Sustos y alegrías. En 2020, un arrastrero de Formentera sacó cuatro ánforas romanas casi intactas a solo 110 metros de profundidad. Y desde 2009, el Consell protege como Bien de Interés Cultural un pecio romano del siglo IV hundido a 75 metros, entre Punta Pedrera y Cap des Falcó, con un derrame de ánforas repartido en 12 por 11 metros de fondo. Las aguas pitiusas guardan, al parecer, un Mediterráneo entero de comercio romano.
Lo que viene ahora. Los sellos de las ánforas de Formentera todavía no revelan fecha ni origen exacto del cargamento. El estudio epigráfico cerrará ese hueco, pieza a pieza. Con suerte, apuntará también hacia el naufragio del que probablemente cayeron. O, como mínimo, dar un marco temporal a este alijo.

articles.title: Rockstar May Move GTA 6 PC Launch in Response to Expected Console Shortages
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Rockstar May Move GTA 6 PC Launch in Response to Expected Console Shortages
It has long been thought that there would be a long delay between the console and PC launches of Grand Theft Auto VI—GTA V launched to consoles a whole two years ahead of the PC port—however, the unprecedented times facing the PC and console hardware markets may be enough to pressure Rockstar into moving the PC launch of GTA VI ahead, according to recent rumors.
In a recent appearance on the VGC Podcast, Andy Robinson mentioned during a discussion about the ongoing gaming hardware situation that he thinks "they'll push the PC version up," referring to GTA VI. He went on to say that "There's a bit of noise about that. That perhaps the PC version might arrive sooner than some people might expect, just because of everything that's going on," suggesting high demand—some of which is induced by GTA VI itself—may drive Rockstar Games to release the PC port sooner.Even discounting the alleged insider chatter Robinson cited, there's some reason to the assumption that GTA VI might be handled differently, and the ongoing DRAM crisis is only part of the explanation. In addition to data center-induced demand, the upcoming launch of GTA VI has seemingly prompted sky-high console prices after retail stock of the PlayStation 5 Pro disappeared overnight, and a restocking was accompanied by a $400+ price jump.
Analysts and retailers have also predicted that console stock would run dry when GTA VI finally launches in November. With evidence to back up these claims, it stands to reason that Rockstar might release GTA VI on PC in order to sell more units early in the game's lifecycle.

articles.title: Edifier ES850NB headphones review: great value option
articles.text:
After my review of their V80 headphones, Edifier was kind enough to send me a pair of their ES850NB headphones to try out. Because I love the V80s, I was excited to give these new and improved headphones a test run. I’ve been using them pretty regularly for several months, and I have quite a few thoughts.
I mentioned in my review of the V80s that my budget is limited, so price is often one of the first things I check for, whether I’ve paid for a product or received it as a gift. The Edifier ES850NB headphones are available on Edifier’s website for $199.99. At the time of writing, they’re on sale for $129.99 on Amazon Canada.
That’s a pretty substantial price jump from the affordable V80 headphones, which are regularly $69.99, and currently on sale for $39.99 on Edifier’s website and on Amazon Canada. In theory, that should mean that the difference in quality is also substantial, if the pricing is to be considered fair. However, I’m not sure that’s quite the case for the ES850NB headphones.
Don’t get me wrong: they’re excellent, and improvements were definitely made. Out of the box, the audio quality is noticeably stronger than the V80 headphones. Where the V80s required a little bit of EQ to get them sounding full and smooth, the ES850NBs can get away with the default audio settings in the EdifierConneX companion app. If you’re picky, you may find the bottom end just slightly lacking, but it wasn’t enough to bother me. I think the average listener would be more than satisfied with the overall sound.
The ES850NB’s Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) has not improved much from that of the V80 headphones. The product details of the ES850NB headphones cite -45dB noise cancellation, where the V80 headphones do -44dB. A difference of one decibel isn’t really detectable to the human ear, but I think Edifier’s use of Passive Noise Cancelling (PNC) makes a huge difference.
While ANC uses tiny microphones in a process called “phase cancellation” to monitor external noise and generate inverted sound waves to cancel out the noise, PNC refers to the use of physical design to minimize external noise interruption. The shape of headphone cups, the density of ear cushions, and the angle at which they sit over the ear are all a part of Passive Noise Cancellation.
With any headphones or earbuds, I like to test noise cancelling in a noisy, crowded environment. The V80 headphones did an impressive job with external noise suppression. It was easy to drown out the chaos and lock in, even at my favourite coffee shop during the lunch rush.
Even though the ANC on the ES850NBs is only one decibel greater than the V80s, it felt a lot stronger because they have better PNC. In addition to the external noise suppression being improved, it also effectively eliminated the sound leakage I noticed with the V80s.
I won’t pretend to know exactly how the ES850NBs reduced sound leakage – physics as a whole is mostly a mystery to me – but the headphones leak a lot less sound than the V80s. I was able to turn the volume up to almost 90% before my partner could hear what I was listening to.
This is great news if you like to listen on the louder side, but you should always be mindful of how loud and how long you listen, unless you’re cool with damaging your hearing.
The physical design of the ES850NB headphones is quite different from the V80s. The ear cups are slightly less oblong. They have gently rounded corners, creating a shape closer to a “squoval”. The cups protrude more abruptly and have much sharper edges than the round design of the V80 headphones. I don’t notice much of a difference in the density of the ear cushions or headband, but the shape of the ear cushions also leans a bit more square than oval.
Aesthetically, the ES850NB headphones are gorgeous. I have them in brown, which feels very luxurious, especially with the faux leather face on the outside of the cups. I was secretly hoping for pink, but even the brown could pass for a deep mauve. They go with everything, and they’re extremely comfortable. They are a bit warm, but I think that’s the case for just about all over-the-ear headphones.
The ES850NB headphones come with a pretty nice travel case, which is handy for keeping your headphones in great condition. I’m never a fan of tossing any device into a bag without some kind of protection, so I appreciate this addition.
The button setup is the same as on the V80 headphones, and the buttons are also customizable through the EdifierConneX app. The ES850NB headphones have a similar Bluetooth range of about 30 feet, and they also sport the same 40mm driver as the V80 headphones. The two also share the same listening modes: High Noise Cancellation, Medium Noise Cancellation, Ambient Sound, and Wind Reduction.
Edifier has added support for the LDAC codec to the ES850NB headphones, which basically allows more audio information to pass through the wireless Bluetooth connection, resulting in higher-resolution audio for the listener. It’s worth noting that device compatibility with the LDAC codec is still pretty limited. Most mid-range and flagship Android phones from 2024 and newer support LDAC, but it still varies by brand and model. Currently, there are no iPhone models with LDAC support.
The ES850NB headphones have gained an interesting new feature called Touch-to-Chat. When using ANC, you can touch and hold the right ear cup to pause playback and switch to ambient sound mode, then release to resume playback. The idea is that if someone is trying to speak to you while you’re listening to something, this will be a seamless way to have a quick chat, then go back to listening.
I really like this idea, but you have to hold for about two seconds before playback pauses. That two-second delay is just a little too long for it to be considered seamless. I find it easier to just move the cup off my ear and then hit the pause button. Touch-to-Chat is a great idea, and that delay is the only drawback for me.
Other than physical design, the biggest difference between the V80 and ES850NB headphones is the battery capacity. The ES850NBs offer a massive 53 listening hours with ANC, and 92 hours without. This is a huge jump from the V80s’ respective 26 hours with ANC and 45 hours without. You still can’t charge while listening, but the Fast Charging makes up for that fact. 15 minutes of charging will get you 11.5 hours of playback without ANC on the ES850NB headphones, versus the V80’s 8 hours.
So after all this, the question remains: “Do the ES850NB headphones live up to their elevated price point?” My answer is ultimately… kind of. Yes, they are awesome headphones. Yes, I thoroughly enjoy using them. However, I don’t feel compelled to spend $129.99 on them when the V80 headphones can do an excellent job for much less.
I think if you’re in a tax bracket where $129.99 isn’t that expensive to you, you really don’t want to bother with equalizing your headphones at all, and sound leakage will be a big problem for you, then the ES850NB headphones are a great option; perhaps even the perfect option. After all, as far as high-quality headphones go, $129.99 is still quite inexpensive.
Otherwise, I would probably advise sticking with the V80 headphones. Edifier may have shot themselves in the foot by making their budget headphones too good. In this economy, I actually think that’s something to be proud of. I’m always in favour of whatever is most accessible to the average person. A company with high-quality products at reasonable prices is a company I feel like I can trust, which is why Edifier will still be one of the first brands I look to for headphones.

articles.title: Intel surpasses one million High-NA EUV wafers processed, outpaces the rest of the industry combined — company also trailblazing giant 6×12 photomasks to speed production and lower costs
articles.text:
Intel surpasses one million High-NA EUV wafers processed, outpaces the rest of the industry combined — company also trailblazing giant 6×12 photomasks to speed production and lower costs
Stitching to be used in the near term future with High-NA tools, but larger 6×12 photomasks envisioned.
Intel announced on Monday that it had processed more than one million 300-mm wafers using its High-NA EUV scanners, less than two and a half years after its first tool was assembled. For now, the company intends to use industry-standard 6-inch photomasks, which can expose 26×16.5 mm half-fields and therefore require field stitching for larger chips. However, Intel is also working on larger 6×12-inch photomasks that would enable High-NA EUV scanners to expose full 26×33 mm fields without stitching.
One million High-NA wafers
Intel's one million wafers figure includes wafers processed during tool installation and certification, R&D, and production. Earlier this year, Intel certified using High-NA EUV scanners for its 18A process technology, so right now these tools are used to make some of Intel's Panther Lake processors. Intel currently has two ASML Twinscan EXE:5000 tools and at least one EXE:5200B scanner. As of late February 2025, Intel processes around 30,000 wafers using its High-NA EUV tool, so going from 30,000 wafers by February 2025 to over a million by September 2026 is an enormous increase in cumulative High-NA utilization.
Since Intel's fleet expanded from two EXE:5000 systems to three and now includes the much faster EXE:5200B, the million-wafer milestone is really a fleet and process-maturity milestone that Intel has achieved first in the industry. What makes the company's milestone even more important is that ASML announced this April that all of the High-NA EUV scanners shipped by then processed over 500,000 wafers which achieving over 80% availability, which means that Intel has now processed more wafers using High-NA tools than the rest of the industry combined.
Sticking to stitching
Conventional 0.33-NA EUV has 4X magnification in both directions, enabling the familiar 26×33 mm exposure field with traditional 6-inch photomasks. However, 0.55-NA EUV uses anamorphic 4X/8X magnification, so the same 6×6 mask can provide only approximately 26×16.5 mm on the wafer. As a result, large dies that fit within a conventional 26 × 33 mm EUV field must be exposed as two half-fields using High-NA EUV, which is called stitching. While stitching is a workable near-term solution, it has several drawbacks.
Firstly, it greatly reduces throughput from 175 wafers per hour to 125 wafers per hour on an EXE:5200B. Secondly, chip designs must account for stitching and must be developed with stitching in mind, which means less floor planning freedom. Thirdly, the two exposures must be aligned extremely precisely so that features crossing the stitching boundary connect properly. Even a tiny misalignment can distort lines and vias, or break interconnects, which potentially creates defects and reduces yields, which will be a particularly costly problem for large CPU and GPU dies.
6×12 mask effort progressing
To avoid using stitching, the industry — led by Intel — plans to shift to larger 6×12 masks, which will enable a 26×33 mm full field in one exposure. While this looks easy on paper, make the mask twice as long, changing the mask represents an enormous ecosystem change.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Moving from 6×6-inch to 6×12-inch photomasks would require substantial changes across the existing mask ecosystem, including mask blanks and deposition, etching, inspection and metrology, cleaning, pellicles, mask writers, and mask handling systems. Crucially, High-NA EUV scanners would also have to be modified or redesigned to accommodate the larger masks, which will make the transition a major retooling effort across the semiconductor supply chain. While neither ASML nor Intel confirmed that existing or planned High-NA EUV scanners can be modified to handle larger masks, all of the future High-NA EUV scanners to be launched before and after 2033 are designed around 6×6-inch reticles and stitching, according to ASML's roadmap.
It remains to be seen whether the industry moves on to larger 6×12-inch photomasks, but Intel appears to be the main evangelist for changing the mask standard that has defined projection lithography infrastructure for decades. If the effort comes to fruition, then Intel will likely have a considerable first-mover advantage over its industry peers because it will define and set the standard for the projection lithography industry for decades to come, an advantage that is hard to overestimate.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Karnataka invites global tech firms, startups to partner in building 'Quantum City'
articles.text:
Karnataka invites global tech firms, startups to partner in building 'Quantum City'
Karnataka would build on its existing strengths in IT and aerospace while expanding into emerging areas such as quantum technologies, SpaceTech, DroneTech, artificial intelligence and geospatial technologies.
The Karnataka government has invited global technology companies, startups, investors, and researchers to partner with it in developing the proposed 'Quantum City' as a globally competitive hub for research, innovation and industry collaboration.
Addressing a high-level roundtable on Space, Mobility and Drones here, Minor Irrigation and Science & Technology Minister Ajay Dharam Singh said the state wants industry and innovators to engage from the early stages and contribute ideas, technologies and partnerships to shape its deep-tech ecosystem.
"Quantum City is an ambitious initiative that we want to build in partnership with industry, researchers, startups and investors. I invite technology leaders to engage with Karnataka and help us shape a globally competitive deep-tech ecosystem," he said.
The minister said the government was focused on creating an enabling environment for technology companies to build, test, manufacture and scale their businesses in the state.
Karnataka would build on its existing strengths in IT and aerospace while expanding into emerging areas such as quantum technologies, spacetech, dronetech, artificial intelligence and geospatial technologies, he said, in a statement.
Referring to the Karnataka Space Technology Policy 2025-30, Singh said the state aims to capture 50% of India's space market and 5% of the global market by 2033.
The policy also seeks to attract $3 billion in investments and train 50,000 professionals, he added.
The minister also called for greater use of satellite imagery, drones, GIS, remote sensing and artificial intelligence for groundwater management, mapping of tanks and lakes, irrigation asset management and monitoring of projects.
"Technology becomes meaningful when it solves real problems faced by people. Our message is simple: Build in Karnataka, Test in Karnataka, Make in Karnataka, Grow from Karnataka and take your technology to the world," he said.
The roundtable at Sheraton Grand Bengaluru was attended by former ISRO chairman S Somanath, Consul General of Israel to South India Orli Weitzman, and representatives of NewSpace India Limited, Pixxel, Dhruva Space, ideaForge, Axelspace, BlackSky, Capella Space, EnduroSat, Sarla Aviation, and TakeMe2Space, besides investors and technology industry leaders.

articles.title: Reprise, déplacements, télétravail : cette eSIM Europe garde la data sous contrôle

Ubigi Europe 10 Go à 15 € : l’eSIM prépayée pour voyager en septembre
Ubigi Europe propose une eSIM prépayée de 10 Go valable 30 jours à 15 €, pratique pour voyager, travailler ou étudier à l’étranger en septembre.
Septembre relance les déplacements. Reprise du travail à l’étranger, séminaire en Europe, Erasmus, salon professionnel, week-end prolongé avant l’automne : la connexion mobile redevient vite un sujet concret. L’eSIM Ubigi Europe répond justement à ce besoin simple : partir avec une enveloppe data séparée, lisible et activable sans carte SIM physique. Son forfait Europe 10 Go valable 30 jours est affiché à 15 €, sous forme de forfait ponctuel prépayé. Ubigi indique aussi une installation immédiate sur appareil compatible eSIM et déverrouillé, sans frais additionnels ni frais de roaming.
Une enveloppe data claire pour les voyages de rentrée
L’intérêt d’une eSIM de voyage se voit surtout quand le séjour est court mais chargé. Une réunion à Milan, quelques jours de télétravail à Lisbonne, un déplacement à Bruxelles, une rentrée universitaire en Espagne : dans tous ces cas, mieux vaut éviter de dépendre uniquement du Wi-Fi public ou de chercher une carte SIM locale à l’arrivée.
Avec 10 Go sur 30 jours, Ubigi vise les usages mobiles essentiels : mails, messageries, navigation web, itinéraires, réservations, appels via WhatsApp ou FaceTime, documents partagés et consultation d’outils professionnels en déplacement. Ce volume ne remplacera pas une connexion fixe pour du streaming intensif ou de longues visioconférences quotidiennes, mais il donne une vraie marge pour rester connecté sans flou sur la consommation.
| Élément | Détail | 
|---|---|
| Offre | Ubigi Europe | 
| Type | eSIM prépayée ponctuelle | 
| Data | 10 Go | 
| Validité | 30 jours | 
| Prix | 15 € | 
| Installation | QR code par e-mail | 
| Usage | Données mobiles uniquement | 
| Partage de connexion | Autorisé | 
Ubigi précise que son service est centré sur la donnée mobile. Pour les appels et SMS, il faut donc passer par des applications de messagerie comme WhatsApp, Skype, Telegram ou Messenger. C’est suffisant pour beaucoup de voyageurs, mais cela mérite d’être clair avant de partir.
Une solution pratique pour travailler hors de France
Pour une reprise professionnelle, le vrai confort vient de la préparation. L’eSIM peut être achetée avant le départ, reçue par QR code, puis installée sur le smartphone compatible. La fonction Smartstart lance l’activation du forfait à l’arrivée dans une destination couverte, ce qui évite de perdre des jours de validité trop tôt.
Les points à retenir :
- 10 Go de data en Europe ;
- 30 jours de validité ;
- 15 € en forfait ponctuel ;
- pas de carte SIM physique ;
- recharge depuis l’application ;
- partage de connexion possible ;
- eSIM réutilisable dans plus de 200 destinations.
Cette dernière possibilité compte pour ceux qui voyagent régulièrement. Une fois installée, l’eSIM peut resservir lors d’un prochain déplacement, avec une recharge depuis l’application, même sans Wi-Fi ni crédit data restant selon Ubigi.
Avant de souscrire, deux vérifications restent indispensables : le smartphone doit être compatible eSIM et débloqué tout opérateur. Pour un déplacement de septembre, Ubigi Europe garde donc un positionnement simple : une enveloppe data claire, prépayée, pensée pour voyager et travailler sans mauvaise surprise de roaming.

articles.title: « 0 g de CO2 » : la promesse ultime des voitures électriques est-elle un gros mensonge ?
articles.text:
« 0 g de CO2/km » : ce sont les émissions de CO2 affichées sur l’écriteau de cette sympathique citadine électrique. Le tout s’accompagne d’une flatteuse étiquette énergétique classée A. De quoi donner droit aux aides maximales tant que l’auto respecte certains critères de production. Et là est tout le problème : ces conditions ne sont pas suffisamment prises en compte pour dresser un bilan carbone plus précis de ces modèles.
L’Université Technique de Munich a en ce sens passé au crible les émissions des véhicules électriques sur l’ensemble de leur cycle de vie. En prenant pour base 19 études antérieures et en s’appuyant sur 47 scénarios modélisés, les chercheurs ont constaté que les voitures à batterie produisent en moyenne 41 % de CO2 en moins sur toute leur utilisation par rapport aux modèles thermiques équivalents.
41 % de réduction de CO2 : une réalité bien loin du « zéro émission »
Si cela rassure, les recherches démontrent que les véhicules électriques polluent tout de même plus qu’attendu. Une réduction moyenne de 41 % d’un quelconque nombre ne permet en effet pas d’arriver à zéro comme le clament officiellement les fiches techniques. C’est mathématique. Et selon les scénarios d’utilisation, les véhicules étudiés, la production des batteries et de l’électricité ainsi que le recyclage, les chiffres varient énormément.
Les émissions de CO2 peuvent ainsi être inférieures de 89 % comme elles peuvent excéder de 21 % celles d’un modèle thermique équivalent en fonction du modèle de véhicule analysé. Ces différences montrent la faiblesse des normes actuelles mesurant les émissions polluantes. L’Union Européenne se concentre uniquement sur les particules émises à l’échappement et non sur le cycle de vie global des véhicules. Raison pour laquelle les modèles électriques sont extrêmement favorisés.
Une « grave erreur d’orientation » pointée du doigt
Outre la prise en compte de la production, de l’utilisation et du recyclage, le calcul pourrait encore être affiné via plusieurs variables. L’emploi d’un acier spécifique à faible teneur en CO2 et la réutilisation des batteries en seconde vie pour du stockage d’énergie sont les très nombreux points pouvant être optimisés. Cela permettrait alors de réorienter les clients vers les modèles vraiment vertueux.
L’Université Technique de Munich considère les méthodes d’homologation actuelles comme une « grave erreur d’orientation » de la politique climatique européenne. Celle-ci favorise l’ensemble des véhicules électriques, ce qui est naturellement voulu, certes, mais place également à égalité les modèles produits sans attention particulière à l’environnement. Les voitures chinoises venant parfois de très loin sont notamment ciblées.
Vers une révision inévitable des règles européennes
Des changements sont donc nécessaires, même si cela impliquera une révision particulièrement longue et laborieuse de l’ensemble des critères. La Commission européenne a déjà proposé de revoir à la baisse l’objectif de réduction des émissions de CO2 des véhicules neufs. Initialement fixé à 100 % de réduction entre 2021 et 2035, il passera finalement à 90 % de réduction. Moins ambitieux, mais certainement plus réaliste…

articles.title: Mayrit llega a Palos de la Frontera un mes antes de lo previsto: la gigantesca tuneladora pilla ritmo por el subsuelo de Madrid
articles.text:
La ampliación del metro de Madrid ha superado otro hito. Y es que la tuneladora conocida como Mayrit se abrió paso el pasado viernes en la futura estación de Palos de la Frontera, lo que marca el segundo “cale” (momento en que la tuneladora conecta con la cavidad de la estación) desde que comenzaron las obras en marzo.
Un proyecto ambicioso. La ampliación de la Línea 11 es uno de los proyectos más ambiciosos en los que Madrid se ha sumergido desde hace décadas. Una vez finalizada se extenderá en diagonal, conectando Cuatro Vientos en el suroeste con Valdebebas en el noreste, reduciendo así los tiempos de viaje y añadiendo una nueva opción para miles de vecinos.
En cifras. Desde que comenzó su viaje en la estación de Comillas en Carabanchel el 26 de marzo, Mayrit ha excavado una galería continua de 2.732 metros en 147 días, instalando 1.606 anillos de dovelas y retirando cerca de 189.000 metros cúbicos de tierra, según las cifras publicadas por El Debate.
En su último tramo entre Madrid Río y Palos de la Frontera, la máquina iba a un ritmo de unos 22,8 metros al día de media. Es un muy buen ritmo teniendo en cuenta que comenzó en unos 15 metros al día en marzo.
En detalle. Miguel Núñez, director general de Infraestructuras de la Comunidad de Madrid, atribuye la mejora del rendimiento a que la máquina y el terreno se comportaron “extraordinariamente bien”, según comparten en 20 Minutos, señalando que las arcillas negras y las capas de sílex atravesadas en este tramo respondieron bien a la excavación. Por su parte, el consejero de Transportes, Jorge Rodrigo, que también asistió al cale, declaraba al medio que "lo que hace unos meses era un desafío hoy lo estamos viendo convertido en realidad".
Antes de lo previsto, con un pequeño contratiempo. No se esperaba llegar a Palos de la Frontera hasta principios de otoño, pero Mayrit ha llegado casi un mes antes, haciendo el cale alrededor de la 1:00 PM y con solo media hora de retraso causado por un problema en uno de sus componentes, según informa el medio. Sin embargo, la velocidad a la que iba la máquina ha superado el ritmo de trabajo de la propia estación, pues la construcción se encontraba cerca del 74 % de ejecución cuando la máquina la alcanzó.
El tramo sur del futuro andén sí estaba completamente terminado, pero la sección central (que abarca 140 metros de distancia a unos 33 metros bajo tierra) todavía tenía zonas encofradas y otros tramos de tierra sin excavar, compartían desde 20 Minutos.
Todavía queda un buen trecho. Terminar el túnel no es lo mismo que terminar las obras, pues junto al avance de Mayrit, los equipos aún están completando aproximadamente 679 metros de túnel a “pico y pala”, una técnica tradicional más lenta que se está utilizando sobre todo cerca de los puntos de acceso a las estaciones. En conjunto, se prevé que la tuneladora y los trabajos manuales se encuentren en torno al 60% de su finalización, según comparte El Debate.
Próximos pasos. Tal y como cuenta el medio, Mayrit permanecerá detenida en Palos de la Frontera durante dos o tres semanas para una revisión técnica, sustituyendo las piezas desgastadas de la rueda de corte antes de ponerse con el siguiente tramo de 709 metros hacia Atocha, una etapa que se estima que comience antes de que termine septiembre. Y es que si se mantiene el ritmo del verano, el próximo tramo de túnel podría estar terminado antes de finales de octubre.
Eso sí, parece que no va a haber más cales ni en Atocha ni en Conde de Casal, ya que el ritmo al que va la tuneladora va más rápido que la excavación de las estaciones. En su lugar, los equipos que trabajan en Atocha y Conde de Casal (actualmente al 57 % y casi al 31 % de ejecución, respectivamente) se encontrarán con unos 140 metros de túnel ya construido bajo tierra, una estructura que luego será demolida y retirada junto con el resto del material excavado.
Calendario. La ampliación de la Línea 11 cuenta con un presupuesto de unos 1.550 millones de euros y su apertura se mantiene para finales de 2027 o principios de 2028. Así que cuando finalice su trabajo la tuneladora, aún quedará mucho que hacer en las estaciones hasta que de por concluida la obra. Tendremos que esperar para saber cómo se acaba materializando el proyecto.
