articles.title: En Chine, les premiers chiens-robots pour aveugle commencent à apparaître
articles.text:
La robotique fait des pas de géants en Chine. Et c'est un appareil extrêmement intéressant qui est en train de naître dans ce cadre dans l'empire du Milieu.
Même Elon Musk l'avait reconnu sur X : la Chine est un concurrent redoutable des États-Unis dans le secteur de la robotique. Et à vrai dire, il semble même qu'aujourd'hui la seconde économie mondiale soit tout simplement la locomotive de ce domaine, avec des exploits régulièrement réitérés - comme celui où un robot a battu le record d'Usain Bolt au 100 mètres. Et cette nouvelle innovation ne fait que confirmer la tendance !
Le plus grand fabricant d'armes chinois présente son chien robot pour aveugle
Que pourront donc remplacer les robots à l'avenir ? Beaucoup de choses semble-t-il, vu la nouveauté qui vient d'être présentée par l'Institut de recherche Zhiyuan, affilié au géant chinois de l'armement North Industries Group.
Ce dernier a en effet lancé un nouveau robot chien, destiné à remplacer les chiens pour aveugle. Baptisé Xiaoyuan, il possède quatre roues pour pouvoir avancer rapidement sur terrain plat, et quatre pattes, utiles pour grimper.
Un marché énorme en Chine en prévision, où les chiens pour aveugles sont rares
Ce robot affiche sur le papier des caractéristiques particulièrement solides, puisqu'il est à la fois très silencieux (utile pour les aveugles habitués à s'aider de leur ouïe pour s'orienter) et aurait un taux d'évitement d'obstacles incroyablement élevé. Celui-ci serait de 99% en intérieur et de 96% en extérieur.
Et il pourrait s'agir rapidement de plus que d'un simple prototype exprimant les capacités ingénieuriales de l'Institut Zhiyuan. En effet, la Chine compte à cette heure aujourd'hui plus de 17 millions de personnes malvoyantes, quand on ne dénombre en comparaison que quelque 400 chiens d'aveugle en circulation dans le pays. Un animal qui demande un an de formation, et coûte environ 200 000 yuans (près de 25 600 euros). Autant dire que sa version robot pourrait trouver facilement preneur !

articles.title: 2 Nigerian startups secure $450k from Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startups Trade Lenda and AirSmat have raised a combined US$450,000 from the Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, a US$4 million pilot investment facility aimed at identifying founders often overlooked by traditional investors, which is making its first investments in the country.
Managed by Village Capital with funding from the Dutch Entrepreneurial Development Bank (FMO) and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), the Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility aims to provide early-stage capital for startups in Ghana, Nigeria, and Tanzania that are advancing climate resilience and economic mobility.
The facility runs a locally-led investment model, partnering with in-market entrepreneur support organisations (ESOs) that help identify strong founder teams, shape investment pipelines, and advise on due diligence. Its first investments in Nigeria bring its total to seven, after backing five startups in Ghana previously.
The first investment is in Trade Lenda, a digital financial services platform expanding access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises through digital business loans, embedded finance solutions, and Sharia-compliant financing products. Since its launch, the startup has supported more than 260,000 SMEs and farmers across five of Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones, with 66% of its customers women.
“The capital has enabled us to accelerate our growth, acquire a higher license, and attract more competitive funding,” said Adeshina Adewumi, co-founder and CEO at Trade Lenda.
“Following the investment, we secured an additional US$2 million in local debt facilities at lower rates, allowing us to expand lending while reducing our cost of capital. As we continue to secure more affordable financing, we’re able to pass those savings on to the SMEs and entrepreneurs we serve across Nigeria and Africa.”
The second investment is in AirSmat, a climate technology company transforming agricultural waste into biochar-based fertiliser. Its solution removes carbon while improving soil health, increasing agricultural productivity, and creating new income opportunities for farmers through carbon markets.
“Access to capital structured around the realities of building a climate-tech company has been transformative for AirSmat,” said Soji Sanyaolu, founder and CEO at AirSmat. “The investment will be used to complete and commission our commercial biochar-based fertiliser factory, and scale our commercial operations. It will also strengthen our manufacturing capacity, expand market access, and accelerate the delivery of climate-smart agricultural solutions that improve soil health, increase farmer productivity, and create sustainable livelihoods.”
Husein Merchant, investment officer at Village Capital, said what made these two startups stand out about these startups was how they are strengthening the systems that businesses and farmers rely on to grow.
“Trade Lenda is expanding access to finance for hundreds of thousands of SMEs and farmers, while AirSmat is transforming agricultural waste into productive inputs that strengthen food systems and improve farmer livelihoods. Both companies are deeply rooted in the realities of their markets, and our role is to make sure they have access to the right capital to grow their impact,” he said.
Africa Fintech Foundry was among the local players that played a key role in sourcing the facility’s first investments in Nigeria, leveraging its local market expertise and founder network to identify high-potential startups for investments.
“We don’t often see investors partnering so intentionally with local ecosystem organisations, and that’s what makes this facility different,” said Carolina Gideon-Krama, venture analyst at Africa Fintech Foundry. “Because we’re deeply embedded in Nigeria’s startup ecosystem, we’re able to identify founders with strong potential long before they’re on the radar of traditional investors. We’re proud to have worked with Village Capital to identify both Trade Lenda and AirSmat for investment and to help connect them with financing designed for their stage of growth.”

articles.title: Why these 5 books keep readers hooked till the last page
articles.text:
Why these 5 books keep readers hooked till the last page
Discover 5 gripping books readers can finish in one sitting, from unforgettable stories to page-turning plots that make stopping nearly impossible.
There is a special kind of book that makes you forget to check the time. You start reading a few pages, tell yourself you will stop after the next chapter, and suddenly you are halfway through the story. Before you know it, the final page is staring back at you. These are the books that create the rare feeling of being completely absorbed in another world.
In an age of short videos, endless notifications, and shrinking attention spans, finishing an entire book in one sitting might sound difficult. Yet readers continue to crave stories that can hold their attention from beginning to end. The appeal is not necessarily about reading quickly; it is about finding a narrative so compelling that putting the book down feels harder than continuing.
From emotional journeys and unexpected twists to beautifully written stories that demand your attention, these five books have the kind of momentum that can turn “just one chapter” into an entire afternoon or night of reading.
5 Books readers can finish in one sitting
1. The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo by Taylor Jenkins Reid
What if a legendary Hollywood icon finally decided to reveal the truth behind her glamorous life and seven marriages? That irresistible premise lies at the centre of The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo, a novel filled with ambition, love, sacrifice, and carefully guarded secrets.
Its blend of old Hollywood glamour and emotional storytelling creates a compelling narrative that immediately captures attention.
What makes the book especially easy to read in one sitting is the constant sense of mystery surrounding Evelyn’s past. With every chapter, new revelations reshape the reader’s understanding of her relationships and choices. As the pieces of her life story gradually come together, the desire to uncover her biggest secret becomes impossible to resist, making the novel a true page-turner from beginning to end.
2. The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho
Few books demonstrate the power of simplicity quite like The Alchemist. Paulo Coelho follows Santiago, a young shepherd who sets out on a journey after dreaming about a hidden treasure. What begins as a physical search gradually becomes a spiritual journey about purpose, courage, dreams, and listening to one's heart.
The book's short chapters, straightforward storytelling, and philosophical ideas make it incredibly approachable. Yet its simplicity does not make it forgettable. Each stage of Santiago's journey introduces another lesson that naturally pulls the reader forward.
You may begin reading because of the promise of adventure, but you continue because you want to discover what the journey ultimately means. It is the kind of book that can be finished quickly yet leave you thinking about its message long after the final page.
3. Before the Coffee Gets Cold by Toshikazu Kawaguchi
What if you could sit down for one last conversation with someone from your past? Before the Coffee Gets Cold explores this emotional possibility through a small café in Japan where customers can travel back in time under very specific conditions. There is one important rule: no matter what they do in the past, they cannot change the present.
That limitation makes every conversation more meaningful. Instead of focusing on changing history, the characters are allowed to say what they never said or hear what they desperately needed to hear. The novel is divided into interconnected stories, which makes it easy to keep reading from one emotional encounter to the next.
4. The Silent Patient by Alex Michaelides
The Silent Patient has all the ingredients of a book that can turn “one more chapter” into an entire night of reading. The psychological thriller follows Alicia Berenson, a successful painter whose seemingly perfect life changes dramatically when she is accused of murdering her husband.
The most mysterious part is what happens afterwards: Alicia refuses to speak a single word. Her silence becomes the central mystery, leaving readers desperate to understand what really happened.
The story keeps building suspense through unanswered questions, shifting perspectives, and carefully placed revelations. Why did Alicia kill her husband? What happened on the night of the murder? And why has she remained completely silent ever since? As the investigation progresses, every new discovery makes the truth seem even more complicated. With its fast pace, psychological tension, and unexpected twists, the novel creates the kind of momentum that makes putting it down remarkably difficult.
5. The Housemaid by Freida McFadden
If psychological suspense is what keeps you turning pages, The Housemaid delivers exactly that kind of reading experience. Freida McFadden's thriller places readers inside the unsettling world of a housemaid who begins working for a wealthy family and soon realises that the seemingly perfect household is hiding disturbing secrets.
The appeal comes largely from its constant tension and unanswered questions. Just when you think you understand what is happening, another detail changes your perception of the characters or situation. The relatively fast pace makes the story particularly easy to race through, especially for readers who enjoy twists and cliffhangers.
Why do some books feel impossible to put down?
The best one-sitting reads aren’t always about complex plots. They hook you with curiosity, emotion, and momentum, making it impossible to stop turning pages.
In a world full of distractions, these books offer pure escape. You don’t read them quickly because you want to finish; you read them quickly because you can’t stop.

articles.title: 220 million traveler records exposed in Vietnam-linked APIS leak
articles.text:
An Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) database holding more than 220 million passenger and crew records, including passport numbers and flight details, was accessible online through a chain of security misconfigurations. The system appears linked to a Vietnamese organization, according to the researchers who discovered it.
Advance Passenger Information Systems are used worldwide to collect identity, passport, and flight information from airlines before passengers and crew arrive at or depart from a country.
The exposed records span January 2017 to April 2026 and could involve travelers of many nationalities who flew to, from, or through Vietnam during that period.
Nine years of passenger and crew data
Kinryū Labs discovered the Elasticsearch cluster on June 3 while surveying exposed databases as part of research into ransomware activity.
The cluster, named 'pax-info', contained 29 indices and roughly 107 GB of data. Its two principal indices held 210,318,069 passenger records and 10,465,631 crew records, for a combined 220,783,700 entries.
According to Kinryū Labs, the cluster was hosted in Viettel-assigned IP space in Hanoi. BleepingComputer could not confirm which Vietnamese organization operated the system.
The exposed information included passengers' and crew members' names, dates of birth, sex, nationalities, passport or travel-document numbers, document expiration dates, and issuing countries.
Associated travel data included flight numbers and dates, airlines, departure, destination and transit airports, seat assignments, baggage references, and scheduled, estimated, and actual flight times, information typically carried by APIS and related airline systems.
Sample records reviewed by BleepingComputer included travelers of Korean, Chinese, Canadian, and New Zealand nationality, among others.
While the researchers could not provide a complete breakdown by nationality, the data covered numerous international airlines across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Middle East. As a result, the exposed records could relate to people from virtually anywhere who visited or transited through Vietnam over the nine-year period.
Kinryū Labs verified that the information was legitimate by matching records in the database against its researchers' own travel to Vietnam.
The figures represent travel records rather than unique individuals. Passengers and crew members who flew multiple times may therefore appear repeatedly in the database.
Database accessible through chained misconfigurations
Kinryū Labs told BleepingComputer that it reached the database by chaining two misconfigurations.
From the open internet, the endpoint returned an HTTP 401 "Unauthorized" response, preventing direct access to the database. However, a cloud-based path enabled researchers to reach the cluster, which then accepted default credentials.
Internet intelligence platform FOFA first recorded the host and port in October 2022 and identified the service as a database in July 2023. However, Kinryū Labs could not determine when the passenger data first became retrievable through the second access path.
As a result, while the records themselves span more than nine years, the actual length of the exposure is unknown.
Kinryū Labs said it reported the issue to Vietnamese authorities, airlines represented in the database, and national computer emergency response teams beginning June 3. The researchers said access to the database was remediated on June 8.
An authenticated email reviewed by BleepingComputer shows that Singapore Airlines' security team helped coordinate the response, informing Kinryū Labs on June 8 that it had "engaged the relevant parties" and "taken steps to contain the issue." Singapore Airlines did not provide an additional comment to BleepingComputer.
The findings shared with BleepingComputer identify several major airlines whose passenger records appeared in the database. However, there is no indication that the airlines operated the exposed system or that their own networks were compromised.
Changi Airport Group, which manages and operates Singapore's Changi Airport, told BleepingComputer that it had investigated the matter but declined to comment.
BleepingComputer also contacted Vietnamese authorities well in advance of publication but received no response.
It remains unclear whether the database was downloaded, sold, ransomed, or otherwise exploited by malicious actors before it was secured. Kinryū Labs said it found no ransom notes or unfamiliar indices on the cluster and could not identify the dataset being offered for sale online.
However, without access to server logs, the researchers could not conclusively determine whether anyone had copied the data.
Kinryū Labs expects to publish additional technical findings on its blog later this week.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Microsoft abandonne Office 2021 le mois prochain : cet éditeur prend le relais sur les mises à jour
articles.text:
Cinq ans après sa sortie, Office 2021 arrive au bout du support que Microsoft lui avait promis : le 13 octobre 2026, Word, Excel et consorts recevront leur dernier correctif de sécurité, éditions LTSC comprises. Les logiciels continueront naturellement de fonctionner, mais chaque faille découverte ensuite restera ouverte. C’est là qu’intervient ACROS Security, éditeur slovène connu pour son service 0patch, s’attelant à sécuriser les produits Microsoft que le géant de Redmond abandonné : Windows 7, Office 2016, Windows Server 2012… Office 2021 n’est donc que la continuité d’un travail déjà bien établi, et le passage de flambeau arrive à point nommé.
Ce qui s’arrête le 13 octobre, et ce qui continue
La fin de support ne débranche rien du jour au lendemain : vos applications s’ouvriront le 14 octobre exactement comme la veille (aucun compte à rebours caché dans le code). Ce qui disparaît, c’est le colmatage mensuel des brèches, sur une suite dont les documents piégés, macros et pièces jointes en tête, restent l’un des vecteurs d’attaque préférés des cybercriminels. Microsoft recommande sans surprise de migrer vers Microsoft 365 ou Office 2024, les deux seules branches encore entretenues de la famille.
L’offre de remplacement fonctionne autrement : à partir du 14 octobre, 0patch diffusera pendant au moins trois ans des micropatchs, de minuscules correctifs injectés en mémoire pendant que le logiciel tourne, sans toucher aux fichiers ni exiger de redémarrage. Une rustine posée moteur tournant, en somme. Le périmètre est assumé : uniquement les failles critiques, uniquement sous Windows, sans assistance technique ni nouvelle fonction. Comptez 24,95 € hors taxes par poste et par an avec l’offre Pro, soit un peu moins de 30 € TTC.
Prolonger, racheter, s’abonner : le vrai calcul
Reste à poser les options côte à côte. Conserver Office 2021 sous perfusion 0patch revient à une trentaine d’euros par an, sans rien changer à ses habitudes. Repasser à la caisse pour Office Famille 2024 coûte 149 € en une fois, pour un support qui court jusqu’en octobre 2029, soit un nouveau cycle de trois ans avant de rejouer la même partition. L’abonnement Microsoft 365 Personnel s’affiche à 99 € par an (ou 10 € par mois), stockage en ligne et mises à jour permanentes inclus. LibreOffice, enfin, ne coûte rien et ouvre sans broncher la plupart des documents Office, un candidat sérieux pour l’usage occasionnel.
Les licences dites perpétuelles paient désormais une deuxième fois pour rester sûres, pendant que Microsoft pousse méthodiquement vers l’abonnement, dont les tarifs professionnels français ont d’ailleurs augmenté au 1er juillet (Copilot et Defender en guise de justification). Le prolongement de vie des logiciels abandonnés, lui, devient un marché à part entière. Le précédent Windows 10 a montré qu’un sursis gratuit pouvait exister : sous la pression des associations de consommateurs, les utilisateurs européens y avaient gagné un an de correctifs offerts (et une rallonge jusqu’en octobre 2027). Personne, cette fois, ne semble prêt à monter au créneau pour une suite bureautique.

articles.title: OpenAI dio acceso a Internet a miles de agentes. Ellos acabaron montándose su propio Slack en una vieja wiki alemana
articles.text:
Un grupo de agentes de OpenAI recibió una tarea que a priori parecía bastante aburrida: buscar información en internet a toda velocidad. Tenían acceso controlado a la web y podían leer páginas, pero en principio no podían escribir en ellas. El experimento se acabó desmandando: los agentes encontraron una viejo sitio alemán en formato wiki que descubrieron que podían modificar, y acabaron convirtiendo esa página en una improvisada plataforma de colaboración.
La tarea era inocente. Es importante destacar que a diferencia de otros incidentes recientes protagonizados por agentes de OpenAI, aquí la IA no estaba intentando hackear un sistema o intentando superar una prueba de ciberseguridad. Lo único que tenían que hacer teóricamente era realizar búsquedas web con ciertos límites de tiempo. A partir de ahí se desencadenó un proceso que hizo que si un agente encontraba una respuesta y la dejaba escrita en algún sitio, otros agentes podrían reutilzarla para completar su tarea más rápidamente. No está claro cómo descubrieron que tenían que acudir precisamente a esa web, pero puede que el aprendizaje por refuerzo acabara contribuyendo a que ese descubrimiento acabara incorporando el conocimiento de ese recurso.
Vamos a montarnos un Slack propio. El sitio que encontraron fue DSEWiki, una antigua wiki alemana para desarrolladores que llevaba prácticamente dos décadas abandonada. Según los investigadores, había recibido apenas diez ediciones durante los últimos 20 años. Los agentes empezaron a utilizarla en mayo para dejar enlaces y resultados de búsquedas. A mediados de junio aquello explotó, y en aproximadamente una semana realizaron unas 13.000 ediciones. Habían convertido una web olvidada en una base de concocimiento compartido entre máquinas: un Slack robótico del que nadie se había percatado.
Se suponía que solo podían "leer" internet. OpenAI había configurado el acceso de estos agentes a internet detrás de un proxy diseñado para permitir solo peticiones GET, es decir, solo lecturas, evitando así operaciones que podían escribir en esos sitios web. El problema es que las viejas wikis basadas en la plataforma UseMod permitían realizar acciones de escritura también con GET. Los agentes buscaron precisamente software antiguo susceptible de funcionar así y descubrieron que podían escribir en esas páginas. Fue el momento "bingo" de un proceso que teóricamente estaba controlado.
Compartiendo información. Los mensajes que se fueron dejaron los agentes contenían respuestas a las pruebas, enlaces útiles y técnicas que otros agentes podían reutilizar. Algunos llegaron bastante más lejos: intercambiaron métodos para eludir las restricciones de los sandbox que OpenAI había creado, como posibles técnicas de XSS (ejecución de código cruzado) contra la propia wiki e ideas para hacerse pasar por moderadores de la wiki. En tres mensajes usaron incluso la palabra swarm (enjambre) para referirse al colectivo de agentes que estaba participando en todo este proceso. Los investigadores de ciberseguridad describen el comportamiento de estos agentes como una colaboración destinada a lo que precisamente les pidieron: mejorar sus resultados en las pruebas.
Entonces apareció un humano. El 2 de junio un administrador del sitio descubrió ese contenido extraño y empezó a borrarlo como si fuera spam, pero los agentes siguieron publicando. Cuando la actividad se disparó semanas después, el administrador llegó a eliminar unas 100 páginas diarias mientras los agentes creaban unas 400. Lo curioso fue lo que descubrieron después.
ZZZ. Uno de los momentos más alucinantes de todo este "hackeo" se produjo cuando los agentes detectaron que ese administrador humano estaba eliminando páginas siguiendo más o menos un orden alfabético. Para esquivar esas acciones, empezaron a crear copias con nombres que empezaban por ZZZ para que tardase más tiempo en llegar a ellas.
OpenAI acaba enterándose. El 22 de junio la actividad de los agentes cayó prácticamente a cero. Los investigadores del incidente descubrieron además visitas aparentemente humanas procedentes de direcciones IP de OpenAI poco antes de que cesara la actividad. OpenAI confirmó después que los agentes eran suyos y que había detectado el suceso. Según la compañía la información revisada no indicaba que los agentes "hackearan" la wiki, aunque sí reconocía que ya habían mostrado comportamientos similares en pruebas internas. En Reuters afirman que directivos de OpenAI se enteraron del incidente hace semanas pero no dijeron nada tras las críticas por el reciente problema que surgió con Hugging Face.

articles.title: Fone de ouvido para corrida: os 10 melhores modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Fone de ouvido para corrida: os 10 melhores modelos para comprar em 2026
Selecionamos os melhores fones de ouvido para correr; encontre modelos para corrida ao ar livre ou em locais fechados, de marcas como JBL, Bose, Shokz e Anker
Os melhores fones de ouvido para corrida em 2026 oferecem certificação contra suor, chuva e poeira, além de inovações em ergonomia, de forma que o dispositivo não caia da orelha durante uma prova.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog reuniu 10 modelos de marcas como JBL, Anker e Shokz, que vão desde os tradicionais intra-auriculares até formatos open-ear, como os de condução óssea. Veja as especificações e os pontos positivos e negativos de cada produto a seguir.
O JBL Endurance Peak 4 é um fone intra-auricular voltado para atividades esportivas, com ganchos que passam ao redor das orelhas e ajudam na fixação. O modelo pesa 10,5 g por lado e tem certificação IP68, que indica resistência à poeira e à água.
Para situações em que o usuário precisa continuar ouvindo o ambiente, há os modos Ambient Aware e TalkThru. Essa combinação permite alternar entre maior isolamento e maior percepção dos sons externos, algo que pode ser relevante conforme o local da corrida.
O sistema de áudio usa drivers de 10 mm e oferece cancelamento adaptativo de ruído. A autonomia é de 12 horas com o ANC desligado ou 8 horas com o recurso ativado, e o estojo soma até 48 horas. O Peak 4 traz Bluetooth 5.4, conexão multiponto e seis microfones para chamadas.
O Bose Ultra Open Earbuds tem uma construção aberta apoiada na lateral das orelhas. Ao contrário dos fones intra-auriculares com modo de transparência, o modelo não precisa processar os sons externos para que você os ouça, preservando a percepção do entorno durante a reprodução de música.
No entanto, esse formato traz algumas limitações: ele não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo e tem certificação IPX4, voltada à resistência contra respingos apenas.
O modelo utiliza Bluetooth 5.3, suporta conexão multiponto com dois dispositivos e permite ajustes de equalização pelo aplicativo da Bose. Já a bateria chega a sete horas e meia de reprodução com o Immersive Audio desligado. Quando ativado, a autonomia cai para até cinco horas; o estojo acrescenta outras 19 horas e meia.
No Soundcore Sport X20, cada unidade pesa cerca de 6,6 g e o encaixe é formado por ponteiras intra-auriculares e ganchos ajustáveis que passam ao redor das orelhas.
A estrutura recebe certificação IP68 e a tecnologia SweatGuard, para proteger fones de ouvido contra a corrosão causada pelo suor, enquanto os drivers dinâmicos têm 11 mm.
O modelo também possui cancelamento ativo de ruído e seis microfones com processamento por IA para chamadas. Para uma corrida ao ar livre, é possível alternar entre o cancelamento e os recursos de audição do ambiente de acordo com a necessidade.
Entre as especificações, o Sport X20 traz Bluetooth 5.3, suporta conexão multiponto e tem autonomia de até 12 horas nos fones — 48 horas considerando o estojo.
O JBL Endurance Race 2 utiliza um estabilizador que se apoia na parte interna da orelha para manter os fones posicionados durante exercícios. O conjunto pesa 53,9 g considerando fones e estojo e vem com três tamanhos de ponteiras, além da presença de certificação IP68 para proteção contra suor, chuva e poeira.
Com drivers de 6,8 mm, o fone da JBL também traz os modos Ambient Aware e TalkThru que podem ser alternados via toque. O aplicativo da marca também oferece configurações específicas para atividades esportivas.
A bateria chega a 12 horas de reprodução com o ANC desligado e o estojo acrescenta outras 36 horas, totalizando até 48 horas de uso. Com o cancelamento ativado, a autonomia dos fones cai para até 7 horas.
O Shokz OpenMove usa condução óssea em vez de alto-falantes convencionais. As vibrações são transmitidas pela região próxima às têmporas, mantendo os ouvidos abertos. Assim, o som ambiente continua chegando ao usuário durante a reprodução, diferentemente dos fones intra-auriculares.
A estrutura pesa 29 g e utiliza uma haste que passa atrás da cabeça. A classificação IP55 indica resistência a poeira e respingos de água, incluindo situações de suor e chuva leve, mas não é uma proteção destinada à imersão.
Porém, sua autonomia é de até seis horas por carga, inferior à de vários modelos deste guia.
O JBL Endurance Zone é um fone esportivo de formato aberto. Em vez de vedar o canal auditivo, os drivers ficam próximos às orelhas e reproduzem o áudio enquanto os sons externos continuam sendo ouvidos.
Os drivers dinâmicos têm 18 x 11 mm, mas não há cancelamento ativo de ruído. A certificação IP68 indica proteção contra poeira e água, tendo bons resultados nos testes feitos pelo Tecnoblog, enquanto quatro microfones são usados para chamadas.
Em bateria, a JBL promete até 8 horas de reprodução, ou 32 horas somando com a case. Mas durante nossos testes, o componente teve desempenho acima do esperado: foram 10 horas de reprodução contínua de músicas no Spotify.
O AeroFit 2 também faz parte da categoria de fones open-ear e utiliza ganchos ajustáveis para posicionar os alto-falantes próximos ao ouvido. Assim, o usuário continua ouvindo os sons do ambiente enquanto escuta o conteúdo reproduzido.
Seus drivers medem 20 mm x 11,5 mm e têm formato oval, uma dimensão maior que a de muitos fones intra-auriculares, mas não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo para bloquear o som ambiente. Ele suporta codec LDAC, Hi-Res, tem certificação IP55 para poeira e respingos e recursos de IA.
A bateria chega a dez horas por carga e 42 horas com o estojo. Dez minutos de carregamento acrescentam até quatro horas de reprodução, segundo a marca, e o estojo também aceita carregamento sem fio.
O HUAWEI FreeClip 2 utiliza um formato de clipe, preso à lateral da orelha por uma estrutura em C que permite ouvir os sons externos enquanto o áudio é reproduzido. Cada fone pesa aproximadamente 5,1 g, e os lados são intercambiáveis: o sistema identifica automaticamente se a unidade está na orelha esquerda ou direita.
Os fones têm certificação IP57 para água e poeira, o sistema acústico utiliza um driver duplo de 10,8 mm, enquanto o processamento de chamadas conta com três microfones. No entanto, não oferece cancelamento de ruído ativo.
Com suporte ao Bluetooth 6.0, é possível conectar dois dispositivos simultaneamente, tendo uma autonomia de até nove horas por carga e 38 horas com o estojo, de acordo com a Huawei.
O JBL Soundgear Clips também adota uma construção open-ear em formato de clipe, permitindo que o usuário continue ouvindo os sons do ambiente durante a reprodução. O modelo pesa 6,5 g por unidade e tem quatro microfones que integram o sistema de chamadas.
O Bluetooth 5.4 permite conexão multiponto, e o aplicativo JBL Headphones oferece seis predefinições de equalização, além de oferecer proteção IP54 contra respingos d’água e poeira.
Sua bateria oferece até oito horas de reprodução, enquanto o estojo aumenta a autonomia total para 32 horas. O carregamento completo leva duas horas e há suporte a recarga rápida. Como acontece com outros modelos de ouvido aberto, o Soundgear Clips não utiliza ANC.
O Mibro O1 também utiliza uma construção open-ear que mantém os ouvidos livres e prende os fones à região externa das orelhas. O fone inclui drivers dinâmicos de 15,4 mm e botões físicos para os comandos, mas não traz ANC durante a reprodução de músicas.
No entanto, o Mibro O1 oferece Cancelamento de Ruído Ambiente (ENC), recurso destinado a reduzir ruídos captados pelos microfones e melhorar a transmissão da voz. Sua classificação IPX6 indica resistência a jatos de água, enquanto o Bluetooth 5.3 é usado para a conexão sem fio, mas sem multiponto.
A autonomia chega a sete horas de reprodução nos fones e a aproximadamente 35 horas com o estojo.
A escolha depende principalmente do tipo de encaixe, da resistência à água e da necessidade de ouvir os sons ao redor. Vale observar:
Não há um formato que garanta o mesmo encaixe para todas as pessoas, pois o tamanho e o formato das orelhas variam. Para atividades com bastante movimento, modelos com ganchos, estabilizadores ou estruturas que envolvem a orelha costumam oferecer uma fixação mais firme.
Depende do ambiente e da preferência do corredor. Fones in-ear oferecem maior isolamento e podem ser mais adequados em locais onde o ruído externo não é prioridade.
Já os modelos open-ear e de condução óssea mantêm os ouvidos mais livres, facilitando a percepção do ambiente, mas deixam o áudio mais sujeito aos ruídos externos e costumam pecar em qualidade sonora.
O JBL Endurance Peak 4 reúne certificação IP68, ganchos ao redor da orelha, ANC adaptativo e até 12 horas de autonomia. O Soundcore Sport X20 é outra opção com IP68, ganchos ajustáveis e até 12 horas por carga, permitindo adaptar melhor o encaixe durante uma prova.
O Soundcore AeroFit 2 é uma excelente opção de fone em formato aberto, pois combina construção com ganchos ajustáveis, certificação IP55, até 10 horas de autonomia e suporte a codecs avançados, como LDAC e Hi-Res.
O Mibro O1 tem um bom custo-benefício, trazendo certificação IPX6 contra jatos d’água e até 35 horas de autonomia considerando o estojo. Para quem prefere um modelo intra-auricular, o Soundcore Sport X20 oferece IP68, ganchos ajustáveis e ANC, embora pertença a uma categoria de preço diferente.
O Modo Transparência usa os microfones do fone para captar sons externos e reproduzi-los junto ao áudio que está sendo ouvido. Dessa forma, é possível perceber conversas, trânsito e outros ruídos sem retirar os fones. Ele é diferente de um projeto open-ear, no qual os sons externos chegam naturalmente ao ouvido.

articles.title: AMD GPUs are climbing the sales charts as Radeon beats Nvidia on Amazon and in Germany
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Despite Nvidia losing fans over the last few years as its focus on gamers diminishes (or disappears), the company's GPUs have dominated the sales charts. But that status quo is starting to change: Amazon's top 10 best-selling GPU list is an even split between Team Red and Team Green, with the highest position held by a Radeon 9000-series card. Meanwhile, in Germany, AMD is the one that's dominating sales – at least at one retailer.
The rise of RDNA 4 was highlighted by TechEpiphany on X.
 – TechEpiphany (@TechEpiphanyYT) September 6, 2026
The Amazon best-selling list has changed slightly since the post, but the Radeon RX 9070 XT is still the top GPU. This Gigabyte version is priced at $749, which, of course, is considerably higher than the GPU's $599 launch MSRP.
The other AMD cards in the chart are an Asus model of the 9070 XT, an Asrock 9070, and an Asus 9060 XT. Nvidia also holds four positions with its RTX 5070, RTX 5060 Ti, and two RTX 5080 models.
Things appear even more favorable for Lisa Su's firm in Germany. The figures, which come from Mindfactory, show AMD accounting for almost 56% of all GPUs sold over the last week, while Nvidia holds a 40% share. Again, the RX 9070 XT is the most popular card by far, followed by the RX 9060.
It's worth remembering that Mindfactory has a reputation for favoring AMD, offering promotions, discounts, and bundles featuring its products, which help push up sales figures. The store's AMD cards have outsold Nvidia's in the past.
However, these charts do illustrate the impact of the memory crisis on the graphics card market. All GPUs are more expensive, but AMD's are often cheaper than equivalent Nvidia cards.
The other reason is likely simple availability. The Amazon chart shows three AMD cards in stock, while Nvidia only has one – a Gigabyte RTX 5080 for a colossal $1,599, and that's with a 6% discount.
Only one company dominates the Steam survey GPU chart
TechEpiphany's claim of AMD "dominating everywhere" might be a bit of an exaggeration, but there are signs of consumers opting for its cards because of the cheaper prices – or just buying them because there are no Nvidia alternatives. The most valuable company in the world still has GPUs in almost 73% of Steam survey participants' machines, compared to AMD's 18.6%, so we're not seeing a red revolution just yet.

articles.title: Italian VC Techshop launches second fund with €43 million first close | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Milan-based VC firm Techshop announces the first closing of Techshop II at €43 million dedicated to pre-Seed and Seed startups developing AI B2B solutions – this edition exceeded its initial fundraising target and is now aiming to to raise €100 million in 2027.
CDP Venture Capital joins as a reference investor, backing the new fund through FoF VenturItaly II and the Digital Transition Fund, which draws on NextGenerationEU resources to support the digital transition of supply chains and SMEs. The commitment of the two vehicles can grow progressively as fundraising with third-party investors advances.
“With Techshop II we want to become the reference Seed fund for European startups applying AI to B2B processes,” say Techshop’s three Partners; Giovanni Strocchi, Gianluca D’Agostino and Aurelio Mezzotero. “The new generation of software does not simply digitise existing tasks, it can automate entire business processes. That calls for specialised investors who move fast and can stand alongside founders from the very earliest stages, bringing operational expertise and international co-investors.”
Techshop II’s first close joins a broader wave of European venture funds raising dedicated capital for early-stage AI, B2B software and enterprise technology in 2026.
EU-Startups has reported approximately €430 million raised across a selected group of comparable vehicles this year, including Merantix Capital’s €103 million early-stage AI fund, Elaia’s €120 million first close for its B2B-focused Digital Venture Fund V, DFF Ventures’ €70 million fund for software and AI in underdigitised industries, and Samaipata’s €70 million first close towards a €110 million AI-native fund.
At the earlier end of the market, Munich-based Vanagon Ventures closed €20 million specifically for pre-Seed B2B AI and DeepTech companies.
“Over the years Techshop has shown consistency in its Seed and post-Seed investment strategy, scouting young startups and supporting them through their growth, including internationally. These capabilities are essential to deliver on our commitment to the development of the Italian and European innovation ecosystem. Techshop II continues a partnership built for the long term, aimed at supporting the creation and growth of new companies in B2B software,” addds Cristina Bini, Head of Indirect Investments at CDP Venture Capital.
Founded in 2021, Techshop is an asset management company specialising in early-stage VC funds dedicated to B2B tech. The firm takes a vertical, hands-on, founder-to-founder approach, supporting pre-Seed and Seed startups in product development, market validation and commercial growth.
Through its first fund, Techshop I, the firm invested in B2B software and SaaS startups, building a portfolio that includes 23 companies such as Shop Circle (now Circeus), Smartness, hlpy, Qomodo, Tot, AxyonAI, GenomeUp, SylloTips and Allsides.
Just over four years from launch, the portfolio shows a MOIC, or “Multiple on Invested Capital”, of 1.8 and a TVPI, or “Total Value to Paid-In Capital”, of 1.5, one of the strongest performances in Europe among funds launched in the same period – according to Techshop.
With Techshop II, the firm becomes a multi-fund platform, with the goal of reaching €150 million in total AUM. The strategy remains focused on early-stage B2B software, with particular attention to the pre-Seed and Seed rounds.
The fund’s thesis is that AI will make the world of B2B SaaS ten times larger (in value) and deeper (in focus), through a multitude of innovations and vertical AI SaaS solutions that will automate tasks, decisions and operational workflows in markets such as consulting, healthcare, finance, software development, customer conversation, data management, enterprise applications, robotics and manufacturing processes.
The fund will invest at least 70% of its capital in private companies resident in the European Union or in the European Economic Area with a permanent establishment in Italy.
The first investments of Techshop II will be announced in the coming weeks and will cover AI solutions for sales, development tools and advisory.

articles.title: CXMT Officially Starts Mass Production of LPDDR6 Memory
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
CXMT Officially Starts Mass Production of LPDDR6 Memory
CXMT has achieved the remarkable feat of officially beginning high-volume manufacturing of LPDDR6 memory. This positions CXMT's LPDDR6 memory modules as some of the first in the industry, with South Korean memory makers on a similar timeline for volume production of this next-generation technology. Reportedly, Xiaomi is the first customer for CXMT's domestic LPDDR6 memory, set to feature in the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold smartphone. Since the Xiaomi 18 Fold is scheduled to launch in September, CXMT's LPDDR6 memory will need to be delivered before the end of the month, indicating that customer shipments are already underway. This news follows recent reports that CXMT is conducting risk production of LPDDR6, suggesting a very high yield in production.
CXMT's LPDDR6 memory will operate at speeds of up to 12.8 Gbps, with the base speed of LPDDR6 being 10.7 Gbps. LPDDR6 builds on where LPDDR5X left off, which could reach speeds of up to 10.7 Gbps when highly overclocked. However, the new standard aims for significantly higher speeds, with the first generation of LPDDR6 from CXMT's fabs reaching 12.8 Gbps. Additionally, CXMT is producing these chips with a 16 Gb capacity, equivalent to 2 GB, and the memory IC is housed in a package-on-package (POP) casing, featuring about 1,295 pins in a ball grid array.Update, 14:55 UTC, September 7th : CXMT's official website confirmed mass production, with Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Tencent, Lenovo, Transsion, Honor, Vivo, and Oppo as customers.
We also learned that SK hynix is close to mass production. The South Korean memory giant announced earlier that its LPDDR6 memory modules would feature a 16 Gb capacity on the sixth-generation 10 nm node, known as 1c, running at up to 14.4 Gbps. Although these SK hynix modules might operate faster, all these speeds fall within JEDEC's official specification for the LPDDR6 standard. We can expect even faster memory chips as technology and manufacturing capabilities continue to advance.

articles.title: Pisa 2025: 17% dos estudantes brasileiros sofrem bullying; cyberbullying atinge 3%
articles.text:
O bullying ainda faz parte da rotina de muitos adolescentes brasileiros. Segundo o Pisa 2025, 17% dos estudantes de 15 anos disseram ter sido vítimas de alguma forma de bullying algumas vezes por mês ou com maior frequência.
O índice ficou abaixo dos 20% da OCDE. O estudo também mostrou que 48% dos brasileiros usam chatbots de IA para estudar, enquanto 81% frequentam escolas que proíbem celulares nas dependências.
Brasil mantém índice de bullying
A Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (OCDE) divulgou os resultados do Pisa 2025 nesta terça-feira (8). O levantamento mostra que a incidência de bullying não mudou de forma significativa no Brasil entre 2022 e 2025.
O resultado contrasta com o cenário observado na maioria dos países e economias participantes, onde o problema aumentou no mesmo período.
Em 2025, 17% dos estudantes brasileiros relataram ter sofrido pelo menos uma forma de bullying algumas vezes por mês ou mais. Na média da OCDE, foram 20%.
O número coloca o Brasil abaixo da média da organização, mas ainda representa uma parcela expressiva dos adolescentes avaliados.
Cyberbullying atinge 3% dos estudantes
A violência no ambiente digital apareceu com menor frequência. No Brasil, 3% dos alunos disseram que informações que os incomodavam ou prejudicavam foram publicadas sobre eles na internet, sem consentimento, pelo menos algumas vezes por mês nos 12 meses anteriores à aplicação do Pisa.
A proporção é exatamente a mesma registrada na média da OCDE.
Os principais números do levantamento são:
- 17% dos estudantes brasileiros relataram sofrer alguma forma de bullying algumas vezes por mês ou mais;
- 20% é a média registrada pela OCDE;
- 3% dos brasileiros disseram ter tido informações prejudiciais ou incômodas publicadas na internet sem consentimento;
- 3% também foi o índice de cyberbullying na média da OCDE.
Tecnologia muda a rotina dentro das escolas
O Pisa também investigou o uso de dispositivos digitais durante o período escolar. No Brasil, os estudantes passam, em média, 1,3 hora por dia usando esses equipamentos para atividades de aprendizagem. A média da OCDE é de 1,7 hora.
Quando o uso não está relacionado ao aprendizado, o tempo chega a uma hora diária entre os brasileiros.
Os aparelhos também aparecem associados à distração durante as aulas. No Brasil, 25% dos estudantes afirmaram que seus colegas frequentemente se distraem com dispositivos digitais durante a maioria ou todas as aulas de ciências. Na OCDE, o índice foi de 28%.
Entre os países da organização, os alunos que relatam esse tipo de distração obtêm, em média, 11 pontos a menos em ciências. No Brasil, a diferença chega a 19 pontos.
Proibição de celulares avança
A restrição ao uso de celulares aumentou bastante entre 2022 e 2025. No ano passado, 81% dos estudantes brasileiros frequentavam escolas onde os aparelhos não eram permitidos nas dependências. Em 2022, eram 37%.
Na média da OCDE, a proporção passou de 34% para 49%.
Leia mais:
- A urgência de formar jovens fluentes em inglês na era dos agentes de IA
- IA não poderá mais corrigir provas e redações nas escolas; veja o que muda
- IA vai substituir professores? “Problema é quando substitui o pensamento”, diz pesquisador
O levantamento encontrou ainda uma associação entre a proibição e a distração: estudantes de escolas que não permitem celulares têm probabilidade cerca de 13% menor de relatar distrações causadas por dispositivos digitais, considerando a média dos países da organização.
O Pisa 2025 também apontou desempenho abaixo da média da OCDE entre os estudantes brasileiros em ciências, matemática e leitura. Os resultados colocam bullying, cyberbullying e o uso da tecnologia entre os diferentes aspectos do ambiente escolar analisados pela avaliação.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: La nueva función de WhatsApp te permitirá chatear y controlar agentes de IA dentro de la app
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara una nueva función que te permitirá chatear con varios agentes de IA. La compañía lanzó una actualización con chats dedicados para agentes de terceros para hablar con ellos en una conversación por separado. Si bien el cliente de mensajería ya cuenta con una IA que puede ejecutar múltiples acciones, todavía no es posible integrar otros modelos que no pertenezcan a Meta a la plataforma.
La nueva función, reportada por WABetaInfo, aparece en la actualización más reciente de la beta para Android. Una vez que la instalas, aparecerá una opción dentro de los ajustes de la app que te permite conectar a un agente externo y hablar con él. La configuración es relativamente sencilla y solo requiere conectarla a través de una API con el servicio en donde vive tu IA.
En términos de funcionamiento, WhatsApp permite vincular hasta cinco agentes distintos por cuenta, cada uno con nombre y foto de perfil asignados que lucirán como cualquier otro contacto en tu lista de chats. Los usuarios pueden hacer preguntas en la ventana de conversación o darle instrucciones para que lleve a cabo tareas en tu nombre. Si alguna vez usaste OpenClaw, entonces sabrás lo que puedes hacer cuando tienes a varios agentes bajo tu mando.
Antes de emocionarse y pensar en crear un grupo con todos ellos, hay algunos detalles a considerar. El primero y más importante es que la función solo es compatible con chats individuales, así que olvídate de añadirlo a tu grupo de amigos o a alguna comunidad. El agente solo puede leer lo que le compartes en la ventana de conversación, por lo que no tendrá acceso a tus contactos ni tus archivos multimedia.
WhatsApp te permitirá configurar hasta cinco agentes por cuenta
Sobre esta línea, si usas un agente deberás ser consciente de que las conversaciones no están cifradas de extremo a extremo. A diferencia de los chats habituales, WhatsApp no puede blindar lo que le dices al agente para que nadie lo lea durante el proceso. Esto se debe a que los chats con los agentes pasan por un servicio de Meta que actúa en representación del desarrollador externo, el cual puede acceder a esos mensajes como parte del funcionamiento del servicio.
WhatsApp ofrece una gestión básica sobre los agentes una vez que ya los creaste. Si quieres cambiar el nombre o la foto de perfil, solo tienes que acceder a la configuración para ajustar los valores. También es posible eliminarlo, aunque esta acción es irreversible y ya no podrás conversar con él. La buena noticia es que el historial y la ventana de chat se almacenan en el historial para que accedas a ellos cuando quieras.
Los agentes de terceros están disponible en la versión 2.26.35.3 de la beta de WhatsApp para Android. El reporte menciona que el despliegue es gradual, por lo que no todos los usuarios que participan en el programa podrán acceder a él. Por el momento no hay detalles sobre un despliegue más amplio, aunque tratándose de IA, es probable que ocurra pronto.

articles.title: RPCS3 emulator can now run PS3 games on PC directly from a disc drive in landmark development — unlocks 20 years of physical titles on Windows, Linux, and macOS
articles.text:
RPCS3 emulator can now run PS3 games on PC directly from a disc drive in landmark development — unlocks 20 years of physical titles on Windows, Linux, and macOS
Test-run games without dumping them to your precious SSD. Less friction more fun.
The developers of the Sony PlayStation 3 emulator RPCS3 have told their social media followers that it is now possible to play games straight from discs. As announced on Twitter/X, the emulator’s latest refinement works only with certain internal and external Blu-ray drives. Happily for retro gamers, there’s a lengthy compatibility list of drives featuring many models and brands, and the same drives are also compatible with dumping your media to fixed storage.
Above you can see the RPCS3 devs are pretty happy with the slick new “plug and play” refinements that are available to users of the latest version of the emulator. “You can now play your PS3 games on PC... DIRECTLY FROM THE DISC DRIVE!” boast the open source emulator programmers. “PLUG AND PLAY! Owning your games as physical media allows you to play games released as far back as 20 years ago without relying on any servers!” The RPCS3 team thanks digant73 and Megamouse, specifically, for contributions making this feat possible.
Indeed, this is another step forward in making a slick emulator that works in a surprisingly frictionless fashion. Though the Tweet mentions PC, specifically, extended disc drive play support is also available on Linux, FreeBSD, and macOS. You just need to check that drive compatibility list. Moreover, all users can enjoy “optimized install times for package installations from the disc drive.” It has also been confirmed that PS4 and PS5 console users with Linux installs can launch PS3 games directly from disc using RPCS3.
Here’s a quick tip for folks who have an obscure Blu-ray drive that isn’t in the list. If you want to confirm compatibility with the drive, just put a PS3 disc in it. If you can browse its files, it's compatible; if nothing shows up, then it's not.
With pricing for the best SSDs now sky-high, being able to test-run new (old) games before dumping them to fixed storage could be a boon. It might also be good for auditioning a batch of discs you have recently bought, to see which ones are keepers.

articles.title: Sony updates its generation-defining headphones for the user-replaceable battery era: meet the WH-1000XM4C
articles.text:
Sony updates its generation-defining headphones for the replaceable-battery era: meet the WH-1000XM4C — same, but different
Also just launched: WH-CH730N entry-level cans and Sony WH-C530N on-ears
- Sony has updated an icon with the new 'mid-range' WH-1000XM4C
- Also unveiled: entry-level WH-CH730N over-ears, to update the WH-CH720N
- …and WH-CH530N on-ears, to supersede the WH-CH530N
Sony asked me, during this particular product briefing, if I too had a habit of counting how many of a specific brand or model of headphones I saw while on public transport? Big yes. Can't stop myself.
And I had to concede that the Sony WH-1000XM4 are a pair I still see most often on London's rail network, despite their 2020 launch date (closely followed by the mid-range Bose QuietComfort, and then the entry-level Sony WH-CH520N).
And it's clear that Sony's team has clocked this too. Apparently, just over 10 million pairs of the XM4 have been sold so far, and fans still hanker after them no matter how highly the next two generations of cans also scored. And given that it's now 10 years since the original 1000X launched in 2016, it was high time Sony did something to mark the occasion.
So, this news will mark a big day for all of us — particularly for my colleague still clinging to their 2018 XM3s, despite one ear cup being held together with sticky tape.
Music-lovers, the WH-1000XM4C are here! And you can buy them in your choice of black, a slightly lighter-gray-than-we're-used-to 'Platinum Silver', and an all-new 'Lavender' finish.
Are the XM4C Sony's new flagship cans? No, those are still the Sony 1000X The Collexion, followed by the very-much-still-current Sony WH-1000XM6. Sony tells me we're to think of the WH-1000XM4C as a new mid-range option, slotting in above the also-new WH-CH730 and WH-CH530 (which I'll come to soon).
Let's get granular: the design and ANC are unchanged from the XM4, so you still get 40mm drivers and the company's HD Noise Cancelling Processor QN1. They also still fold up nicely for easier transportation — although you'll want them around your neck or over your ears most of the time.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
But Sony has upgraded the sound-tuning slightly, following a lot of research "to match current music trends". What does that mean? Sony tells me its aim was "richer, clearer vocals" and "tighter bass definition", all of which sounds very promising, given the well-documented sonic talents of the XM4.
Also added is a 10-band EQ tab to tweak the sound yourself and Quick Access, which allows you to launch Apple Music or Spotify on-ear, rather than digging out your phone. It's not new to Sony headphones (it made its debut in 2022 and, in terms of over-ears, within the XM5) but it is new to the XM4, because those launched in 2020.
Sony is quite open about why it had to go back to the drawing board here: when the XM3 launched in 2018 (the design also adopted by the 2020 XM4) any stance on user-replaceable batteries in headphones was just a glint in the eye of European lawmakers. Now that headphones have to comply with such legislation, Sony had to have a rethink. And the XM4C are now compliant, so users will be able to replace the batteries, although at the time of writing Sony hasn't yet disclosed the cost of said juice packs.
What I do know is that providing the update has caused a minor drop in stamina from the XM4 to XM4C, from 30 hours to 27 hours with ANC on. It seems a small price to pay for headphones that will hopefully last (and last and last), but may come as a disappointment when some cans are stretching up to 90 hours in 2026…
Speaking of prices to pay, the WH-1000XM4C's price is set at $299.99 / £219 / €250 / AU$449.95.
Sony's trio of 2026 headphone goodies includes entry-level options too
Something for our best noise-cancelling headphones buying guide that will cost double figures, not triple? Sony gets it — although only one product in this trio of releases dips to that price point, and it's not the next one.
Also unveiled today is the Sony WH-CH730N (pictured above), to update the highly popular cheap and cheerful Sony WH-CH720N. Interestingly, here we do have a stamina increase, from up to 50 hours to up to 75 hours without ANC. Also onboard is the 10-band EQ, but here Sony says you're also getting better ANC and AI-enhanced call tech.
The new design is foldable and features slightly bigger ear cups that sit slightly more flush against your ears, and there's a new Beige colorway. You get Sony's basic DSEE upscaler engine, 360 Reality Audio support, dual noise-sensor tech for noise cancellation, optional max-volume control in the app, Bluetooth 6.0, LE Audio support and they're Auracast ready.
Pricing? Of course: Sony WH-CH730N can be yours for $179.99 / £100 / €120 / AU$229.95 in your choice of Black, White, Pink, Beige and Blue, from September 2026.
Last but by no means least are the new Sony WH-CH530N, updating the Sony WH-CH520N on-ears, which we rated an excellent 4.5-stars shortly after their release in 2023.
Here, battery life is up to 55 hours (from 50 in the older set) with ANC on, or 75 hours with ANC off. You also get the AI call tech for clearer calls, multipoint pairing, LE Audio support, and optional maximum volume control, i.e., adjustable 5-step volume level for hearing protection.
And the pricing is low, at just $69.99 / £50 / €60 / AU$99.95 in your choice of Cobalt Blue, Coral, Mint, Pink, White or Black.
We can't vouch for the sound-per-pound value just yet. But we're working on it — watch this space.

Before this, she spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing and reviewing everything from wallet-friendly wireless earbuds to huge high-end sound systems. Prior to gaining her MA in Journalism in 2018, Becky freelanced as an arts critic alongside a 22-year career as a professional dancer and aerialist – any love of dance starts with a love of music. articles.title: Nvidia Acquires HuggingFace for $12.9B - EE Times
articles.text:
Nvidia has acquired HuggingFace for $12.9 billion. The startup, which is named after an emoji, was founded by three French entrepreneurs in 2016. It has become the go-to repository for open-source AI models, datasets, and associated software libraries.
In a press conference announcing the deal, Nvidia VP of AI software Justin Boitano was faced with many questions about the neutrality of HuggingFace’s offering.
“We’re committed to helping build this community, stewarding, and fostering this community, Boitano said. “We want to continue to work with all AI developers globally to make sure that they’ve got an open and neutral platform that interoperates with every cloud provider, every hardware company in the world.”
Nvidia believes in maintaining a healthy ecosystem of closed model providers and open models, he added, noting that open models give companies the ability to build their own domain-specific intelligence. Nvidia is by far HuggingFace’s biggest contributor.
Boitano said that it’s in Nvidia’s interests to keep HuggingFace hardware-neutral.
“The Hugging Face team has built an amazing community, […] and the only way you do that is by building the trust of the developer community and giving developers access to run the models and access the datasets from any platform in the world that they want to run it on,” he said. “We are incentivized and motivated to keep this open and neutral and ensure that developers can work wherever they want to work, accessing and connecting the best open models into and across every cloud provider, every neocloud, and into every data center and make availability on every device.”
Nvidia-specific runtimes will continue to exist alongside open-source runtimes such as vLLM and SGLang, which are open and neutral, ensuring all open models in the HuggingFace repository can be optimized for all hardware, Boitano said.
HuggingFace co-founder and CEO Clem Delangue said that the acquisition would still mean all the players in today’s ecosystem can use open-source foundations to build whatever they want.
“The vast majority of what we do is open source—open models, open datasets that are by definition neutral—everyone can take them, everyone can optimize them, everyone can fork our open source if they’re not happy about it,” he said. “Almost by definition, everything that we do is open and neutral and gives everyone the capabilities to build more.”
Delangue, who is French, shot down a suggestion that the acquisition of HuggingFace was emblematic of the difficulties of building tech giants in the EU.
“All three co-founders are French, but I was already in the U.S. when we started the company, so quite naturally, we built it with American investors,” he said. “I think it’s going to create really positive effects on the European tech ecosystem because obviously the founders are French, a big part of the team is French, and so we hope that after this acquisition, they’ll be able to reinvest quite a lot in the European tech ecosystem.”
HuggingFace will continue to support open models and open datasets from around the globe, and Delangue said he hopes to include more open models out of European labs such as Mistral in France and Black Forest Labs in Germany.
Delangue said that the HuggingFace team is excited to now have the ability to “think long-term.” Nvidia’s support will enable HuggingFace to reach its goal of 100 million builders on the platform much more quickly, he said, noting that the platform has around 18 million users today.
“We think we’re at the inflection point for HuggingFace and for open-source AI in general,” he said. “We think with the resources, with the support, with the long-term approach of Nvidia, we’ll be able to do basically what we’ve been doing for the past 10 years, meaning, supporting the open-source AI community, but to the next level at a much bigger scale, which we think is really needed for the field and for the world.”

What It Takes to Build an AI Chip Startup in Europe

We dive into the realities of launching and scaling a European semiconductor startup, covering key challenges like raising capital, overcoming risk aversion, and competing for top engineering talent.

Nvidia’s Groq deal raised more questions than answers. EE Times examines what happened, what it means, and why the details matter.
