articles.title: Japan is launching a mission to bring back the first samples from a Martian moon
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: Japan plans to send a spacecraft to Phobos in 2026 to collect material from the small Martian moon and return it to Earth. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's mission is scheduled to launch from Tanegashima Space Center on October 20. If the mission succeeds, the spacecraft will bring back at least 10 grams of material from Phobos, making it the first mission to return samples from a moon orbiting Mars.
The "Martian Moons eXploration" mission, or MMX, is expected to take about a year to reach Mars. It will then spend three years operating around the planet and its moons before beginning a roughly one-year trip back to Earth. The sample return is expected in 2031.
Landing on Phobos will be one of the mission's biggest challenges. The moon is small, with a radius of about 11 kilometers, but its gravity is still much stronger than that of asteroid Ryugu, where JAXA previously landed a spacecraft. At the same time, Phobos has far less gravity than Earth's moon.
That leaves MMX operating in a difficult middle ground. The spacecraft cannot use a long hover-and-touchdown approach like the one used at Ryugu because it would burn too much fuel. But it also cannot rely on landing techniques designed for the Moon.
Instead, the probe will make key decisions on its own. Communications between Earth and the spacecraft could be delayed by as much as 20 minutes, making real-time control impossible during descent and landing.
As it approaches Phobos, MMX will compare the surface below it with existing crater and terrain maps. The spacecraft will use that information to adjust its position and guide itself toward the landing area. Below 300 meters, it will also look for unexpected elevation changes that could make a site unsafe. If it detects a problem, MMX can shift to another location, abandon the attempt, and climb away.
Mitsubishi Electric designed the main spacecraft. It will launch with a mass of 4,480 kilograms (9,877 pounds), with more than half of that weight made up of fuel. The spacecraft carries separate fuel reserves for its trip to Mars, its operations near the planet, and its return to Earth.
After reaching the Mars system, MMX will discard its outbound module after using its propellant. It will later fly by Deimos, Mars' other moon, before jettisoning the exploration module.
A small rover called IDEFIX will be deployed before MMX makes its main landing attempt. The French and German space agencies developed the rover, which is expected to explore Phobos for about 100 days. Its work is intended to help assess surface conditions before the larger spacecraft begins sampling.
MMX will use a robotic arm to drill into the surface and collect material in cylindrical tubes. It also carries a nitrogen-gas sampling device originally developed by NASA. That system is intended to collect fine dust from the surface.
The samples could help scientists determine how Phobos and Deimos formed. One theory is that the moons formed from debris ejected after a major collision with Mars. Another is that they were asteroids from the outer solar system that Mars captured.
The moons have dark surfaces that resemble water- and carbon-rich asteroids. But their nearly circular orbits, which follow Mars' equatorial plane and move in the same direction as the planet's rotation, are more consistent with the impact-debris theory.
Scientists also expect Phobos to hold traces of Mars. Impacts have blasted Martian material into space over time, and some of that debris is believed to have settled on the moons. Researchers estimate that about 0.1% of the material collected by MMX could have originated on the Red Planet.
The mission is expected to cost about $345 million and will be Japan's first Mars probe launch in 28 years. In addition to the scientific goal, MMX will test autonomous navigation, landing, and sample-return systems that could support later Mars missions.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: TornadoVM 6, JReleaser, LangChain4j, Java Operator SDK, JHipster, Yupiik Fusion
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for August 31st, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA release of TornadoVM 6.0; point releases of JReleaser, LangChain4j, Java Operator SDK, JHipster, Kotlin Toolchain and Yupiik Fusion; and maintenance releases of Micronaut and GraalVM Development Kit.
JDK 27
Build 35 remains the current build in the JDK 27 early-access builds. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JDK 28
Build 14 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was also made available this past week featuring updates from Build 13 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28 and JDK 27, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
TornadoVM
The release of TornadoVM 6.0.0 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a full replacement of the Java Native Interface with the more modern Foreign Function & Memory API used in the backends and library tasks; the removal of the experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) in favor of "sourcing all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer, and makes that the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26, 27);" and an expansion of the CUDA Backend. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes. InfoQ will follow up with a more detailed news story.
Micronaut
The Micronaut Foundation has released version 5.1.3 of the Micronaut Framework, based on Micronaut Core 5.1.13, featuring patch updates to modules: Micronaut SQL Libraries; Micronaut Micrometer; Micronaut OpenAPI/Swagger; Micronaut OpenSearch; Micronaut Email; Micronaut Reactor; Micronaut Data; and Micronaut AWS. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
GraalVM Development Kit
Oracle Labs has released version 5.1.3 of the Graal Development Kit (GDK) featuring alignment with the aforementioned Micronaut 5.1.3. This new release features the ability to generate and build GDK apps with JDK 25 when creating apps using the GDK Launcher and GDK CLI. Formerly known as Graal Cloud Native, the Graal Development Kit for Micronaut provides a curated set of Micronaut framework modules that simplify cloud application development. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JReleaser
The release of JReleaser 1.26.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: improved support of Snapcraft with the addition of the platforms node in the generated snapcraft.yml file and a deprecation of the runOn() method, defined in the SnapPackager class, in favor of the buildFor() method; and a new option to skip tagging the JBang packager repository to resolve the potential for incorrect JBang tags. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirtieth beta release) of LangChain4j 1.20.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: experimental support for non-blocking and reactive, for AI service methods that call a thread for an entire interaction, that now return a CompletableFuture<T> and Flow.Publisher<T>; and opt-in support for JSON SPIs against Jackson 3. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Java Operator SDK
The release of Java Operator SDK 5.6.0 delivers notable changes such as: a new InformerPool interface where informers are now shared between controllers and event sources instead of one informer per event source; and a change in configuration of the EventRecorder interface from the RegisteredController interface to the eventRecorder() method defined in the ConfigurationService interface. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JHipster
The release of JHipster 9.3.0 ships with bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: full support for Spring Boot 4, Jackson 3 and Angular 22; reactive applications that are now built with Vite; and consistent use of the Spring Boot @ServiceConnection annotation on integration tests using Testcontainers. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Kotlin Toolchain
The JetBrains team has released version 0.12.0 of Kotlin Toolchain, a unified entry point utility into the Kotlin programming language. Along with bug fixes and dependency upgrades, new features include: expansion of published Kotlin libraries, originally limited to JVM libraries, that now include multiplatform libraries; the ability to execute Wasm apps using the kotlin run command; and improvements to the Terminal UI and IDE. More details on this release, including breaking changes, may be found in the release notes.
Yupiik Fusion
Version 1.1.0 of Yupiik Fusion, the lightweight Java stack for building microservices and APIs, provides bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a new JsonSchemaService class that implements the Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema specification; a new CurlLoggerListener class designed to force all exchanges to be logged; and the addition of a snapshot deployment workflow. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.

articles.title: DRAM Industry Revenue Rises 59.5% QoQ in 2Q26 as Supply Expansion Continues to Lag Demand Growth
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
	
	
	
DRAM Industry Revenue Rises 59.5% QoQ in 2Q26 as Supply Expansion Continues to Lag Demand Growth
TrendForce's latest findings on the memory industry reveal that sharp rises in traditional DRAM contract prices have led to a 59.5% QoQ increase in total DRAM industry revenue, reaching nearly US$154.73 billion in 2Q26.
Growing demand for AI servers, fueled by expanding LLM training and AI inference, has driven higher shipments of HBM3e, LPDDR5X, and high-capacity RDIMMS. The surge in agentic AI applications is further boosting RDIMM demand across various capacities.On the supply side, suppliers' inventories remain at historic lows, with additional supply mainly allocated for server use. Consequently, DRAM bit shipments grew only modestly in the second quarter.
Looking ahead, modest growth in bit shipments is expected to be one of the key factors affecting third-quarter revenue. Conventional DRAM contract price growth, however, is projected to moderate to 13-18% QoQ. This reflects a shift in some demand from high-capacity RDIMMs toward lower-capacity products, as well as the limited ability of PC and smartphone customers to absorb further price increases. Consumer DRAM is expected to post the strongest price growth, as suppliers have significantly curtailed supply.
TrendForce notes that Samsung posted the strongest QoQ bit shipment growth among the three major suppliers in 2Q26, supported by its early move into HBM4 mass production and shipments. Combined with a substantial increase in ASP, this lifted Samsung's quarterly revenue to $60.98 billion, up 63.4% QoQ. The company ranked first with a market share of 39.4%.
SK hynix ranked second. Since HBM accounted for the highest proportion of its total bit shipments among the top three suppliers, growth in ASP was relatively limited. Its 2Q26 revenue increased 37.9% QoQ to $38.59 billion, while market share edged down to 24.9%.
Micron continued to prioritize higher-priced server DRAM in its product mix amid capacity constraints. Revenue rose 65.5% QoQ to $36.0 billion in 2Q26, lifting its market share slightly to 23.3%. TrendForce notes that from 2026 to 2027, the three major suppliers will primarily increase bit supply by accelerating migrations to advanced processes.
Meanwhile, wafer starts are expected to see only modest increases through production process optimization, cleanroom acquisitions, and the reallocation of cleanroom space from other product lines.
By comparison, suppliers such as Nanya, Winbond, and PSMC remain focused on mature-process products, with their 2Q26 growth continuing to benefit from demand that the three major suppliers can no longer fully serve as they migrate to more advanced processes. Significant increases in DDR4 and DDR3 contract prices drove Nanya's revenue up 68.3% QoQ to $2.612 billion. Winbond's revenue increased 75.8% QoQ to $998 million.
PSMC's reported DRAM revenue, primarily derived from consumer DRAM products, surged 167.8% QoQ to $115 million in 2Q26. Including foundry revenue, its total revenue increased 54% QoQ. Looking ahead, the company is expected to begin its next phase of supply expansion after obtaining a process technology license from Micron.

Think of it this way. The US practically uses no oil from the middle east, but the conflict over there is still indirectly impacting prices in the US. The market is far more connected than you probably think it is.

articles.title: Lua hoje: confira a fase da Lua desta terça-feira 08/09/2026
articles.text:
Hoje, 8 de setembro de 2026, a Lua está na fase minguante e 10% visível. Confira o calendário completo de fases da Lua deste mês, de acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).
Confira as próximas fases
As fases da Lua no mês de setembro de 2026 começaram no dia 4 com a chegada da Lua Minguante, às 04h52 (horário de Brasília). Depois disso, dia 11, é a vez da Lua Nova, que chega à 0h27. A Lua Crescente surge às 17h44 do dia 18. Por fim, vem a Lua Cheia, dia 26, à 13h50.
Leia mais:
- Entenda o que é a Lua, como e quando ela se formou
- Saiba como tirar a melhor foto possível com uma câmera de celular
- 7 dicas para fotografar a lua com seu celular
Calendário das fases da lua em setembro de 2026
- Lua Minguante: dia 4, às 04h52
- Lua Nova: dia 11, às 0h27
- Lua Crescente: dia 18, às 17h44
- Lua Cheia: dia 26, às 13h50
O que é o ciclo lunar?
Uma lunação ou ciclo lunar, como é chamado o intervalo de tempo entre luas novas, é sutilmente variável, com média de duração de 29,5 dias. Durante esse período, ela passa pelas quatro fases principais (nova, crescente, cheia e minguante), e cada uma se prolonga por aproximadamente sete dias.
Também existem as “interfases”: quarto crescente e crescente gibosa (entre as fases nova e cheia) e minguante gibosa e quarto minguante (entre a cheia e a minguante).
Entenda cada fase da Lua
Lua Nova
Na Lua Nova, o satélite se posiciona entre a Terra e o Sol. Isso faz com que o lado iluminado da Lua fique voltado para o Sol, enquanto o lado escuro fica voltado para nós. Por esse motivo, a Lua não é visível no céu noturno. Essa fase marca o início de um novo ciclo lunar e está relacionada ao recomeço e a novas possibilidades.
Lua Crescente
Depois da Lua Nova, surge a fase Crescente. Aos poucos, uma pequena faixa iluminada começa a aparecer no céu, aumentando noite após noite. No início, vemos apenas um fino arco de luz, mas com o passar dos dias a parte iluminada cresce até que metade da Lua esteja visível, momento chamado de Quarto Crescente. Essa fase simboliza crescimento, desenvolvimento e a construção de novos caminhos.
Lua Cheia
Na Lua Cheia, a Terra se encontra entre o Sol e a Lua. Isso permite que o lado lunar voltado para nós receba luz por completo, tornando-se totalmente visível e brilhante no céu. É o período de maior intensidade luminosa, quando a Lua nasce no horizonte exatamente no momento em que o Sol se põe. A Lua Cheia é associada à plenitude, ao auge de processos e à energia em seu ponto máximo.
Lua Minguante
Após a Lua Cheia, a luz da Lua começa a diminuir gradualmente. A cada noite, vemos menos da sua superfície iluminada. Quando apenas metade dela está visível, ocorre o Quarto Minguante, fase oposta ao Quarto Crescente. A Lua continua a perder luminosidade até chegar novamente à Lua Nova, reiniciando o ciclo. A fase Minguante simboliza reflexão, encerramento e preparação para novos começos.
Qual a fase da Lua hoje?
Hoje a Lua está na fase Minguante.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: Si quieres un buen iPhone, no merece la pena esperar: el iPhone 17 Pro está más barato que nunca en Amazon
articles.text:
Sí, estamos a solo dos días de que salga el iPhone 18 Pro, pero si lo que tú quieres es un buen iPhone, te gusta el diseño de la última generación y prefieres ahorrar algo de dinero, Apple acaba de ponerte sobre la mesa una de las mejores ofertas del año. El iPhone 17 Pro está al precio más bajo de la historia en Amazon. Y, si bien es un escenario que se suele dar cuando el nuevo modelo está a la vuelta de la esquina, este año tiene aún más sentido sacrificar esas mejoras que se esperan e ir a por un dispositivo un poco más barato.
¿Por qué? Bueno, es bien sabido que el diseño del iPhone 17 Pro se mantendrá en el nuevo modelo. En este sentido, las únicas novedades vendrán por el lado del color: se espera que Apple lance el iPhone 18 Pro en burdeos, azul cielo y un tercero que podría ser el clásico plateado o el negro.
Sí estarán presentes otro tipo de novedades, pero no se espera que estas sean tan avanzadas como para diferenciar tanto ambas generaciones. En otras palabras: puedes ahorrar algo de dinero si optas por el iPhone 17 Pro sin tener esa sensación de haber tenido algo mucho mejor por un poco más.
iPhone 17 Pro de 256 GB - Completamente nuevo y con garantía de 3 años.
*Los precios pueden haber cambiado desde la publicación
Este año tiene aún más sentido. Puede que 140 euros de ahorro no parezcan demasiado, y otros años la recomendación puede haber sido diferente, pero con el iPhone 18 Pro la cosa cambia. Está casi confirmado que Apple subirá el precio de los dos móviles, por lo que si quieres lo último de lo último, tendrás que pagar la diferencia de la oferta y, además, el aumento que considere la compañía.
Todas las filtraciones auguran que el iPhone 18 Pro subirá entre 150 y 250 euros, por lo que el ahorro podría ser significativo por renunciar a un par de mejoras en la cámara, un chip un poco más potente y la opción de elegir los nuevos colores.
En estos momentos puedes comprar el iPhone 17 Pro en Amazon por 1.179 euros en los tres colores disponibles y con 256 GB de almacenamiento. ¿Es la oferta del año? 140 euros de ahorro no es la panacea, pero nunca antes había estado tan barato en Amazon.
¿Merece la pena esperar al nuevo iPhone?
Por supuesto, todo depende del tipo de usuario que seas. Tener el último modelo siempre es una ventaja para probar las últimas novedades, pero sabiendo que Apple lanzará una generación bastante continuista, optar por el iPhone 17 Pro es una muy buena opción.
Seguirá siendo totalmente compatible con iOS 27, Siri AI, todas las opciones de Apple Intelligence, se actualizará durante años y su cámara debería tener poco que envidiar a la del iPhone 18 Pro. En cambio, esos 300-350 euros de ahorro y el hecho de poder tenerlo mañana mismo en la mano pueden ser más que suficientes para dar el paso, renunciar a las novedades y tener un iPhone que sigue siendo uno de los mejores móviles del momento.
Si no crees que puedas sacarle todo el partido a la cámara del móvil y los nuevos colores no te convencen demasiado, nuestra recomendación, si necesitas un iPhone ahora mismo, es que optes por el iPhone 17 Pro: te ahorrarás dinero, lo tendrás mañana en tu casa y difícilmente sentirás que estás haciendo una mala compra incluso cuando Apple anuncie el nuevo modelo en un par de días.

articles.title: Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
articles.text:
Thanks to their ability to provide a smooth ride and quiet powertrain with ease, electric vehicles are a true shoo-in for the high-end luxury automotive segment. Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac’s Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne.
Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
The British automaker is on the hunt for a new demographic with its first electric vehicle.
I recently got a quick ride in a heavily camouflaged preproduction Torcal as a way to experience it before its official debut toward the end of this month. Between this brute’s spacious interior, supple ride quality, and focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, all signs point to it not just being a viable competitor in the segment, but also characteristically Bentley.
When I say heavily camouflaged, this not only covers (pun intended) the Torcal’s exterior, but the interior as well. Thick black cloth was draped over most of it, to the point of the engineers punching holes in the cloth for proper seatbelt usage. The exterior was rather deceiving, too; apparently they affixed false body paneling under the wrap so as not to fully spoil its overall shape and profile. Upon first glance, it seemed like Bentley took a page from Lucid’s Gravity by making it wider at the front than at the back—in the name of teardrop-resembling aerodynamics—but Martin Page, the Torcal’s product line director-slash-chauffeur for my ride, assured me that what I was seeing (or rather, trying to see) wouldn’t be production.
However, this enabled me to zero in closer on what I could feel and hear. Whether up front or in back, the Torcal is amply spacious, even though it’s noticeably smaller in size and shape than Bentley’s current Bentayga. Page explained the great lengths that engineers reached to ensure it had an isolating and tremendously smooth ride. Running off-the-shelf two-chamber air suspension — common in the rest of the brand’s lineup — would seemingly suffice with an EV’s inherently good chassis balance, but engineers took it a step further by carefully altering the flow of oil through its adaptive dampers. This means that the jump in ride and handling between Comfort and Sport modes is much more discernible. No matter the mode, it rode incredibly smoothly. Heavy focus was paid to the Torcal’s alignment, too, with steering that returns to and maintains center as confidently as possible.
Diving deeper into signature Bentley characteristics, developing the best simulated engine note was high on the list of priorities. Inspiration came from the brand’s V8-powered Turbo R of the 1980s, except the track itself was recorded by a musician’s drum beat and mixed accordingly, rather than simply churned out from a synthesizer.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects,” Page shared.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects.”
— Martin Page, Torcal’s product line director
The reasoning behind this lies in hearing subtle imperfections, much like one would from an analogue internal combustion powertrain. Going one step further, the Torcal’s throttle tuning seemed to mimic a torquey V8 with progressive power delivery. In light of this, Page added that with this sound turned on, it gives occupants auditory cues to tie to the vehicle’s torque delivery, which is known to help reduce motion sickness. The sound has not yet been finalized and is still being finely tweaked at the time of this writing.
I got a peek at the digital instrument cluster and center infotainment screen — Page had to observe the speed limit, after all. The image these display in the background is of a fine crystal decanter hand-cut by Cumbria Crystal with light shone through it. In Page’s words, this shows the natural refractions and reflections that you get from every one of the cuts. It’s another indication of the brand’s focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, albeit a subtle one.
It’s also worth pointing out that Bentley takes net environmental impact seriously. “In this car we take sustainability to another level, we have clear targets for circular material and green aluminum,” Page shared. “The door cards are made with a natural fiber — not injection-molded plastic — that’s fully recyclable and fully sustainable.”
Then, Bentley is working with fellow UK company Fox Brothers to offer a Merino wool interior option, not just as a lesser-taken route for comfort (Volvo’s done well with wool, too) but also as a sturdy, renewable material that will hold up to automotive use. Finally, the assembly plant in Crewe, England, has tough requirements for green energy use (namely solar) and other renewable practices.
Output, battery, and charging specs are not carved into stone just yet. Power will be north of 800 hp and 700 lb ft of torque, and curb weight is estimated to be nearly 6,000 lbs. Page was quiet about battery size (though, expect it to mirror the Porsche’s 108 net kWh unit), and the targeted range is over 370 miles. With a peak charging rate of 400 kW, the brand is aiming for a 10–80 percent top-up in under 20 minutes, with 100 miles tacking on in as little as seven.
“We’re trying to be authentic in the whole experience,” Page summed up as we headed back to the parking lot where I met him.
The approach with the Torcal is to make a great Bentley first, and in the process of doing so, a great EV. It combines some already hashed-out tech from Volkswagen, but the brand is hoping its focus on craftsmanship and fine-tuning will attract discerning, well-heeled potential customers who want an electric luxury vehicle. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet, but it will be interesting to see how the Torcal is received after its full official unveiling.
Images by Bentley

articles.title: Holistic Digital Twins are Needed to Accelerate SDV Development - EE Times
articles.text:
In the automotive industry, there is broad agreement that future vehicle development methodologies will need to transform to meet the needs of “Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV)”. The move from “Hardware-defined” to “Software-defined” will require significant restructuring of processes that have been in place in some cases for decades. Development lead times need to be shorter, and innovation needs to be faster, which goes against the grain of increased software and systems complexity. That’s why OEMs, Tier 1’s, Tier 2s and IP providers are all investigating the potential of virtualization, or “digital twin,” to address the SDV challenge.
Complexity is slowing down the rollout of the SDV
Today’s SDV platforms are blighted by software and system-level complexity, which often leads to software schedule delays, threatening value-add feature sets, and even resulting in the cancellation of vehicle platform programs. A potential solution is what’s known as “shifting-left,” whereby software development and integration using virtual models is performed pre-silicon availability, but severe challenges remain in actually realizing a development flow that is fit-for-purpose.
The time and resources needed to develop and mature a complete vehicle electronics modeling platform is a significant barrier to the uptake of these new methodologies. There are many different types of models in different development environments to deal with, which have varying fidelities that require different timing domains. Synchronization of these domains presents real issues when trying to create an integrated and meaningful virtual simulation platform. Added to that, many current modeling techniques are also too slow for SW developers to use for coding and debugging. So, trying to reconcile what is developed in the virtual world with what will eventually end up on the physical vehicle platform is a chasm developers find challenging to cross.
What is an “integration storm”?
Complexity is not the only issue facing automakers. The integration effort required to create a valuable asset from the disparate elements available is for some OEMs and Tier 1s an insurmountable task. Today’s hardware and software development happens largely in silos, with disparate teams working in parallel, often with no true insight on the progress of their colleagues. It’s no wonder then that in electronics development the system integration phase is the riskiest part of any project. Many issues occur when bringing together the final hardware to create the final system, and they are often due to unforeseen system interdependencies. This can be referred to as an “integration storm”. Which at the later stages of development, has the potential to cause catastrophic delays. The likelihood of such issues is greatly increased when there is no common, continuous approach to design, test, and validation.
Virtualization is needed at the system level, but this brings its own challenges
It goes without saying that the idea of using digital twin to provide greater insight and analysis, pre-hardware availability, is a good one and has been used in some segments of the automotive industry for many years, and adoption is increasing. But the lack of joined-up-thinking at the systems level means that outcomes are currently limited; it’s just too fragmented to tackle the “integration storm”
As an EDA vendor working across the automotive electronics industry, Siemens has been well placed to identify the challenges associated with attempting systems-level virtualization. These are the main issues observed that affect the whole value chain from OEMs to Tier 1’s, Silicon and IP providers:
- There is a general lack of experience in virtual system-level modelling
- Suppliers lack a consolidated validation environment that gives a full system view (and come to realize that the time and expense involved in developing one internally is often prohibitive)
- Software and hardware teams are working independently of each other in isolation
- Software workloads should drive hardware selection, rather than the other way around; this results in hardware that is out-of-date before it even hits the market
- Modeling and simulation systems are not equipped to handle real-world stimulus and are not integrated with CI/CD/CC flows
- There is rarely a system-level test and validation strategy
The combination of all these issues boils down to a simple fact. Today it simply takes too long to build a meaningful digital twin; in many cases, it can take years, negating the benefits which are supposed to include the ability to shift development left and accelerate time-to-market.
Who needs to use system-level virtualization and verification and why does it benefit them?
An additional level of complexity is derived from the fact that there is a broad cross-section of engineers developing software across the automotive supply chain, all of whom are facing different challenges and have different end goals.
Let’s have a look at some of the major personas:
Systems architects: OEMs and Tier 1 architects need to determine the high-level structure of a vehicle’s complex electronic and electrical (E/E) systems and define how hardware and software components interact to achieve functional requirements. An SoC architect may need to integrate heterogeneous multi-core architectures, plus processors, graphics, AI engines, as well as various peripherals onto a single chip. Both groups need to adhere to strict safety and security standards.
- Virtualization goal: They need a single holistic environment where they can run software workloads across an entire system; it needs to be customizable and fast so that multiple configurations can be evaluated to cover the entire SDV development flow.
Software application developers: Again, this category can be segmented further: user space application developers use generic OS level environments to write software, then the final software is “ported” to the hardware-relevant BSP. Virtual models could be used for this but are often too slow. Low-level firmware application developers, on the other hand, do not rely on fast models; they need fidelity and accuracy so they can make significant use of today’s virtual models
- Virtualization goal: User space developers want to be able to develop earlier, so need pre-silicon availability. They need faster models, and want the model base to be as close to the final BSP as possible to reduce porting efforts. Their results could be much more effective if they were able to access code from colleagues in other design teams to take account of interdependencies. If models were available that were fast and accurate, they could be used by both user space and BSP developers:
Software validation and testing engineers, including CI/CD integration: This team ensures that the vehicle meets its performance and quality goals and all the relevant automotive standards. They design and execute tests and utilize simulation and testing tools to predict system behavior. In the SDV, this is becoming a full vehicle lifespan process, as fixes and upgrades are introduced via Over-The-Air (OTA) updates.
- Virtualization goal: Want to be able to start validating software at the systems level, pre-hardware, and be able to find where faults are occurring and feedback the issues to the systems architects so that the design can be iterated
HiL engineers (migrating to vHiL) are pushing to reduce the number of tests required in hardware, which are cost-prohibitive. They want to virtualize as much as possible at the system level to eliminate the vast majority of fails before testing in hardware.
- Virtualization goal: They need to build a full system platform to find errors early and to be able to spot those resulting from interdependencies. They also need greater insight into what is happening when the system fails.
Moving towards a holistic digital twin
Several of these virtualization goals could be considered cross-persona. What they all need is the ability to perform virtualization at the systems level and to have an environment available that enables them to share results and utilize the learning of the other personas.
What is needed is a clear route to an integrated, customizable, cloud-based, holistic Digital Twin that can deliver on the needs of multiple personas. This is the only way to truly enable the cross-silo engineering required for SDV.
Kick-start SDV development using a pre-integrated digital twin
As discussed, the cost and integration effort to build out full system simulation models, not to mention the fact that it can take years, has prevented widespread use of system-level digital twins by OEMs and Tier 1s.
That’s why Siemens EDA are taking a new approach by offering a pre-integrated system-level digital twin for the ADAS and IVI market. Of course, there can be no one-stop-shop solution for complex automotive systems, but having a common platform that can be used across an organization to kick-start development can greatly accelerate the adoption of virtualization. With such a digital twin, bring-up can happen in days, not months or years. Software development using the latest automotive IP such as the Zena-CSS from Arm can start immediately. The platform has the capability to offer scenario generation and to connect to real hardware so the design can be iterated using real-world hardware. When it’s necessary to create a more accurate simulation of end users’ systems, it can then be customized to reflect the final design.
By offering a common platform that can be used by multiple personas for cloud-based development, it is now possible for digital twin to be adopted at the systems level and to play a key role in accelerating SDV development in a scalable way.
Find out more about how to shift left with Siemens EDA’s digital twin solution: “PAVE360 puts a virtual car on every engineer’s desk”.
About the Author
Heather Campbell is the Marketing Director for PAVE360 at Siemens EDA, focusing on accelerating development with Digital Twin to automotive customers worldwide. Prior to joining Siemens in 2022, Heather worked for several leading electronics vendors including Infineon, Texas Instruments, and Freescale Semiconductor in a variety of Product Marketing and Management-focused roles. She holds an MEng in Electronics and Electrical Engineering from Strathclyde University.

                                                                Smart Outlier Detection                                                    
                        Just because a chip is deemed good doesn’t mean it will work as expected.
								September 8th, 2026 - 
								By: Ed Sperling
								
							
						
Nearly all leading-edge designs today are multi-die assemblies, which means that one defective die can render the entire device unusable. But not all dies that are deemed defective should be scrapped, and not all dies that pass inspection will behave as expected in the field, especially over time. Nir Sever, senior director of business development at proteanTecs, explains how to train machine learning models to identify outliers in context, replacing a rigid pass/fail decision tied to a spec with one that assesses its usefulness based on its behavior under real workloads in a complex system.

articles.title: Mistral lève 3 milliards d'euros pour imposer l'IA souveraine comme « nouvelle frontière technologique » - Numerama
articles.text:
C’est la plus grosse levée de fonds jamais réalisée par une tech européenne.
Trois ans après son lancement, Mistral AI annonce, ce 8 septembre 2026, avoir levé 3 milliards d’euros lors d’un tour de série D, valorisant l’entreprise à plus de 21 milliards d’euros.
Ce nouveau tour intervient alors que Mistral affirme désormais opérer dans une vingtaine de pays et accompagner plus de 125 grandes entreprises internationales dans leur transformation IA, parmi lesquelles Airbus, ASML ou HSBC.
Le tour a été mené par le géant sud-coréen Samsung Electronics, associé à deux co-chefs de file : le Scaleup Europe Fund, géré par EQT, et PSG Equity, déjà investisseur historique de Mistral.
Parmi les nouveaux entrants figurent Advent, des fonds gérés par BlackRock, ainsi que le Grand-Duché de Luxembourg. Une longue liste d’investisseurs existants a également remis au pot, dont a16z, ASML, BNP Paribas CIB, Bpifrance, Nvidia ou encore Salesforce Ventures.
Les objectifs de cette levée de fonds de Mistral
Selon la communiqué de l’entreprise française, l’argent investi servira à trois priorités :
- Muscler la recherche « frontier » qui sous-tend modèles, infrastructures et produits ;
- Augmenter la capacité de calcul dédiée à l’entraînement de modèles puissants ;
- Accélérer la croissance commerciale et l’implantation internationale du groupe.
Mistral revendique une position unique : être la seule entreprise d’IA à construire l’ensemble de la chaîne (modèles ouverts, infrastructure, capacité de calcul et produits) afin d’offrir à ses clients une alternative aux géants verticaux. L’objectif : éviter qu’ils ne dépendent d’un seul fournisseur pour leurs modèles, leur cloud et leur puissance de calcul, et restent ainsi maîtres de leur feuille de route, de leurs coûts et de leur approvisionnement.
Pour cela, l’entreprise articule sa promesse de souveraineté autour de quatre piliers : des données qui restent dans le périmètre du client, des modèles personnalisables et contrôlables, du calcul privé et prévisible, et des systèmes de production pleinement auditables.
Une stratégie construite brique par brique
L’ambition générale de Mistral est d’ailleurs martelée dès le titre de l’annonce : « faire de l’IA souveraine et open-weight la nouvelle frontière technologique. »
Cette dernière levée s’inscrit dans une trajectoire cohérente, amorcée depuis plusieurs mois par le groupe. Mistral avait notamment investi 1,2 milliard d’euros dans un data center en Suède en février 2026, présenté comme une étape vers une pile technologique européenne complète, même si les GPU Nvidia utilisés restaient un maillon non européen de la chaîne. Le groupe avait aussi commencé à concrétiser sa propre capacité de calcul en France, avec un data center de 830 millions de dollars annoncé en mars 2026 à Bruyères-le-Châtel (Essonne).
En juin 2026, son PDG, Arthur Mensch, avait d’ailleurs largement développé la ligne stratégique de la startup sur ses réseaux, érigeant les modèles open-weight en argument de souveraineté, promettant notamment aux entreprises de « posséder et contrôler les systèmes qui intègrent spécifiquement leur propriété intellectuelle ».
Un positionnement largement mis en avant par le marketing de l’entreprise française, et qui tombait alors à point nommé dans une industrie encore sonnée par la coupure soudaine de l’accès aux modèles Fable 5 et Mythos 5 d’Anthropic, sous ordre de Washington.
Sur le plan opérationnel, Mistral a également renforcé en juillet son partenariat avec Microsoft pour déployer ses modèles en Europe, aussi bien en cloud public qu’en environnements entièrement déconnectés, afin de répondre aux besoins des secteurs les plus réglementés.

articles.title: Hisense ajoute du cyan à ses TV RGB MiniLED : le 116UXS arrive en France
articles.text:
Présentée au CES sous l’appellation RGB MiniLED evo, l’évolution du rétroéclairage RGB de Hisense se concrétise. Désormais désignée RGB-C dans la communication de la marque, elle ajoute une quatrième composante cyan aux MiniLED rouges, vertes et bleues, avec un premier téléviseur de 116 pouces attendu en France avant la fin de l’année.
Au CES 2026, Hisense avait déjà montré une évolution de son RGB MiniLED en ajoutant une quatrième composante cyan au rétroéclairage. La technologie était alors présentée sous le nom de RGB MiniLED evo, sans calendrier précis de commercialisation.
À l’IFA, les choses se précisent : Hisense parle désormais de RGB-C, avec un premier modèle destiné au marché français, le 116UXS, attendu au quatrième trimestre 2026.
Quels avantages à l'ajout d'une diode cyan ?
Le principe reste le même : aux MiniLED rouges, vertes et bleues vient s’ajouter une source cyan, afin d’affiner le contrôle du spectre lumineux. Hisense associe cette architecture à son système ChromaMagic 2.0 et revendique jusqu’à 110 % de l’espace colorimétrique BT.2020, ainsi que plus de 40 000 zones de contrôle des couleurs.
La marque met également en avant une gestion plus fine des couleurs et du spectre, avec notamment les fonctions AI RGB Colour Dimming et AI RGB Colour Peaking. Le téléviseur repose sur une dalle avec une fréquence de rafraichissement maximale de 180 Hz et intègre un système Eye Comfort destiné à réduire fortement la part de lumière bleue émise entre 415 et 455 nm.
16 999 euros pour le 116 pouces
Hisense donne surtout désormais un prix et une fenêtre de lancement. Le 116UXS sera proposé à 16 999 euros, avec une disponibilité prévue au quatrième trimestre 2026. Un modèle de 100 pouces, le 100UXS, est également annoncé, mais son tarif reste encore à confirmer.
Sur son stand, Hisense nous a également indiqué vouloir reproduire la stratégie adoptée avec le RGB MiniLED classique : lancer d’abord la technologie sur une très grande diagonale, puis chercher à la rendre plus accessible par la suite. La marque ne donne toutefois encore aucun détail officiel sur les modèles concernés en 2027.
Après avoir déjà testé cette année le RGB MiniLED "classique" sur l’Hisense UR9S, il restera surtout à vérifier ce que cette quatrième composante cyan apporte réellement à la restitution des couleurs, notamment dans les teintes bleu-cyan et à forte luminance.

articles.title: Nasa-Forscher entdecken zehneckige Wolke am Saturn: „So etwas haben wir noch nie gesehen“
articles.text:
„So etwas haben wir noch nie gesehen“: Nasa-Forscher entdecken zehneckige Wolke am Saturn
Eine Forschungsgruppe der Nasa hat in Aufnahmen des Hubble-Weltraumteleskops eine riesige, zehneckige Wolke über dem Südpol des Saturns entdeckt. Sie ähnelt stark dem berühmten Sechseck am Nordpol des Planeten, weist aber auch entscheidende Unterschiede auf. Diese könnten darauf hindeuten, dass die Wissenschaftler:innen die Entstehung eines neuen atmosphärischen Phänomens in Echtzeit mitverfolgen können. „So etwas haben wir auf der südlichen Hemisphäre des Saturns noch nie gesehen”, kommentiert Amy Simon in einer Pressemitteilung. Sie ist leitende Wissenschaftlerin am Goddard Space Flight Center der Nasa und Mitautorin der Studie.
Hubble liefert detaillierte Aufnahmen
Als die Voyager-Raumsonde im Jahr 1981 am Saturn vorbeiflog, machte sie Aufnahmen von dessen Nordpol. Darin entdeckten Forscher:innen Jahre später eine auffällige, sechseckige Wolke, die stabil an einer Stelle verharrte. „Das nördliche Sechseck war jedes Mal da, wenn wir seit mehr als 40 Jahren nachgeschaut haben“, so Simon. Das neu entdeckte Phänomen scheine sich dagegen zu verstärken. Laut Archivaufnahmen habe die Bildung des Zehnecks erst im Jahr 2023 begonnen. Die Raumsonde Cassini, die den Saturn zwischen 2004 und 2017 umkreiste, hatte das Merkmal noch nicht erfasst, was laut Nasa darauf hindeutet, dass es erst danach entstanden ist. „Die Frage ist: Warum hat sich [die Wolke] gerade jetzt plötzlich gebildet, wo wir doch zuvor noch nie eine gesehen haben?“
Die Bilder entstanden im Rahmen des „Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy“-Programms (OPAL) des Hubble-Teleskops. Einmal im Jahr wird dabei ein Teil der Beobachtungszeit für Aufnahmen der äußeren Planeten des Sonnensystems genutzt. Ziel ist es, Langzeitbeobachtungen zu gewinnen und so die Daten von Raumfahrzeugen, die sie umkreisen oder passieren, zu ergänzen. Dank der langen Betriebsdauer des Hubble-Teleskops können Astronom:innen Veränderungen bei Planeten und anderen astronomischen Objekten über die Zeit verfolgen. Dadurch ermöglicht das OPAL-Programm auch, saisonale Veränderungen und kurzlebige Stürme zu beobachten und weitere atmosphärische Merkmale zu identifizieren, die sich langsam entwickeln.
Untersuchung des Dekagons geht weiter
Das Forschungsteam kann beobachten, wie sich die zehneckige Wolke über mehrere atmosphärische Schichten erstreckt und damit über die Wolkenobergrenzen hinausreicht. Zudem befinde sie sich in einem großen Jetstream am Saturn. „Als wir das OPAL-Programm starteten, rechneten wir mit spannenden Überraschungen, wussten aber nicht genau, was uns erwarten würde”, so Mike Wong in dem Nasa-Blogbeitrag weiter. Er ist an der Berkeley-Universität tätig und ebenfalls Mitautor der Studie. „Viele der Entdeckungen, die wir dank OPAL machen, basieren nicht nur auf einer einzigen Beobachtung, sondern auf Daten aus vielen, vielen Jahren. Regelmäßige Untersuchungen über einen längeren Zeitraum ermöglichen zahlreiche neue Erkenntnisse.“
Die Ergebnisse der Studie sind im Fachmagazin Science Advances erschienen. Damit sind die Untersuchungen des neuentdeckten Zehnecks aber noch nicht abgeschlossen. Das Team plant, Saturn weiterhin zu beobachten, um festzustellen, ob sich das Dekagon zu einer langlebigen, stabilen Formation wie das nördliche Hexagon entwickelt oder ob es sich weiter verändert. Das könnte auch dabei helfen, die Antriebskraft der Wolke zu ermitteln. Zusätzlich erhoffen sich die Forscher:innen neue Erkenntnisse über die atmosphärische Dynamik von Riesenplaneten und inwiefern diese mit Phänomenen zusammenhängen, die sich auch auf der Erde beobachten lassen.

articles.title: India's battery industry set to generate up to 2M jobs by FY30: Adecco India
articles.text:
India's battery industry set to generate up to 2M jobs by FY30: Adecco India
The industry's evolution from import dependency to a fully integrated cell-to-recycling industrial ecosystem is expected to create several jobs, says talent company Adecco India.
The country's battery industry is expected to generate 1.5 million to 2 million jobs by 2029-30 as it enters its most capital- and employment-intensive phase, evolving from an assembly-and import-dependent sector into a fully integrated cell-to-recycling industrial ecosystem, talent company Adecco India said.
India's battery industry is moving from importing and assembling lithium-ion cells to manufacturing batteries domestically, spanning across cells, complete battery packs, and recycling, Adecco India Director and Head of General Staffing Deepesh Gupta told PTI.
The industry could create 1.5 million to 2 million jobs by 2030, with about 25% direct jobs and 75% indirect jobs. Hiring is expected to grow by 25-30% annually, according to Adecco India.
This insight about the battery industry by Adecco India is based on inputs from over 30 of its client based in the country.
Further, Adecco India revealed that recruitment in the industry will tilt toward more skilled professionals in electro chemistry, materials science, battery engineering, manufacturing, and recycling.
"With battery manufacturing capacity currently at around 60 GWh and expected to approach 100 GWh by the end of 2026, along with upcoming gigafactory investments in Gujarat, Karnataka, Haryana and Telangana, the sector is moving beyond assembly and building the depth of a full industrial ecosystem," said Gupta.
Catalysing the vision of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', this localisation drive, supported by the Critical Minerals Mission and India's participation in the Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework, will reduce the country's reliance on imported cells and refined materials, while creating employment opportunities across established manufacturing hubs and emerging tier II and III industrial corridors, he added.
Lithium battery manufacturing is expected to contribute 50-60% of India's projected green manufacturing jobs by 2030, with specialised battery engineering talent commanding salary premiums of up to 35-40% over conventional manufacturing and electronics roles.
India's battery manufacturing is now translating into plant-level capacity. Under the PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cells, the government has committed Rs 18,100 crore to develop 50 GWh of domestic ACC manufacturing capacity, with an additional 5 GWh reserved for niche chemistries.
Gigafactory clusters continue to be the primary employment engine for the sector, concentrated in Karnataka, Telangana, Gujarat and Haryana.

articles.title: Hackers exploit new MikroTik RouterOS flaws to hijack routers
articles.text:
Hackers are exploiting a chain of two recently disclosed vulnerabilities in MikroTik routers to take control of devices with SSH services exposed to the internet.
One of the security issues, tracked as CVE-2026-67276, is an SSH authentication bypass flaw in MikroTik RouterOS caused by incomplete validation of RSA public keys.
An attacker who knows a username and the public modulus of that user’s key can exploit it by crafting a different key and logging in without the legitimate private key.
The second security issue is identified as CVE-2026-86060. It is an SSH privilege escalation flaw in MikroTik RouterOS due to improper handling of specially crafted usernames.
Hackers can leverage it using a specially crafted username to manipulate the SSH session so that the attacker obtains full administrative privileges.
Both vulnerabilities were discovered by Poland's CERT agency with the help of GPT-5.5-cyber and GPT-5.6-sol and received a critical severity rating.
The Polish agency dubbed the exploit chain “MikroTrick,” and warned that it is now actively exploited in the wild.
“In recent days we have been observing attacks against RouterOS devices accessible from the internet,” Poland's CERT warns.
“We have obtained confirmation that the attackers are exploiting this combination of vulnerabilities to take full control of devices whose SSH service is accessible from public networks.”
The Polish CERT also highlighted a third flaw, CVE-2026-67277, which affects the RouterOS bandwidth-test service and allows unauthenticated attackers to leak kernel memory or to remotely crash/restart the router.
MikroTik fixed the vulnerabilities in RouterOS 7.25beta3, 7.24.2, 7.23.4, and 6.49.21, released on September 3, and Poland's CERT validated the fixes.
In its advisory, the vendor notes that not all configurations are affected, but did not disclose any details to give users time to apply the security updates.
The updates add a compromise-detection mechanism to the routers that looks for known signs of unauthorized configuration changes at startup, disables malicious entries, and logs a critical warning.
However, the CERT notes that the absence of a marker indicating compromise should not be taken as a guarantee that a router has not been compromised.
The CERT shared the following indicators of compromise (IoCs):
- Log entries: ‘login failure for user -2 from <ip> via ssh’ and ‘user <name> added by ssh:-2@<ip>’
- Presence of a highly privileged ops account
- 82.192.72.4 — linked to confirmed successful attacks
- 103.102.31.18 — observed attempting to exploit MikroTrick
If compromise is suspected, the Polish agency recommends isolating the router, preserving logs and configuration, then factory-resetting the device and rebuilding it from a trusted configuration while rotating passwords, keys, and other secrets.
For those unable to apply the updates immediately, one recommendation is to restrict or disable externally accessible SSH, WWW/WWW-SSL, and bandwidth-test services, and avoid the built-in SSH clients and outbound TLS connections over untrusted networks.
As of September 5, there were 122,500 MikroTik devices with an exposed SSH interface, according to data provided by The ShadowServer Foundation. The exact number of devices vulnerable the MikroTik exploit was not determined, though.

articles.title: Audi A2 e-tron : je suis monté dans la moins chère des Audi électriques
articles.text:
25 ans plus tard, elle est de retour. Comme d’autres, à commencer par Renault, Audi a cédé aux sirènes de la nostalgie et a été piocher dans son passé récent l’inspiration pour développer une nouvelle voiture électrique. Mais à l’inverse de la marque au Losange qui a misé sur un succès emblématique avec la R5, l’Allemand a fait un choix pour le moins curieux : celui de ressusciter l’A2, un modèle remarqué certes, mais un échec commercial certain, symbolisé par une courte période de commercialisation (2000 – 2005).
Ce choix est d’autant plus étonnant que l’A2 est un modèle critique pour Audi. La marque aux quatre anneaux mise énormément sur sa compacte électrique à tel point que le succès ou non de ce modèle pourrait donner le ton des prochains mois pour la marque du groupe Volkswagen.
Alors cette Audi, est-elle un pari complètement fou ? Premier avis après être monté à bord de celle qui est dès à présent l’Audi électrique la moins chère du marché.
Design : des clins d’œil appuyés sans en rajouter
Le premier aspect qui va nous intéresser, c’est évidemment de savoir si cette nouvelle A2 électrique ressemble à l’ancienne. Pourquoi est-ce important ? Parce que le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que le design de l’A2 originale était discutable… ou disons qu’il a divisé… ou disons juste que pour une partie du public c’était franchement moche et que ça a joué dans l’échec commercial du modèle. Quid de la version 2026 ?
La nouvelle A2 ne reprend pas complètement les traits de l’ancienne, mais il y a quand même quelques clins d’œil, voire un peu plus, notamment avec cette ligne de toit plongeante qui reprend la philosophie du modèle original. C’est donc l’arrière du véhicule qui reprend la tradition, ce qui laisse à la face avant la lourde tâche d’innover. Audi assume ce choix avec une calandre plus resserrée qu’à l’accoutumée, marquée par des optiques très fines et un « black panel » qui simule la présence d’une grille d’aération. Outre l’aspect esthétique, celui-ci est idéal pour dissimuler une partie des capteurs de la voiture (radar, caméra, capteur de proximité), qui ne sont perceptibles que lorsqu’on s’approche assez près.
Cette fausse grille est doublée d’une seconde, en dessous, véritable cette fois et disposant de volets pilotés qui s’ouvrent et se ferment au besoin pour aider à diffuser les flux d’air sous le véhicule. Le même principe est appliqué aux diffuseurs latéraux qui évacuent l’air sous les roues puis sur le flanc de la voiture, évitant au maximum les turbulences et contribuant à améliorer le coefficient de traînée. Concrètement, le Cx est de 0,24 soit le meilleur pour une voiture compacte dans toute l’histoire d’Audi.
Dernière originalité immanquable cette fois : les poignées de porte. Audi a opté pour un nouveau système totalement électrique qui se matérialise par des petites « ailettes ». Celles-ci intègrent un retour haptique et réagissent au simple toucher de l’utilisateur, que ce soit pour l’ouverture ou la fermeture. Et pas de panique, chaque poignée dispose de sa propre batterie de secours, ce qui fait qu’il est possible d’ouvrir et de fermer sa voiture même s’il y a une défaillance du système électrique à bord ou en cas d’accident.
Au final, la filiation avec le modèle des années 2000 est là, mais Audi n’a pas été dans la surenchère. C’est une proposition un peu moins radicale que la version originale, qui ne plaira pas à tout le monde, mais qui ne manque pas de caractère.
Habitacle : Audi sans prise de risque
Ce parti pris assez osé au niveau du design s’arrête à la portière. Dès lors qu’on pénètre dans l’habitacle, le soufflet retombe. Audi a fait dans le classique aussi bien au niveau de l’aspect général (assez cosy cela dit) que de l’équipement. On retrouve le traditionnel système MMI avec deux écrans. Le Virtual Cockpit de 11,9 pouces pour l’instrumentation et un écran tactile incurvé en position centrale de 12,8 pouces. Ce dernier sert aux médias et au réglage de l’ambiance à bord. Si l’intégration est soignée, on aurait aimé que l’ensemble épouse davantage l’esprit de la compacte avec un peu plus d’originalité.
Celle-ci n’est présente qu’à travers le système Fidlock, un procédé assez proche du YouClip cher à Dacia. Concrètement, il s’agit d’un écosystème d’accessoires qui viennent se clipper sur des emplacements prévus dans l’habitacle mais aussi dans le coffre. Sacs, porte-gobelets et autres joyeusetés seront disponibles en option.
Non, décidément le point fort de l’habitacle de cet Audi A2. Il est à chercher du côté de l’espace à bord et de l’habitabilité. Malgré ses 4,32 m de long, la petite dernière affiche le même empattement que le Q4. La place ne manque pas, que ce soit pour les places avant comme à l’arrière.
Côté techno, c’est là encore du grand classique avec toutefois un niveau d’équipement qui se rapproche davantage du segment supérieur que des premières pages du catalogue. Il en va ainsi de l’assistant de freinage d’urgence, de celui d’évitement ou encore de la caméra à vision périphérique avec modélisation 3D. Audi ajoute également dans cette A2 e-tron sa fonctionnalité « connected work », soit la compatibilité avec les outils Microsoft tels que Teams ou Outlook. Côté son, c’est Sonos qui est à l’honneur avec un système audio à 14 haut-parleurs et un caisson de basse délivrant jusqu’à 660 watts.
En outre, Audi a eu la bonne idée de proposer la charge bidirectionnelle V2L et V2H (on peut aussi bien charger des objets qu’un réseau domestique). Toujours au chapitre de l’habitabilité, l’A2 e-tron dispose d’un coffre affichant 396 L de capacité ainsi que d’un tout petit « frunk » de 13 L sous le capot (de série sur les finitions les plus élevées) dont la mission se limitera probablement au rangement du câble de recharge.
Une consommation record : l’A2, un modèle d’efficience
L’A2 originelle a marqué son époque par une efficience assez incroyable. L’A2 e-tron veut en faire autant, et à l’ère de l’électrique cela passe par une consommation annoncée assez étonnante : moins de 13 kWh/100 km (12,8 si on veut être très précis).
À titre de comparaison, la plupart des modèles concurrents tournent entre 18 et 20 kWh/100 km et ce chiffre peut encore grimper pour peu qu’on reste un peu plus longtemps sur une voie rapide.
L’efficience, c’est bien, mais comment ça se traduit en autonomie ? Sur l’A2 e-tron, si on opte pour la plus grande batterie (84 kWh), on serait en droit d’attendre 650 km d’autonomie (649 km selon le cycle WLTP). C’est conséquent et ça demande bien sûr à être vérifié lors d’un essai en conditions réelles, ce que nous ne manquerons pas de vous proposer dans les prochains mois.
Même le modèle le moins cher du catalogue, celui doté d’une batterie de 52 kWh, peut se targuer d’une autonomie relativement généreuse (432 km en WLTP).
C’est sans doute sur ce point que la filiation avec l’A2 de 2000 est la plus forte. Et c’est sans doute l’une des raisons qui ont poussé Audi à choisir cette appellation pour leur modèle « d’entrée de gamme ».
La moins chère des Audi électriques
Dès sa commercialisation, l’A2 e-tron va devenir l’Audi électrique la moins chère du catalogue. Ce statut assez honorifique était pour l’instant l’apanage de l’A4 e-tron dont le tarif dépassait les 45 000 euros. L’A2, elle, débute sous les 40 000 euros, avec un prix de départ de 38 600 euros pour la version de base (dotée d’une batterie de 52 kWh et d’un moteur de 125 kW (170 ch)).
Au total, ce sont quatre versions de l’A2 qui seront proposées par la marque allemande. Toutes utilisent les mêmes technologies de moteur (synchrone à aimant permanent), mais diffèrent sur la technologie de batterie. Les deux « petits » modèles (52 kWh et 61 kWh) sont en chimie LFP. La version de 84 kWh opte pour une batterie NMC.
Côté moteur, la version de base affiche une puissance de 125 kW (175 ch). Les versions intermédiaires optent pour des moteurs de 140 kW (190 ch) et 170 kW (231 ch). Quant à la version la plus performante, elle affiche 240 kW, soit 326 ch. Cette dernière dispose aussi du couple le plus impressionnant (545 Nm), là où les autres se contentent de 350 Nm.
Quant à la performance pure, dans sa version la plus musclée, l’A2 e-tron abat le 0 à 100 km/h en 5,7 secondes.
L’autre différence majeure se situe au niveau de la puissance de recharge et elle est loin d’être anodine. Les deux versions les plus accessibles de l’A2 électrique devront se contenter d’une modeste puissance de 100 et 105 kW. Les deux versions supérieures s’en sortent honorablement avec une puissance maximale de 185 kW. Dans tous les cas, le 10 à 80% théorique s’effectuerait en moins de 29 mn (24 mn au mieux).
Audi A2 électrique : le pari fou ?
Que penser du pari d’Audi avec cette A2 ? La nouvelle compacte électrique va-t-elle rebooster la côte de la marque aux quatre anneaux ou son histoire ressemblera-t-elle à son aînée ? Car les enjeux sont énormes pour ce modèle taillé pour le marché européen et qu’Audi a choisi de faire assembler dans son usine historique d’Ingolstadt. Tout un symbole.
Sur le papier, cette première rencontre est pleine de promesses : Audi a fait du très bon boulot, mais… car il y a un mais… Même si l’A2 est aujourd’hui la moins chère des Audi électriques, son prix reste relativement élevé : 38 600 euros au minimum.
À l’époque l’A2 originale avait souffert d’un prix trop élevé justifié en partie par toutes les révolutions techniques qu’elle intégrait. 25 ans plus tard, le tarif semble toujours salé, surtout en comparaison de certains modèles chinois ou même d’une Tesla Model 3. Cette fois, l’innovation technologique ne peut servir d’excuse (l’A2 est basée sur une plateforme déjà bien connue, MEB+, et n’a pas de « killing feature » qui pourrait justifier un tel prix. Ce qu’elle a en revanche, c’est du style et une efficience du tonnerre. Est-ce que ça sera suffisant ?

articles.title: Dreame unveils the latest products for its smart living ecosystem at IFA in Berlin - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Dreame has unveiled its new smart home products at IFA in Berlin under the banner “Redefining Tomorrow’s Home” including the X60 Ultra Extreme and Aqua20 Ultra Roller robot vacuums and the T16 Series of wet and dry vacuums.
The goal for Dreame is to deliver even smarter cleaning experiences for Australian households by creating a connected smart living ecosystem that cover floor and garden care along with other emerging lifestyle categories.
“Dreame’s focus has always been on solving everyday household challenges through meaningful innovation, whether it’s reaching previously inaccessible areas, reducing manual cleaning effort or delivering smarter decision-making through advanced AI, our latest product lineup is designed to help consumers spend less time on chores and more time doing what matters most,” says Harold Xu, Dreame’s head of marketing Australia and New Zealand.
DREAME X60 ULTRA EXTREME
This is Dreame’s flagship robot vacuum and it brings industry-leading cleaning coverage throughout your entire home.
The new unit is the first to feature Dreame’s Dual-Joint UltraExtend Arms that can reach out 12cm with the brush and 18cm with the mob to get into the all the spaces that are out of reach for other robot vacuums.
This means it can reach all the way across to skirting boards, corners and under and around furniture and chairs.
DREAME AQUA20 ULTRA ROLLER
The Aqua20 Ultra Roller offers a deeper floor clean by combining steam, hot water and intelligent roller technology.
It brings 180-degree Celsius steam and hot water to rid your floors of those stubborn baked on stains like dirt, grease and other messes.
The roller mop can extend into corner and other narrow spaces.
At the same time the onboard proactive dirt detection can help find and identify the hidden messes and deliver the right amount of cleaning to get rid of it.
DREAME T16 SERIES
The Dreame Wet and Dry Vacuum portfolio had been bolstered with the T16 TriForce which brings together strong suction and intelligent surface recognition.
Also onboard is anti-tangle technology which makes everyday maintenance a breeze.
Dreame has also previewed the T16 Pro CarpetFlex and T16 Ultra Series which were also unveiled at IFA 2026 in Berlin.
The Dreame X60 Ultra Extreme is expected to launch in Australia and New Zealand in late October 2026.
The Dreame Aqua20 Ultra Roller will launch in September 2026.
* Stephen Fenech travelled to Berlin with support from Anker, Roborock, Ecovacs, Dreame, MOVA and EZVIZ.

articles.title: North Korean Hackers Deploy New Linux Espionage Toolkit
articles.text:
North Korea-aligned threat actors have been using a new Linux toolkit in attacks targeting automotive and media organizations in South Korea, Rapid7 reports.
Designed for long-term surveillance, the framework consists of a HAProxy instance called ‘ted backdoor’ and trojanized versions of tools such as ‘agetty’, ‘atd’, ‘crond’, ‘polkitd’, and ‘sshd’.
The toolkit supports remote command execution, credential harvesting, and script injection into web traffic, enabling attackers to spy on victims for long periods of time without detection.
According to Rapid7, the framework is deeply integrated within the target infrastructure, with the ted backdoor being compiled as part of the HAProxy version 2.8.12 running on the victim’s environment.
“It uses its native filter API, internal memory pools, event scheduler, and process management infrastructure to intercept traffic and hide from monitoring, while genuine load balancing traffic operates as expected,” the cybersecurity firm explains.
Likely in use since late 2024, when the first involved HAProxy iteration was released, the toolkit also uses a curl-based RAT, an SSH keylogger, and a stager.
Initial access to an edge server was obtained through the exploitation of a Groupware login portal vulnerability. The SSH keylogger, which also serves as a staging server, was used for credential harvesting, enabling lateral movement to internal systems.
“The stager checks for the presence of either crond or HAProxy, and only then deploys CurlRAT, retrieving it either from its data section or the edge web server. In parallel, the ted backdoor is dropped onto the HAProxy load balancer,” Rapid7 explains.
The backdoor establishes C&C communication for data exfiltration, script injection, and command execution, and the balancer starts redirecting or serving malicious content to selected clients browsing through it.
CurlRAT, the curl-based RAT deployed in the attacks, polls the C&C every 12 hours for commands. Based on these, it can decrypt and execute commands stored in its configuration, decode and write a new config payload to disk, and deploy a full interactive PTY shell.
The ted backdoor is a custom HAProxy plugin compiled within the HAProxy source code, directly hooked into the balancer’s built-in HTTP parser. It can intercept and inject HTTP traffic, execute C&C tasks, and achieve persistence, among others.
As part of the observed attacks, the threat actor used domains registered under low-cost commodity top-level domains (TLDs) and blended the payload delivery traffic into normal web browsing, mimicking Naver’s pstatic.net static content domain.
“Ted backdoor and curlRAT were designed to persist during long-term espionage operations with the ability to steal cookie sessions, credentials, redirect selected users, conduct drive-by download attacks, and hide evidence of the tampered page to a specific range of IPs to evade detection,” Rapid7 notes.
Attack artifacts recovered by the cybersecurity firm, along with the infrastructure used, point to watering-hole techniques previously used by APT37 and Lazarus, and the campaign timeframe overlaps with that of Operation SyncHole, attributed to Lazarus last year, which suggests that a North Korean threat actor might be behind this campaign as well.

articles.title: On est tombé sur les trois futurs vélos cargo électriques de Decathlon : du très lourd en préparation
articles.text:
En 2022, Decathlon a fait trembler le créneau des vélos cargo électriques. Son Btwin R500E au prix plancher a séduit des milliers de familles, et popularisé le format. En 2026, la marque française a prolongé la carrière du longtail avec quelques améliorations, sous le nom de Btwin E-Three 500. Mais ce ne serait que temporaire, car le remplaçant pourrait prochainement débarquer avec deux modèles cousins.
Nous avons en effet découvert la nouvelle gamme de vélos cargo électriques Decathlon, au travers de leur programme de développement produits adressé à une sélection de clients. Et ce n’est pas un mais trois modèles que nous attendent. En voici en résumé :
- E-Three 100 : longtail entrée de gamme, 2 enfants, prix estimé 2 000 €
- E-Three 500 : longtail milieu de gamme, 2 enfants, prix estimé 2 500 €
- E-Two 500 : midtail milieu de gamme, biplace, prix estimé 2 200 €
Decathlon duplique son célèbre vélo longtail
Le Btwin E-Three 500 est donc le remplaçant de l’actuel modèle éponyme. Toujours dans un format longtail pour transporter 2 enfants à l’arrière, il réduit sa taille de roue avant à 20 pouces avec de gros pneus, façon fatbike. Plus pratique, son cadre est ouvert pour offrir un enjambement plus facile, avec une batterie externe, qui laisse penser à une réduction de poids.
Il conserve aussi l’antivol avant, les barres de maintien (avec ouverture a priori), les repose-pieds, une double béquille centrale et ajoute de nouvelles jupes latérales. L’assistance passe toujours par un moteur arrière et la transmission par un dérailleur, qu’ils restent à définir. Clairement, la firme parisienne Gaya est devenue la cible.
Le Btwin E-Three 100 est une déclinaison plus abordable. Exit la fourche suspendue, la selle à ressort, les coussins et le dossier, tandis que certains composants sont spécifiques (éclairage, pneus, etc.) à ce modèle. L’objectif est un prix plancher, plus proche des 2 000 euros.
Un vélo électrique biplace Decathlon façon fatbike
Quant au Btwin E-Two 500, il reprend le format 20 pouces aux pneus bicolores et l’avant du cadre de l’E-Three. Toutefois, l’arrière est inédit avec une structure renforcée, afin de conserver une capacité d’emport élevée.
Ici, ce midtail est un vélo électrique biplace avec son siège arrière muni de poignée, encore plus typé fatbike, ce qui le rapproche de l’UTO OG200. Decathlon devrait ainsi le positionner entre les deux longtails en termes de tarifs, autour de 2 200 euros pour rivaliser avec le Nakamura Crosscity+.
Quid des modèles haut de gamme Owuru « 900 » ?
Précaution à prendre : ces trois vélos cargo électriques ne sont pas encore officiels. Decathlon peut encore les modifier ou changer de stratégie. En effet, depuis 2 ans, plusieurs fuites ont révélé le développement de vélos cargos électriques plus premium. Celle du plan produit en 2024 montrait un midtail démarrant à 2 500 euros, et un longtail à 3 200 euros.
En 2025, nous découvrions les Btwin E-Two 900 et E-Three 900. Ces VAE cargo en développement étaient équipés de la motorisation centrale Owuru, à transmission automatique continue, notamment vue sur les Rockrider E-ACTV 900 et Btwin LD 920 E.
Cependant, la marque nous a confié cet été avoir changé de stratégie pour revoir sa gamme. La présence des trois modèles plus abordables sont-ils devenus la priorité ? S’il est impossible de dire s’ils sont abandonnés, leur report a minima illustre le marché tendu du VAE, qui pourrait enfin signer une reprise.
Son concurrent Intersport a également conservé un positionnement plus grand public, avec des modèles abordables à l’image du Nakamura Crosscity dès 1 099,99 euros, tandis que la concurrence asiatique s’est renforcée.
Nous devrons ainsi surveiller les prochaines annonces officielles de Decathlon, pour confirmer ou non ces futurs vélos cargos électriques Btwin E-Three 500, E-Three 100 et E-Two 500, ainsi que leurs possibles grands frères « 900 ».

articles.title: El ajuste de iPhone que permite leer y ver videos en el auto sin sufrir mareos
articles.text:
Apple incorporó en el iPhone una función de accesibilidad que ayuda a reducir los mareos por movimiento cuando el usuario intenta leer o mirar videos como pasajero en un vehículo. Se trata de los indicadores de movimiento del vehículo, puntos animados que aparecen en los bordes de la pantalla y representan el desplazamiento del auto sin interferir con el uso normal del teléfono.
Esta herramienta forma parte del menú de accesibilidad del sistema operativo y busca corregir un conflicto sensorial habitual entre lo que ven los ojos en la pantalla y lo que percibe el oído interno durante el trayecto. A continuación, el paso a paso para activarla, configurarla y personalizarla.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué son los indicadores de movimiento del vehículo en el iPhone
Los indicadores de movimiento del vehículo son puntos que se mueven en los bordes de la pantalla del iPhone para simular el desplazamiento del vehículo en el que viaja el usuario. Esta señal visual periférica ayuda a mitigar los mareos que produce el uso del teléfono durante un viaje, ya que reduce la sensación de conflicto entre el movimiento real y la quietud de la imagen en pantalla.
Según explica Apple, estos indicadores funcionan mejor cuando la persona está sentada mirando hacia el frente del vehículo. La compañía advierte, además, que esta función está pensada exclusivamente para pasajeros: no debe usarse mientras se conduce ni en ninguna situación que exija atención plena para preservar la seguridad al volante.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo activar los indicadores de movimiento en la configuración de Accesibilidad
Para habilitar esta función, hay que ingresar a la app Configuración del iPhone y luego avanzar por el siguiente camino: Accesibilidad y, dentro de ese menú, Movimiento. Allí aparece la opción Indicadores de movimiento en vehículos, donde el usuario puede elegir entre distintas alternativas de uso.
Una de esas alternativas es el modo Automático. Cuando se selecciona esta opción, el iPhone muestra los puntos animados de manera espontánea apenas detecta que el dispositivo se encuentra dentro de un vehículo en movimiento. Los puntos desaparecen solos cuando el vehículo se detiene, sin necesidad de intervención manual.
PUBLICIDAD
También existe la posibilidad de manejar la función de forma manual desde el centro de control. Basta con abrirlo, tocar el botón correspondiente a los Indicadores de movimiento del vehículo y elegir si se muestran u ocultan en ese momento. Apple recomienda, además, configurar un atajo de accesibilidad para activar o desactivar la función de manera rápida desde cualquier pantalla.
Cómo personalizar el aspecto de los puntos animados en pantalla
Además de activar o desactivar la función, el iPhone permite modificar la apariencia de los indicadores. Para hacerlo, se debe repetir el recorrido inicial (Configuración, Accesibilidad, Movimiento) y tocar nuevamente Indicadores de movimiento en vehículos, pero esta vez seleccionando la opción Personalizar aspecto.
PUBLICIDAD
Dentro de este menú se pueden ajustar tres aspectos distintos. El primero es el patrón de movimiento: la opción Regular ofrece un desplazamiento predecible y estable, mientras que la opción Dinámica genera una experiencia visual con mayor variación.
El segundo aspecto personalizable es el color de los puntos. El sistema ajusta automáticamente la saturación de ese color para garantizar el contraste con el contenido que queda detrás de cada punto en la pantalla.
PUBLICIDAD
Por último, se puede regular la visibilidad de los indicadores mediante dos variantes: Puntos más grandes, que aumenta el tamaño de cada punto, o Más puntos, que incrementa la cantidad total que aparece distribuida en los bordes de la pantalla.
PUBLICIDAD
