articles.title: Nigeria’s GDP growth is creating output, not enough jobs
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria’s economy is growing faster than it has since the second quarter of 2021. But beyond the headline growth rate, Nigeria’s economy is not growing evenly.
A growing share of economic expansion is coming from telecommunications and the service sector, while some of the sectors that employ the most Nigerians are growing much more slowly.
This helps explain why stronger gross domestic product (GDP) growth has not necessarily translated into better living standards for many Nigerians. An economy can produce more without creating enough employment to materially improve living standards. About 139 million Nigerians still live below the national poverty line, the World Bank said in July.
Nigeria’s gross domestic product grew by 4.43% in real terms in the second quarter of 2026, up from 4.23% a year earlier. Real GDP strips out the effect of rising prices. In an economy experiencing high inflation, nominal output can increase simply because goods and services cost more. Real GDP growth is therefore a better measure of whether the economy is actually producing more.
GDP measures the total value of economic activity in a country, making its growth rate a useful indicator of whether the economy is expanding or contracting. But the headline number does not tell where that expansion is happening, how broad it is, or whether the sectors employing the most people are growing quickly enough to change household incomes.
A 5-Year High for Nigeria’s GDP
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026—the fastest quarterly growth rate since Q2 2021. Tap across the timeline to see the five-year trajectory.
Nigeria’s growth slowed sharply after the 2021 post-pandemic recovery, spending much of 2023–2024 trapped in the 2–3% range. The steady acceleration throughout 2025 and into Q2 2026 marks a meaningful aggregate improvement.
The economy is growing, but not everything is growing equally
Nigeria’s services sector, which accounted for 56.62% of GDP, grew by 4.60% in Q2. The industry sector grew by 3.96%, down from 7.46% a year earlier, while agriculture grew by 4.39%.
Telecommunications and information grew by 10.38% in Q2, more than twice the pace of overall GDP growth. Trade grew by 2.40%. Manufacturing grew by 3.24%, while real estate grew by 3.76%.
Agriculture, which remains one of the country’s largest sources of employment, grew by 4.39%.
What Is Holding Nigeria’s Growth Back?
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026. But some of its biggest sectors are still constrained by problems that growth alone cannot solve. Pick a sector to see what’s holding it back.
WHAT’S HOLDING IT BACK?
THE RESULT
THE BIGGER PROBLEM
Nigeria can digitise parts of its economy. It cannot digitise away the infrastructure needed to grow the sectors that produce food, goods and mass employment. Telecoms can expand digitally. Agriculture, manufacturing and trade still depend heavily on physical infrastructure.
Growth in agriculture has picked up, supported by government efforts to promote mechanisation and dry-season farming, as well as improved weather conditions in parts of the north-west, north-east and south-west, according to the World Bank.
But the sector continues to face structural constraints that limit how much it can expand. Conflict and insecurity disrupt production in key regions. Farmers also face limited access to quality seeds and fertilisers, climate risks such as flooding, high costs of imported inputs and machinery, limited access to finance, and poor logistics infrastructure.
Across most non-oil sectors, including manufacturing, inadequate infrastructure—particularly electricity, transportation and logistics—limited access to credit, high input costs and shortages of skilled labour continue to constrain growth, according to the World Bank.
Telecoms is becoming an increasingly important engine
Nigeria’s economy was worth ₦121.26 trillion ($91.78 billion) in Q2 2026.
Telecommunications and information services contributed ₦12.04 trillion ($9.11 billion) to that output. Only trade, at ₦27.38 trillion ($20.72 billion), and crop production, at ₦14.37 trillion ($10.88 billion), contributed more among the activities reported by the NBS.
Telecoms is now the third-largest contributor to the economy as the demand for connectivity in the country continues to grow.
MTN Nigeria, the country’s largest telecom operator by subscriber count, reported that average data usage per subscriber increased by 15.2% in the first half of 2026, while total data traffic rose by 25.8%. Smartphone penetration reached 66.4%. The company’s service revenue increased by 25.9% to ₦2.99 trillion ($2.26 billion) in the first half of 2026.
Across the country, data consumption grew 46.75% year-on-year in June 2026. With broadband penetration still below 60%, there is still room for the sector to expand further as it moves toward 100%.
Telecoms can therefore continue to add economic output as more Nigerians come online, businesses become more dependent on digital infrastructure, and existing users consume more data. That growth can also create opportunities for indirect job creation across the wider digital economy. But its impact on direct employment is likely to remain limited because many jobs in this industry require specialised skills, while the number of available roles tends to narrow as the industry becomes more efficient and technology-driven.
The problem is jobs
Telecoms can generate enormous economic value without employing as many people as agriculture, trade, manufacturing, or construction. As industries become more productive, they can generate more output without increasing their workforce at the same pace.
Between 2001 and 2010, Nigeria ranked among the world’s 15 fastest-growing economies, averaging 8.2% annual growth, according to the World Bank. Sectoral reforms in banking and telecoms also unlocked private sector development.
GDP per capita almost quadrupled during that period, from $568 in 2001 to $2,280 in 2010.
But the growth failed to produce significant job creation.
“The expansion of good quality non-farm jobs—a feature that characterised East Asia’s growth in the 1980s and 1990s—was absent in Nigeria,” the World Bank said. “Meanwhile, industries in the formal sector, such as financial services and hospitality, were either not very employment-intensive, or have added labor from a very low base, hence failing to make a significant difference in wage employment growth.”
Companies, especially those in the service sector, can become more valuable without becoming proportionately more labour-intensive.
For instance, the United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA) had 12,770 employees in 2015 and spent ₦57.45 billion ($43.48 million) on employee benefits. By 2025, its workforce had fallen to 10,821, while employee benefit expenses had risen to ₦123.49 billion ($91.68 million).
Between 2020 and 2025, MTN Nigeria’s direct employee count increased by 8.51% to 2,001.
Since 2001, the telecoms industry has created more than 500,000 direct jobs, as of 2025, while also creating an extensive ecosystem of indirect employment and economic activity. The telecom sector’s contribution to GDP, directly and indirectly, was estimated at ₦33 trillion ($24.98 billion) in 2023.
But 500,000 direct jobs is still small relative to the size of Nigeria’s labour force.
In 2023, agriculture alone employed more than 25 million people in farming, forestry and fishing activities, accounting for 30.1% of total employment, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
Nigeria Is Growing. But Where Are the Jobs?
Nigeria’s economy grew 4.43% in Q2 2026. But growth is not reaching workers evenly. Compare four major sectors to see why GDP growth does not always translate into broad-based job creation.
Telecoms is growing much faster than the economy—but it does not need millions of workers to do it.
DIRECT EMPLOYMENT
THE GAP
Telecoms is one of the fastest-growing parts of Nigeria’s economy. But because the sector is capital- and technology-intensive, more output does not require proportionately more workers. It can lift GDP without becoming a mass employer.
THE BIGGER PROBLEM
Nigeria needs growth that does more than increase GDP. It needs growth that can absorb the millions of people entering the labour market.
Yet agriculture’s growth rate is less than half the telecoms’ growth rate. Manufacturing, another major source of employment and productive capacity, generated ₦9.38 trillion ($7.09 billion) in real output across its 13 subsectors.
The sectors producing some of the fastest growth are not necessarily the sectors capable of translating that growth into enough jobs and higher household incomes.
Telecoms will keep growing as Nigerians consume more data, and more economic activity moves online. But telecoms cannot carry the entire economy indefinitely.
Nigeria’s next phase of economic expansion needs manufacturing to expand, agriculture to become more productive, and construction to boom. These sectors not only add to GDP when they grow, but create productive jobs at a scale that services such as telecoms cannot.
The World Bank expects Nigeria to average real GDP growth of 4.2% between 2026 and 2028. However, infrastructure gaps, security challenges, and weak agricultural productivity are likely to constrain diversification and job creation, limiting gains in per capita incomes despite steady aggregate growth.
For now, the numbers show that Nigeria’s economy is growing, but it is not yet broad or deep enough to translate into real income growth for the average Nigerian.

articles.title: Creíamos que el vino protegía nuestra salud. El problema es que quizá confundíamos la copa con la compañía
articles.text:
Durante años, el vino ha ocupado un lugar peculiar en las conversaciones sobre si de verdad es bueno o no para nuestra salud. Se ha hablado de sus polifenoles, de sus supuestos beneficios cardiovasculares y de los estudios que lo relacionan con una mayor longevidad, pero ahora se apunta a que la vida social que lo suele acompañar es lo que de verdad puede estar ayudando.
Tener una buena vida social sí que se relaciona con vivir más, como apunta un estudio publicado en PLoS Medicina que reunió a más de 300.000 participantes. Aquí sus autores encontraron que las personas con relaciones sociales más fuertes tenían una mayor probabilidad de vivir más tiempo. Y la asociación se mantenía incluso teniendo en cuenta factores como la edad, el sexo o el estado de salud inicial.
Pero en el sentido contrario, la ciencia también ha visto que mantenerse aislado y en soledad aumenta el riesgo de mortalidad. En otras palabras, hay una base científica bastante sólida para decir que el aislamiento social es un factor relevante para la salud y que mantener vínculos sociales se asocia con mejores resultados a largo plazo.
El papel del alcohol. Para algunas personas, lograr estas relaciones sociales puede ser un auténtico reto por su personalidad, y es por ello que se apunta a que el alcohol puede tener un efecto positivo en este punto de nuestras vidas. Y aquí un experimento con 720 personas apuntó a que, en determinadas ocasiones, el alcohol aumenta el efecto positivo y la sensación de vínculo entre los participantes.
La razón puede estar en que el alcohol puede reducir la inhibición y favorecer que algunas personas hablen, rían o interactúen con una mayor facilidad. Pero hay una diferencia entre decir que el alcohol puede facilitar una interacción social puntual y afirmar que el alcohol mejora nuestra salud a largo plazo.
Lo que pensábamos. Durante mucho tiempo, numerosos estudios encontraron que quienes consumen pequeñas cantidades de alcohol presentan, en algunos análisis, una mortalidad inferior a la de los abstemios. Y esta idea sin duda caló entre la sociedad, sobre todo la famosa curva en forma de J que apunta a que poco alcohol parecía asociarse a mejores resultados, mientras que el aumento de este se relaciona con riesgos más lesivos.
Pero la ciencia analizó estos estudios que justifican el consumo de un poco de alcohol, y se vio que muchos de estos presentaban problemas metodológicos, entre ellos la composición del grupo de referencia. Por ejemplo, algunas investigaciones incluían a antiguos bebedores dentro del grupo de "abstemios", aunque hubieran dejado de beber precisamente por problemas de salud. Y esto puede hacer que el grupo de personas que no beba parezca artificialmente más enfermo y que el consumo de alcohol parezca más saludable.
El vino es una de las bebidas alcohólicas que se ve como más saludable debido a sus compuestos bioactivos como, por ejemplo, el resveratrol, catequinas y quercetina. Pero aquí debemos tener en cuenta que una sustancia presente en un alimento tenga efectos biológicos potencialmente positivos no significa que consumir la bebida que la contiene sea beneficiosa para la salud.
Además, la evidencia no respalda con claridad que el vino tenga una ventaja especial respecto a otras bebidas alcohólicas.
Si le quitamos alcohol. Ante esta tesitura, se puede llegar a pensar que el vino tinto sin alcohol puede tener algunos beneficios positivos relacionados con estos compuestos fenólicos. Pero aunque la ciencia ha encontrado algo en ese sentido, todavía hay bastante incertidumbre para extraer conclusiones firmes sobre el efecto a largo plazo.
No hay consumo seguro. Aunque como sociedad tratamos de justificar el consumo de alcohol, ya sea porque mejora nuestras relaciones sociales o para reducir nuestro estrés oxidativo, la realidad es que la OMS apunta a que no existe un nivel de consumo que sea seguro para la salud. Hay que recordar que el alcohol está clasificado como carcinógeno del grupo 1 por la IARC, y su consumo aumenta el riesgo de distintos tipos de cáncer.
La OMS recuerda, además, que incluso cantidades relativamente pequeñas de alcohol pueden incrementar el riesgo de determinados cánceres, y no importa que proceda de vino, cerveza o destilados: lo relevante en este contexto es el etanol.
La conclusión del vino. Con toda esta información, podemos saber que no hay pruebas sólidas de que beber vino alargue la vida. Sí que existen pruebas que apuntan a que las relaciones sociales de calidad son importantes para nuestra salud y que las personas socialmente conectadas presentan, de media, mejores resultados de supervivencia.

articles.title: Sony officialise le WH-1000XM4C : le retour d’un classique... privé de modernité
articles.text:
Sony officialise le WH-1000XM4C : le retour d’un classique... privé de modernité
Six ans après son lancement, le Sony WH-1000XM4 revient… sans vraiment changer. Le WH-1000XM4C reprend les caractéristiques de son aîné, tout en s’offrant quelques retouches minimes, dont un réglage sonore hérité du XM6.
Fiche technique quasi complète, visuels officiels, disponibilité prévue à la rentrée 2026… La version modernisée du célèbre casque Sony WH-1000XM4 faisait déjà parler d’elle depuis quelques semaines. L’heure est désormais à son lancement, puisque la marque vient de dévoiler discrètement le WH-1000XM4C, aux côtés de nouvelles versions de ses casques Bluetooth d’entrée de gamme, baptisées WH-CH730N et WH-CH530.
Ce nouveau souffle donné au WH-1000XM4 s’explique notamment par le succès durable de la première version. Lancé en 2020 et commercialisé jusqu’en juillet 2026, le casque n’a cessé de séduire par son confort, sa pliabilité et son excellent rapport sonorité-prix, malgré l’arrivée de ses successeurs WH-1000XM5 et WH-1000XM6. Sony entend désormais l’inscrire officiellement comme un modèle de milieu de gamme, plutôt que comme un ancien flagship maintenu au catalogue.
Un design inchangé et une évolution matérielle anecdotique
Pour capitaliser sur le succès du premier modèle, Sony n’a pris aucun risque côté design. La structure du WH-1000XM4C étant strictement identique à celle du WH-1000XM4, les changements se cantonnent à la disparition de la référence inscrite sur les branches, ainsi qu’à celle de l’appairage NFC et de son logo, une fonction devenue pour le moins anecdotique.
Si le WH-1000XM4C est inchangé sur le plan esthétique, la partie matérielle ne connaît pas non plus de révolution. On retrouve ainsi la désormais vieillissante puce de réduction du bruit QN1, la même architecture à cinq microphones et les traditionnels transducteurs de 40 mm en néodyme. En revanche, ce statu quo serait particulièrement décevant si Sony n’avait pas pris soin d’améliorer la qualité des appels en environnement bruyant, franchement dépassée sur le premier modèle.
De plus, notons que le casque se contente du codec LDAC et ne prend pas en charge la norme LE Audio (technologie Auracast et codec LC3), malgré son passage à une puce Bluetooth 6.0. Un choix d’autant plus surprenant que tous les casques Sony lancés depuis 2025 en bénéficient, tout comme le nouveau casque supra-auriculaire d’entrée de gamme WH-CH530.
Réglage sonore hérité du XM6 et autonomie annoncée en baisse
Néanmoins, au milieu de cette fiche technique ultra-conservatrice, Sony évoque un nouveau réglage tonal inspiré du WH-1000XM6. Si cette évolution se confirme à l’écoute, elle pourrait redonner de l’intérêt au WH-1000XM4C sur son segment de prix. Le casque profite également d’un égaliseur à 10 bandes introduit pour la première fois sur le XM6, ainsi que de la technologie DSEE Extreme, chargée de restaurer une partie des informations perdues lors de la compression audio.
L’autonomie annoncée atteint 27 h avec la réduction de bruit enclenchée, soit 3 h de moins que celle officiellement revendiquée par le WH-1000XM4. Toutefois, il ne serait pas étonnant que Sony se montre simplement plus précis dans ses estimations. Lors de notre test du premier modèle en 2020, nous avions en effet mesuré exactement 27 h d’autonomie avec l’ANC activé.
Le WH-1000XM4C est désormais disponible dans des coloris noir, argent et lavande au prix de 250 €, soit un tarif officiel identique à celui du WH-1000XM4 avant sa rupture de stock.
Au regard d’améliorations très marginales et de composants qui n’ont guère évolué par rapport à ceux d’un casque datant de 2020, nous aurions toutefois apprécié que Sony revoie ses prétentions tarifaires à la baisse. Il faudra par ailleurs sans doute patienter avant de voir le WH-1000XM4C passer sous la barre symbolique des 200 €, un niveau de prix que son prédécesseur atteignait régulièrement lors des périodes de promotion.

articles.title: AI agents are creating more work, not less — and OpenAI's own numbers back it up
articles.text:
AI agents are creating more work, not less — and OpenAI’s own numbers back it up
OpenAI says it hit a goal it set last fall, stating researchers are now using what the company calls an “automated research intern,” which is an agent that can handle well-defined tasks that would normally take a researcher several days.
The data shows coding-agent use climbing throughout 2026, and by mid-August its agents were logging 3.1 agent-workdays for every human workday across the research organization. The median researcher was spending more than $600 on inference per day at API prices, while those in the 90th percentile spent more than $7,000.
The median researcher was spending more than $600 on inference per day at API prices, while those in the 90th percentile spent more than $7,000.
Agent hours versus useful output
But everyone knows that an agent-workday and a human workday aren’t the same. The company converts the time agents spend working on tasks into standard eight-hour workdays. Because researchers can run several agents at once, the figure tells us how long the agents are working, but not necessarily what they’re completing.
For engineering teams, that leaves plenty of work on the human side, which means running more agents can increase the amount of work happening at once, but it can also increase the amount of work a human needs to keep track of.
OpenAI’s very specific definition of a research intern highlights that it must be able to complete well-defined research tasks that would take a skilled person several days, but a human is still in charge. The company’s next goal, an automated AI researcher, is one they hope to reach by March 2028.
The company’s next goal, an automated AI researcher, is one they hope to reach by March 2028.
Supervision becomes the constraint
Using a taxonomy from Epoch AI, OpenAI broke the agents’ work into six areas — Decide, Design, Build, Run, Analyze, and Communicate — and found activity increased across all six between January and August, although agents still did relatively little of the work involved in deciding what research to pursue.
Much of the work is practical, with agents writing research and infrastructure code, monitoring experiments, and providing enough technical support that OpenAI says attendance at debugging office hours has fallen, prompting one team to stop holding the sessions altogether.
And yet, more agent hours don’t automatically mean more useful research. OpenAI says code output and experiment counts are relatively easy to track, but neither shows how much progress those agents actually made. Compute also increased significantly as the number of experiments rose.
OpenAI used another model to judge how well agents performed on tasks of varying difficulty and found that, despite improving success rates between January and July, humans still had to step in on more than half of successful tasks that would have taken a person four to eight hours.
Security incidents limit Astra deployment
Once engineers can run several agents at once, with those agents launching subagents of their own, the challenge shifts to keeping up with what they produce — catching runs that go off track, reviewing code diffs, and deciding what is ready to ship or feed into a training run.
Astra’s persistent-agent capabilities already let researchers hand off multi-day assignments, which makes this supervisory strain worse, not better.
The company acknowledges that as agents take over more of the execution, the parts of research that are hardest to automate will consume more of an engineer’s time, putting a practical limit on how much agent output one person can realistically review.
On July 20, a series of outages caused by agents disrupted OpenAI’s research infrastructure badly enough that the company took its training container service offline and later brought it back with tighter restrictions.
Nearly a month later on August 7, OpenAI tightened access again after early evidence suggested Astra could reach the “Critical” cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework, restricting the model to higher-security research areas and adding safeguards that developers may already be encountering as unexpected API interruptions
Workloads shift between models fast
Astra-class GPU allocation fell 59.2% the following week, but that compute didn’t sit idle for long. Researchers moved much of the work to other models, which saw GPU allocation rise 17.2% and made up for roughly 85% of the drop in Astra usage. Instead of reducing the amount of work being run, the restrictions pushed it to other models, showing how easily workloads can move when one part of the system is locked down.
OpenAI’s researchers are handing off larger jobs to agents, running more of them at once and launching more experiments, but whether that translates into faster research is harder to measure — and OpenAI is still figuring out how to price it.

articles.title: Humanoid robots are being prepared for combat as China moves them from labs to military training grounds
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Back when humanoid robots could barely stumble forward without falling over, there were plenty of jokes about their use on the battlefield, Terminator-style, not being much of a concern. Now, though, these machines are running faster than the fastest human and doing parkour – and China wants to turn them into robotic miltary "combatants."
August saw the World Humanoid Robot Games take place in China, where robots took parts in several events. The same month, Unitree claimed its Superman robot can run faster than Usain Bolt, although the figure has not been independently verified.
 – Unitree (@UnitreeRobotics) August 17, 2026
Reuters reports that two days after the Games ended, the People's Liberation Army's official newspaper, the PLA Daily, called for researchers to accelerate the transfer of these technologies from laboratories to military training grounds.
Reuters reviewed more than 100 Chinese military procurement notices, academic studies, patents, official publications, government records, and defense-company materials. It found that the country is accelerating research into the robots' military uses and planning for their eventual wartime deployment.
China has long led the world when it comes to humanoid robots. Its manufacturers accounted for about 95% of shipments of these bots in 2025, giving the PLA plenty of access to the machines.
The good news is that while humanoid robots have come a long way since those slow, lumbering, ungainly early efforts that required a tethered connection to operators, we really are still a long way from seeing squads of marauding T-800 killbots marching across fields. They require a lot of energy, so can't operate for great lengths of time, and even the most advanced designs occasionally fall over, especially on rough terrain.
Robot powered by Qualcomm's new AI chip dies mid-presentation
by u/SuggestionMission516 in singularity
However, China still has plans for how to use humanoid robots. It envisions them being used alongside robot dogs – something that ICE could soon use – and unmanned vehicles, an area that is becoming increasingly popular among global militaries.
In a scenario described by a research paper last year, six combat robots – a mixture of humanoids, robot dogs, and unmanned vehicles – would be split up between two assault teams. Working with ground troops, the robots would clear an enemy-occupied building, floor by floor and room by room. The authors believe the equipment to make this a reality will be ready in 5 to 10 years.
Other proposed uses include reconnaissance, logistics, patrols, and operations inside tunnels and ships. State-owned defense company Norinco says its Fuxi humanoid can carry out sentry duties and all-weather reconnaissance, though it can also be remotely controlled instead of operating autonomously.
There's also the important question of whether a machine can reliably distinguish combatants from civilians or recognize when someone is surrendering. China's defense ministry said in March that AI-powered weapons should remain under human control, though that might bring little assurance to skeptics.
Reuters found no evidence that an armed humanoid has been deployed with an operational PLA unit, but one Chinese military researcher warned that, once the remaining technical and cost barriers are overcome, humanoid robots will "stream onto the battlefield."

articles.title: Huawei lança Mate XT 2 com nova dobra e tela de privacidade • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Huawei lança Mate XT 2 com nova dobra e tela de privacidade
Novo trifold abandona a dobra em sanfona e adota recurso de privacidade apresentado recentemente pela Samsung.
O smartphone com três dobras da Huawei recebeu uma nova versão nesta segunda-feira (07/09). O Huawei Mate XT 2 troca o formato de dobra externa das versões passadas pela estrutura em Z, além de trazer uma tela OLED com modo de privacidade, tecnologia semelhante à apresentada pela Samsung.
Assim como o Huawei Mate XTs, o novo trifold da marca não inova muito em design, mantendo o corpo fino e um módulo octagonal na traseira, onde ficam as câmeras. A exceção está na adição de uma tela externa, que aparece pelo novo mecanismo de dobra adotado pela marca.
Na China, o Mate XT 2 parte de 19.999 yuans, cerca de R$ 15.275 em conversão direta, sem impostos. Portanto, chega mais caro que o Mate XTs e a primeira versão, o Mate XT Ultimate Design, que desembarcou no Brasil por R$ 32.999. Por enquanto, a Huawei não anunciou uma versão global.
Entre as principais mudanças em relação ao Mate XT original está o mecanismo de abertura. Anteriormente, a marca criou um mecanismo de dobra no formato de Z. No Mate XT 2, as duas extremidades do painel se dobram para dentro, em direção ao centro, assim como ocorre no Galaxy Z TriFold.
Aberto, o aparelho oferece uma tela OLED de 10,2 polegadas, com resolução de até 2.232 x 3.148 pixels. O painel interno usa taxa de atualização variável de 1 a 90 Hz. Na parte externa, há uma tela OLED de 6,5 polegadas, com taxa de atualização de 1 a 120 Hz e proteção de vidro Kunlun, da Huawei.
A outra grande novidade do Mate XT 2 também está no display, que traz um modo de privacidade integrado. A tecnologia, apresentada antes pela Samsung, no Galaxy S26 Ultra, altera a forma de emissão da luz pela tela para estreitar o ângulo de visão.
Com a função ativada, quem olha diretamente para o smartphone vê a imagem normalmente, enquanto ela fica menos visível em posições diferentes. O recurso pode ser útil em situações como transporte público, reuniões ou outros ambientes nso quais o usuário não queira deixar informações pessoais serem vistas por quem está por perto.
Assim como na solução da sul-coreana, é possível ativar a função a todo momento ou apenas quando apps específicos forem abertos.
O Mate XT 2 possui uma câmera principal de 50 MP com sensor de 1/1,28 polegada, maior que as gerações anteriores, com abertura física variável de f/1.49 a f/4.0, que permite controlar a quantidade de luz captada e alterar a profundidade de campo. O conjunto inclui, ainda:
Segundo a Huawei, o celular oferece aproximadamente 3,5x de zoom óptico, até 7x de zoom com qualidade óptica e zoom digital de até 100x. As câmeras traseiras podem gravar vídeos em até 4K.
O novo trifold da Huawei estreia o chip Kirin 9050 Pro, da própria Huawei, e vem com 16 GB de RAM e 1 TB de armazenamento. A bateria tem 5.600 mAh e suporta carregamento de até 66 W com fio e 50 W sem fio.
Na conectividade, o aparelho traz Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC e suporte a dois chips. A Huawei também inclui comunicação via satélite por meio de redes como a BeiDou na China.
O modelo roda HarmonyOS 7.0 e conta ainda com leitor de digitais na lateral, infravermelho para controle remoto e GPS de dupla frequência.

articles.title: Samsung Foundry Allocates Half of 4 nm Capacity for HBM4 Base Dies
articles.text:
Monday, September 7th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Samsung Foundry Allocates Half of 4 nm Capacity for HBM4 Base Dies
According to Korean media, Samsung Foundry, a division that operates silicon manufacturing as a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is reportedly allocating significant capacity for HBM4 base die manufacturing. For HBM4, Samsung is producing the base die on a 4 nm node, which reportedly receives half of the entire manufacturing capacity of the 4 nm node, internally referred to as SF4. Customers of HBM4 and the upcoming HBM4E memory standards are now requesting base dies to be filled with custom logic. For instance, customers could implement custom logic like memory controllers and PHYs directly on the HBM base die, significantly reducing the area occupied by these components on the main compute chiplet.
Samsung operates its SF4 manufacturing at Pyeongtaek Campus 2 (P2) and Campus 3 (P3) on lines S5 and S6. An increase in manufacturing is not only coming for ASIC designs by external customers but also for HBM4 base die manufacturing, which is becoming especially important for ASIC customers aiming to maximize the performance of their designs.With its HBM manufacturing business, Samsung is capturing a significant volume from buyers. In Q2 2026, Samsung secured 38% of the HBM market share by revenue, a notable increase from just a year ago when the company held 15%. Meanwhile, SK hynix's share has decreased from 64% in Q2 2025 to 50% in Q2 2026, as many customers have diversified and started sourcing their HBM from Samsung. With more offerings like custom base dies and capacity expansions, Samsung could capture even greater revenue share in the coming quarters if the foundry business continues to perform well.

articles.title: Robbie Williams-backed Tickets for Good raises €4.5 million for international expansion | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Tickets for Good, a UK startup that provides key workers with low-cost tickets for live events, has raised a further €4.5 million (£3.9 million) to accelerate its international expansion and create 10 new jobs in Sheffield in the next three years.
The funding was secured from NPIF II – Mercia Equity Finance, which is managed by Mercia Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), alongside Shaping Impact Group (SI3), Finance Yorkshire, Leansquare and private investors.
Steve Rimmer, CEO and co-founder, says: “Tickets for Good was built on a simple belief that live events should be available to everyone, especially the people who give so much to our communities. This investment is a huge vote of confidence in our team, our partners and the impact we’re creating. It will help us grow internationally, create skilled jobs in Sheffield and connect many more people with live events.
“Neville and I started this with a shared love of music and the belief that unused tickets could do something good. Today, that idea has helped more than a million people experience live events they might otherwise have missed, and we’re only just getting started.”
Tickets for Good’s financing sits amid broader investment in technologies supporting events and live fan experiences in Europe.
EU-Startups’ 2026 coverage saw Ghent-based EventTech startup Exhibitly’s €1.4 million pre-Seed round for its AI-powered event personalisation platform, alongside adjacent fan-experience investments such as €6.5 million for Warsaw-based connectivity specialist Microamp, €3.6 million for Lausanne-based immersive-technology startup AlphaLum and €37 million for Amsterdam payments infrastructure company Silverflow.
Together, these financings amount to approximately €50 million.
Chris Borrett, Investment Director at Mercia Ventures, adds: “Demand for live experiences has never been stronger, however rising ticket prices are creating barriers to access for many consumers, while venues and promoters increasingly recognise the value of full attendance and engaged fans. Tickets for Good has created a powerful solution that aligns these interests. We believe the business has the potential to become a category-defining platform within the global live entertainment market.”
Founded in 2022, Tickets for Good distributes surplus tickets donated by event partners to NHS workers, teachers, charity staff and people receiving Cost of Living support. Recipients sign up to the platform for free then pay a nominal transaction fee for each ticket.
It looks to make live events accessible for those who might otherwise miss out, while helping venues maximise capacity, drive ancillary revenues and grow their audiences.
The Sheffield-based company now has almost 750,000 verified members globally and has distributed over 1.25 million tickets.
Robbie Williams is an ambassador for the company, along with former Dutch international goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar and music entrepreneur Hans Brouwer.
Dave Dirks, Managing Partner at Shaping Impact, says: “Tickets for Good is a strong example of the kind of company we want to support: commercially ambitious, highly scalable and built around a clear social purpose. By making live events more accessible to people who too often face barriers to participation, the company is creating meaningful impact in a sector with enormous cultural and social value. We are excited to support the team in this next phase of growth.”
The company expanded into the US in 2023 when it was accepted onto the Comcast SportsTech accelerator in St Louis and now also has operations in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.
The company also reportedly doubled its revenue in 2025 and aims to achieve a further five-fold growth in the next three years.
Alex McWhirter, CEO of Finance Yorkshire, adds: “In a relatively short space of time, Tickets for Good has achieved significant growth and is now reaching an international audience with its socially driven consumer platform. Finance Yorkshire is pleased to support Tickets for Good in its ambitions to further expand, particularly in overseas markets, and the creation of additional jobs in Yorkshire is particularly welcome.”

articles.title: Pisa 2025: proibição de celulares nas escolas salta de 37% para 81% no Brasil
articles.text:
A proibição de celulares avançou rapidamente nas escolas brasileiras. Dados do Pisa 2025, divulgados pela Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (OCDE) nesta terça-feira (8), mostram que 81% dos estudantes estão em instituições onde o aparelho não é permitido. Em 2022, eram 37%.
O levantamento também aponta uma relação entre as restrições e a distração em sala de aula. Na média dos países da OCDE, alunos de escolas que proíbem celulares têm cerca de 13% menos probabilidade de relatar distrações provocadas por dispositivos digitais.
O relatório, ainda, revelou que quase metade dos alunos brasileiros usa inteligência artificial para estudar, além de apontar dados de proficiência e bullying.
Cerco aos celulares ganhou força
A mudança no Brasil aconteceu em apenas três anos. Em 2022, 37% dos estudantes frequentavam escolas onde o uso de celulares não era permitido nas dependências. Em 2025, o percentual chegou a 81%.
A média da OCDE também aumentou, mas em ritmo menor: passou de 34% para 49% no mesmo período. O índice brasileiro, portanto, ficou bem acima do registrado entre os países da organização.
Os dados ainda mostram uma associação entre as restrições e a distração provocada por dispositivos. Na média da OCDE, estudantes de escolas que proíbem celulares têm cerca de 13% menos probabilidade de relatar esse tipo de distração.
Quando a tela tira o foco
Os dispositivos digitais continuam presentes na rotina escolar. No Brasil, os estudantes relataram passar, em média, 1,3 hora por dia usando esses equipamentos para atividades de aprendizagem. Na OCDE, são 1,7 hora.
Parte do tempo também é dedicada a atividades sem relação com os estudos. Os brasileiros passam, em média, 1 hora por dia usando dispositivos digitais na escola para lazer. A média da OCDE é de 1,1 hora.
Os próprios alunos percebem a distração entre os colegas:
- 25% dos estudantes brasileiros disseram que colegas frequentemente se distraem com dispositivos digitais durante a maioria ou todas as aulas de ciências;
- Na média da OCDE, o percentual é de 28%;
- Entre os países da organização, estudantes que relatam esse tipo de distração obtêm, em média, 11 pontos a menos em ciências;
- No Brasil, a diferença chega a 19 pontos.
IA entra na rotina de estudos
A tecnologia usada pelos alunos não se resume aos smartphones. Pela primeira vez, o Pisa também levantou informações sobre o uso de chatbots de inteligência artificial.
No Brasil, 48% dos estudantes de 15 anos disseram usar ferramentas como o ChatGPT pelo menos uma vez por semana para estudar. A média da OCDE ficou em 46%.
Leia mais:
- A urgência de formar jovens fluentes em inglês na era dos agentes de IA
- IA não poderá mais corrigir provas e redações nas escolas; veja o que muda
- Olhar do Amanhã: a inteligência artificial está criando uma nova elite cognitiva?
Para realizar pesquisas preliminares sobre novos temas, 40% dos brasileiros recorrem à tecnologia, contra 31% na média da organização. Já 31% usam chatbots para resumir textos e 27% para elaborar rascunhos de trabalhos escolares.
Apenas 11% afirmaram nunca ou quase nunca usar essas ferramentas nas atividades analisadas. Na OCDE, são 14%.
O desafio é equilibrar tecnologia e atenção
Os dados do Pisa 2025 mostram que a tecnologia ocupa espaços diferentes na rotina escolar. Celulares são cada vez mais restringidos, enquanto dispositivos digitais e ferramentas de inteligência artificial continuam sendo usados pelos estudantes.
No Brasil, onde 81% dos alunos estão em escolas que não permitem celulares, a questão passa pelo equilíbrio entre o uso desses recursos para aprender e a necessidade de manter a atenção durante as aulas.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Gary Oldman lo confirma: el nuevo actor de James Bond ya está fichado y él tiene su favorito
articles.text:
El oscarizado sir Gary Oldman acaba de anunciar lo que millones de personas esperaban desde hace meses: James Bond ya tiene nuevo actor. Después del final de la saga de Daniel Craig con No Time to Die, la propiedad creativa de la saga pasó a manos de Amazon MGM Studios, que durante mucho tiempo ha empezado a desarrollar su propia manera de revitalizar la franquicia. Por lo pronto, ya se sabe que el director de este ansiado reinicio será Denis Villeneuve (Dune, Blade Runner 2049).
Pero ahora parece que estamos muy cerca de conocer al actor que se convertirá en el próximo James Bond. Y es que Gary Oldman ha afirmado en una entrevista concedida al programa canadiense The Morning Show que la compañía ya tiene tomada la decisión. "Lo sabremos muy pronto, ¿verdad? Porque ya lo han elegido. Ya han tomado una decisión, aunque aún no la han anunciado", desvela.
Aunque Amazon MGM ha permanecido en silencio acerca de todos los rumores que han circulado durante meses, esta vez la información viene de uno de los nombres más potentes e importantes de la industria. Por ello, parece que esta vez sí es cierto, el nuevo actor de James Bond ya está fichado. De hecho, Gary Oldman ha dejado claro quién es su favorito para hacerse con el papel.
"Se rumorea que Jack Lowden está entre los finalistas", sugiere. No es de extrañar que mencione su nombre, pues Gary Oldman lleva años compartiendo trabajo con Lowden, pues juntos protagonizan la aclamada serie de espías Slow Horses. Ahora, el veterano intérprete no esconde que quiere que su compañero pase a vestir el esmoquin del agente 007. "Cruzo los dedos por Jack", sentencia.
El nuevo actor de James Bond está al caer
Lo cierto es que las palabras de Gary Oldman sobre el próximo actor de James Bond coinciden con un fuerte rumor surgido la semana pasada. En él, se especulaba con que Amazon MGM había programado unas audiciones para principios de septiembre y, así, cerrar definitivamente el proceso.
Los finalistas, según ese rumor, eran Jacob Elordi (Euphoria, Frankenstein), Paul Mescal (Normal People, Gladiator II), Harris Dickinson (Triángulo de la tristeza, El clan de hierro), Jack Barton (Heartstopper, Los hombres del S.A.S.), Callum Turner (One Night Only, Animales Fantásticos) y el mencionado Jack Lowden. Es muy posible que en las próximas semanas se desvele la decisión final.

articles.title: Huawei copies Samsung’s privacy display in its latest trifold
articles.text:
Huawei has released its third trifold phone in China, and the company has clearly had half an eye on Samsung during development. Not only does the Mate XT 2 adopt the inward-folding form factor used on Samsung’s Galaxy Z TriFold, it’s also the first foldable to include a privacy-enhancing display, much like the one Samsung added to the Galaxy S26 Ultra this year.
Huawei copies Samsung’s privacy display in its latest trifold
The Mate XT 2 also borrows Samsung’s inward-folding design.
The first Mate XT, which launched in China in late 2024 and internationally a few months later, used an accordion-esque folding design. It removed the need to include an additional cover screen on the phone, but left parts of the delicate folding display permanently exposed. The follow-up XTs retained the design, but the XT 2 instead takes inspiration from Samsung’s trifold, folding both sides of the 10.2-inch flexible screen inwards to keep them safe from harm.
More surprising is the addition of a privacy OLED display. This looks much like Samsung’s, so far only found on the S26 Ultra. When activated, it switches on pixels that emit light at narrower angles, making the screen appear almost black from the sides, but still visible head-on. It’s an optional extra, only available if you opt for 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage and pay a further ¥1,000 (about $150) to add the privacy screen.
Beyond the display, the XT 2 has Huawei’s new Kirin 9050 Pro chipset, improved water-resistance with an IP59 rating, and a triple rear camera. It launched today in China, starting at ¥19,999 ($3,000), though international release plans remain unknown. Samsung’s own Galaxy Z TriFold was discontinued shortly after its release last year, though leaks suggest that Samsung is still working on a follow-up.

articles.title: Le prix du remake de Zelda Ocarina of Time laisse craindre un jeu moins ambitieux que prévu
articles.text:
C’est sur l’eShop australien (actuellement en maintenance, tiens tiens…) que le prix de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time est apparu. En mettant à jour son catalogue, Nintendo a en effet laissé apparaître le tarif du jeu sur Switch 2 : 94,95 dollars australiens pour la version dématérialisée, soit environ 60 euros. Seulement 10 euros de plus que le remake de Star Fox, et 10 euros de moins que le prochain Fire Emblem.
Le montant affiché par Nintendo place finalement Ocarina of Time dans une sorte d’entre-deux : un peu plus cher que Star Fox, mais bien moins coûteux que les productions Switch 2 vendues au tarif fort. Le site Vooks souligne, dans un article publié ce 8 septembre 2026, que le prix australien de 94,95 dollars correspond au tarif numérique, tandis que la version physique devrait atteindre 109,95 dollars australiens, soit sans doute autour de 69,99 € en Europe.
À première vue, difficile donc d’y voir le signe d’un remake totalement repensé. Depuis l’apparition des premières informations autour du projet, les attentes sont pourtant particulièrement élevées. Ocarina of Time reste l’un des jeux les plus importants de l’histoire de Nintendo, et un simple lifting graphique pourrait sembler insuffisant pour justifier son retour sur une nouvelle génération. Le tarif pourrait malheureusement laisser penser que Nintendo est resté prudent avec ce remake.
Zelda Ocarina of Time pourrait n’être qu’une simple refonte graphique
Plutôt qu’un gigantesque remake venant réinventer Hyrule, le jeu pourrait être une simple modernisation du classique de 1998 : graphismes entièrement retravaillés, contrôles adaptés, interface améliorée et quelques ajustements dans les donjons et le monde.
Il faudra toutefois éviter de tirer des conclusions définitives à partir d’un simple tarif. Nintendo n’a pas communiqué sur le budget du jeu, sa durée de développement ou la quantité de contenu créée pour l’occasion. Mais après des mois d’attente et alors que Nintendo entretient soigneusement le mystère autour du projet, le moindre indice est forcément scruté, et cette fuite du prix ne rassure pas spécialement les fans.
Sur Reddit, cette annonce nourrit justement une certaine inquiétude. Dans le subreddit r/GamingLeaksAndRumours, plusieurs internautes s’interrogent sur ce que ce tarif révèle des ambitions du projet. « J’espère vraiment que ce ne sera pas 60 $ US, car cela garantirait qu’il ne s’agit pas d’un remake complet. Il est absolument hors de question que Nintendo facture moins de 70 $ s’il s’agit d’un remake intégral », écrit un utilisateur.
Il faudra maintenant patienter jusqu’au Nintendo Direct de ce 8 septembre à 16 heures, consacré au 40e anniversaire de The Legend of Zelda, pour en voir un peu plus sur le remake d’Ocarina of Time, et si les images dévoilées confirment (ou non) les craintes suscitées par ce prix.

articles.title: La verdadera razón por la que Microsoft eliminó el Pinball 3D de Windows Vista
articles.text:
3D Pinball: Space Cadet desapareció de Windows Vista por un error de programación que nadie logró resolver a tiempo. El fallo apareció durante la migración de Windows XP hacia una arquitectura de 64 bits y afectó de forma directa el funcionamiento del juego. Un obstáculo legal posterior terminó de sellar su destino y explica por qué nunca regresó de manera oficial.
El error técnico que sacó al pinball de Windows
El problema surgió cuando el equipo de desarrollo trabajaba en adaptar Windows XP de 32 a 64 bits. Esa transición implicaba revisar cómo el procesador y el sistema manejaban la información, y obligaba a ajustar programas escritos bajo reglas anteriores.
PUBLICIDAD
En un juego que depende de cálculos físicos constantes, cualquier diferencia mínima en la forma de representar o redondear un número podía alterar la posición de la pelota. Eso fue exactamente lo que ocurrió: en la versión de 64 bits, la bola atravesaba los objetos de la mesa como si no existieran.
Al iniciar una partida, la pelota bajaba con lentitud por el lanzador, cruzaba el resorte y terminaba cayendo fuera de la pantalla. El detector de colisiones, responsable de calcular los impactos contra paredes, obstáculos y paletas, había dejado de funcionar por completo.
PUBLICIDAD
Raymond Chen, ingeniero con más de tres décadas de trayectoria en el desarrollo de Windows, relató el episodio en diciembre de 2012 en su blog The Old New Thing, alojado en el sitio oficial para desarrolladores de Microsoft. Según su versión, dos ingenieros intentaron localizar el origen de la falla sin éxito.
El código tenía varios años, había sido escrito por una compañía externa y casi no contenía comentarios que explicaran su lógica interna. Chen aseguró que ni siquiera lograron identificar con precisión la parte del programa encargada de detectar las colisiones.
PUBLICIDAD
Con millones de líneas de Windows todavía pendientes de adaptación, el equipo no podía destinar varios días a resolver un error que probablemente estuviera vinculado a diferencias en los cálculos de coma flotante entre ambas arquitecturas. “Tomamos ahí mismo la decisión ejecutiva de eliminar Pinball del producto”, escribió Chen.
Qué reveló Microsoft años después sobre el fallo original
La historia tuvo una corrección relevante en 2022, cuando Chen publicó una actualización de su relato original. Allí explicó que el fallo más grave se había detectado en una versión experimental de Windows de 64 bits diseñada para procesadores Alpha AXP.
PUBLICIDAD
Según esa precisión, alguien corrigió el problema con posterioridad, posiblemente mediante cambios en el compilador o en el modo de redondeo utilizado por el sistema. Como resultado, Pinball llegó a funcionar en algunas ediciones de Windows de 64 bits.
Chen sostuvo que nadie le informó en su momento que el juego había sido recuperado, por lo que asumió durante años que había desaparecido de manera definitiva. Este dato cambia parcialmente la narrativa original: el error técnico explicó la eliminación inicial, pero no impidió que existiera una solución posterior dentro de la propia compañía.
PUBLICIDAD
El obstáculo legal que impidió el regreso oficial del juego
El componente técnico no alcanza para explicar por qué Space Cadet nunca volvió a versiones modernas de Windows. Microsoft intentó revivirlo mediante un proyecto interno de Microsoft Garage, y los desarrolladores lograron empaquetar de nuevo la edición de 32 bits.
Ahí apareció un segundo obstáculo, esta vez de naturaleza legal. Space Cadet no había sido creado originalmente por Microsoft: era una de las tres mesas de Full Tilt! Pinball, desarrollado por Cinematronics y publicado por Maxis en 1995.
PUBLICIDAD
Microsoft había obtenido una licencia para adaptar esa mesa e incluirla primero en el paquete Microsoft Plus! para Windows 95, y luego en Windows NT 4.0, Windows 2000, Windows Me y Windows XP. Esa licencia, sin embargo, había sido redactada bajo condiciones específicas.
El acuerdo firmado con Cinematronics autorizaba a Microsoft a incluir el juego en Windows 95, en Microsoft Plus! y en sus productos sucesores, pero no contemplaba su lanzamiento como una aplicación independiente. Chen reveló en 2018 que esa restricción impedía tanto publicarlo en Microsoft Store como liberar su código fuente.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué opciones existen hoy para jugar al pinball clásico
En la actualidad, la única forma de acceder a Space Cadet es a través de vías no oficiales. Existen adaptaciones, versiones reconstruidas mediante ingeniería inversa y páginas web que permiten jugarlo directamente desde el navegador.
Ninguna de estas alternativas constituye una reedición oficial de Microsoft. La compañía no ha publicado ninguna versión propia del juego desde su desaparición de Windows XP, y la licencia original sigue vigente como impedimento legal.
PUBLICIDAD
Descargar ejecutables que prometen recuperar el Pinball original desde sitios desconocidos implica, además, un riesgo de seguridad para los usuarios. La ausencia de canales oficiales deja este tipo de descargas fuera de cualquier garantía o control por parte de Microsoft.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Pour son cloud interne, l'Urssaf choisit l'open source américain de Red Hat
articles.text:
Red Hat annonce fièrement ce mardi 8 septembre que l’Urssaf a choisi ses solutions pour son infrastructure. Red Hat est le géant américain de l’open source et des solutions Linux, une filiale d’IBM. On le retrouve notamment derrière le projet Fedora.
L’Urssaf, l’organisme qui collecte les cotisations sociales en France, a déployé 38 clusters OpenShift, la plateforme de conteneurs de Red Hat, avec 1 450 namespaces et 45 applications en développement ou en production. On y trouve CESU et Pajemploi, que des particuliers utilisent tous les jours pour déclarer un salarié à domicile. Certains de ces services encaissent plus de 4 000 transactions par seconde.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Linux : tout savoir sur l’OS libre de droit pour débuter
            
Le reste de l’infrastructure suit la même logique. Red Hat Enterprise Linux, le système d’exploitation maison, tourne sur environ 41 % des serveurs et fait fonctionner SNV2, l’outil qui gère les cotisations des usagers.
Protégez votre vie numérique et vos appareils contre les virus, arnaques, ransomwares et menaces en ligne avec Bitdefender, primé pour sa protection et compatible avec Windows, Mac, Android et iOS.
Au-delà du choix d’une solution open source, mais pas vraiment souveraine, l’Urssaf y gagne concrètement. Les mises à jour techniques, qui demandaient plusieurs semaines à plusieurs mois, se font désormais en quelques jours, sans coupure de service.
Frédéric Bronnert, product owner de la plateforme de cloud interne, assume le refus du cloud public : « nous ne pouvions pas faire appel à des services de cloud externe », en raison de la sensibilité des données. Plus de 100 personnes ont été formées pour tenir le rythme, avec un responsable de compte technique Red Hat en contact chaque semaine avec les équipes.
Open source ne veut pas dire non-américain
C’est là que le mot souveraineté demande un peu de précision. L’Urssaf modernise ses serveurs sans toucher aux postes de travail de ses 16 000 salariés pour le moment. Elle ne quitte donc pas Windows.
La solution open source déployée ici reste éditée par Red Hat, filiale de l’américain IBM. Bronnert vante une base open source qui « renforce la souveraineté technologique, l’autonomie et l’indépendance », mais la souveraineté est un peu limitée par un partenariat aussi fort avec une entreprise américaine, même si le code est ouvert. L’Urssaf installe également un cluster GPU dédié à l’IA et prépare une plateforme d’IA générative interne, toujours sans service extérieur.
En avril 2026, la direction interministérielle du numérique a annoncé sa propre sortie de Windows vers Linux, avec l’idée d’entraîner toute l’administration derrière elle. La DGFiP, l’administration fiscale, étudie le même virage pour ses postes. Et Jean-Baptiste Courouble, DSI de l’Urssaf, défend depuis des années un cloud privé mutualisé pour toute la sphère sociale, CNAM et MSA comprises.
Ces décisions vont dans le même sens, sans former encore une doctrine claire. L’Urssaf garde ses données en interne, forme ses équipes et sort des éditeurs captifs, ce qui reste rare dans le secteur public et rejoint les efforts européens pour se passer des géants américains du cloud. La vraie bascule, celle des postes de travail et des outils du quotidien de millions d’agents, est encore devant l’État français.

articles.title: OpenAI Agents Hijack Another Victim Website
articles.text:
OpenAI agents overwhelmed a small German Wikipedia-style website with thousands of posts that fought the moderator to avoid being removed.
On September 4, 2026, Reuters reported that ‘a swarm’ of OpenAI agents ‘had hijacked a German wiki site’. Open AI acknowledged the event describing it as a misalignment incident (a behavior that deviates from human instructions or safety guardrails).
The victim site is DseWiki (currently unavailable), a site for programmers open to the site’s community. The agents apparently made between 15,000 and 18,000 autonomous edits, including advice on how to recover pages that the site’s editors had deleted.
The hijack apparently began back in May, was unnoticed for three months, and seemingly predates the Hugging Face incident. The agents adapted the style of their posts to evade the moderator’s attempts to delete them.
“Autonomous agents ran on Microsoft Azure infrastructure for weeks, identified themselves as OpenAI systems, coordinated on how to evade shutdown, and no monitoring caught any of it for three months until outside researchers went looking,” explains Seemant Sehgal, founder and CEO at BreachLock.
On September 5, OpenAI posted a response on X: “It’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.” However, there is growing concern that frontier models simply grant too much power to their agents.
“I struggle here with not getting too doomsday-ish,” comments Ashley Knowles, lead cybersecurity consultant at Black Hills Information Security, “but realistically, this is showing a pattern of concerning behavior. I’m wondering if this race to become ‘first’ is undercutting security measures that need to be taken to properly secure and guard AI agents as they’re in development. My concern grows when you consider that OpenAI is also resisting further investigation.”
Lydia Zhang, president and co-founder at Ridge Security, is more forthright. “We shouldn’t blame the agents, we should hold their designers accountable,” she says. “The technology to control agent behavior exists. The real question is: what are the consequences when designers fail to use it?” It is not entirely clear whether she is referring to the user agent designer, the AI provider, or both.
Steven Swift, managing director at Suzu Labs, posits a possible cause behind OpenAI’s misalignment incidents. “One of the problems OpenAI was trying to solve was agentic systems that would declare tasks complete when there was obviously more work to do. So, they invested heavily in training that part of the process, so that when an agent tries to determine if a task is complete or not, it is less likely to exit early.”
He suggests that a side effect is that the agent declines to terminate its action because it sees further options that can be performed: ‘Not out of options yet. Iterate and keep trying’.
“The interesting question here is how the swarm was configured, what was its task and how did that task benefit from having the swarm coordinate on an obscure location on the internet. And if the swarm needed a place to communicate, why was breaking into a website chosen instead of any of the more standard communication tools that are available for free, which don’t require gaining illicit access first.”
He compares the DseWiki hijack with the Hugging Face incident. “In the Hugging Face breach, agents were found to be writing to a package manager, using it as a message board. This allowed bypassing of some of the isolation and controls that were intended to be in place,” he explains.
“Similarly, we have agents here again using a system that they found access to as a message board. It’s interesting that the same behavior is present on this breach as in the Hugging Face one. Considering the timing of this, it seems likely the same or similar configuration was present in both hacks, leading to similar security incidents independently of each other.”
However, perhaps the biggest question here is who is responsible for such hijacks. OpenAI describes them as misalignment incidents; that is, not the ‘fault’ of OpenAI, but the failure of the agent and network designers to adequately constrain autonomous agents. This also appears to be the attitude of many users of these agents, who clearly want the benefits of autonomy even though autonomy comes with severe risk. In this instance, the agents were created by OpenAI employees as internal experimental models before ‘breaking free’.
“To defend against self-concealing software, security teams must enforce strict egress filtering on outbound application programming interfaces, restrict non-human identity permissions, and deploy automated continuous monitoring to detect anomalous bot interactions across corporate networks,” says Noelle Murata, COO at Xcape, Inc.
But perhaps we should not completely exclude the culpability of the frontier AI developers. These may be misalignment incidents, but users have been given the freedom to create that misalignment. Maybe the rush to be the first and most powerful AI provider impinges on base safe design. A lesson could be learned from history. Weapons were first developed to assist in hunting for food; but have evolved into general killing contraptions irrespective of the original purpose.
